author: rian-dolphin
body:
I was working in a long session on my Claude subscription and noticed my usage being eaten up far faster than the equivalent work in Claude Code. I realised it was due to lack of prompt caching.

Tau has always *read* cache usage — `cache_read`, `cache_write` and `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` are all parsed off `message_start` and priced — but it never put `cache_control` breakpoints in a request. The reporting half was wired up and the requesting half was not, so those counters sat at zero and every request re-billed the system prompt, the whole tool schema block, and the entire conversation as fresh input. Tool schemas alone are tens of thousands of tokens, resent on every tool call.

After implementing this change I am seeing cache usage in the high 90%s for longer sessions as expected.

## What this adds

Anthropic allows four cache breakpoints per request:

| # | Position | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Last tool schema | Caches the whole tool block |
| 2 | Final system block | Not the OAuth identity block — its prefix is already covered |
| 3 | Previous request's tail | Guarantees the read hit (see below) |
| 4 | Current request's tail | Extends the cache to the new tip |

Breakpoints 3 and 4 are the interesting pair. Anthropic only looks back 20 block positions from a breakpoint, and one turn appends `2N+2` blocks for `N` tool calls — so a turn with ~9+ parallel tool calls pushes the previous cache entry out of the window and misses. Marking where the previous request ended opens a second lookback window there. That position is derived from the payload, not tracked across requests: the transcript is append-only and every request stops just before the assistant message it produces.

## The one-hour cache

One of the efficiencies of the Claude Code subscription is the one-hour prompt cache it includes, rather than the five-minute API default. Five minutes is shorter than a build, a test run, or reading a diff — so it expires mid-session constantly. This asks for the one-hour TTL on subscription OAuth, which is where it's free.

- **Subscription OAuth** → 1h TTL
- **Anthropic API key** → 5m default, so nobody silently pays the 2x cache-write premium
- **Anthropic-protocol gateways** → no breakpoints at all, unless opted back in

That last case is worth noting: `minimax`, `minimax-cn`, `fireworks` and `vercel-ai-gateway` are all `kind = "anthropic"` and route through `anthropic_config_from_provider` despite not being Anthropic, and `vercel-ai-gateway` proxies to non-Anthropic models entirely. They're detected by base-URL host, along with Copilot's Anthropic-protocol models, and receive an identical payload to today's.

Capability and intent are resolved separately, so that detection is a default rather than a hard rule. Intent comes from the auth mode above; capability comes from three `compat` booleans layered detected → provider → per-model, the same path `forceAdaptiveThinking` already takes on this provider:

| Key | Effect when `false` |
| --- | --- |
| `supportsCacheControl` | No breakpoints at all |
| `supportsLongCacheRetention` | Clamps the 1h TTL to 5m |
| `supportsCacheControlOnTools` | Drops only the tool-schema breakpoint |

Capability only ever narrows intent, so the two compose with no precedence rule. Two of those keys were already in the catalog with nothing reading them — `_detected_compat` emitted `supportsLongCacheRetention`, and the Fireworks model entries declare both it and `supportsCacheControlOnTools`, mirrored in from Pi — so this makes existing data live rather than adding a parallel vocabulary. It also means a gateway fronting real Claude, or a caching-capable proxy, can opt in without a source edit.

The session sidebar now shows a cache hit rate, since otherwise there's no way to tell this is working short of watching a rate limit. It's hidden rather than shown as 0% for providers that never report cache usage.

## Verified against the live API

Not just unit tests — driving `_build_messages_payload` on a real subscription credential:

| Turn | Read | Write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold | 0 | 4737 |
| +12 tool calls | 4737 | 1149 |
| +12 more (26 new blocks) | 5886 | 1153 |

The third row is the case breakpoint 3 exists for — 26 new blocks is outside the 20-block lookback, so a single-breakpoint design misses there. Also confirmed `ttl: "1h"` is genuinely honored on OAuth rather than silently downgraded to 5m.

`uv run pytest` (1258), `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` all clean.

## Prior art

Placement is adapted from Pi's [`anthropic-messages.ts`](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts), with two deliberate differences: Tau doesn't mark the OAuth identity block, and spends the freed slot on the second message breakpoint.

["Prompt Caching In Agents"](https://earendil.com/posts/prompt-caching/) by one of Pi's creators is why the OAuth default here is one hour rather than Pi's five minutes — Pi defaults short because it isn't a permitted subscription harness and its users pay per-token API prices, which doesn't apply to a subscription.

## For reviewers

Two things I'd flag, and one known follow-up:

1. **1h write pricing.** `_response_cost` still prices 1h writes at the 5m `cacheWrite` rate and `Usage.cache_write_1h` is unconsumed. Harmless while `long` is OAuth-only, but it understates cost if `long` ever reaches an API-key path.
2. **Unverified:** I confirmed OAuth *honors* the 1h TTL, but not how Anthropic weights cache writes against subscription rate limits. Writes bill 2x for 1h vs 1.25x for 5m, so if limit accounting mirrors cost weights, very short sessions could conceivably consume limit faster. Reads dominate writes heavily in real sessions so I expect a large net win regardless — but I couldn't verify it and didn't want to imply I had. If it does turn out wrong, or if Anthropic stops honoring `ttl: "1h"` at all, `supportsLongCacheRetention = false` in a catalog overlay clamps it back to 5m without a source edit. Worth having, since an unsupported ttl is a hard 400 and Tau doesn't retry 400s.

**Follow-up:** compaction and branch-summary requests still inherit full retention, so they write a cache entry that can never be read back — they use their own system prompt and no tools, so they share no prefix with the conversation. Pi passes `cacheRetention: "none"` for these. Left out here since compaction is infrequent and the plumbing outweighed the saving.

Contributor notes in `dev-notes/prompt-caching.md`; user-facing docs under `website/content/guides/` and `website/content/reference/configuration.md`.

author: moscowchill
body:
## Why

On 2026-07-28 nginx on the explorer host was down for **9 hours** and no alert fired. Every site on the box served Cloudflare 521 the whole time.

`monitor.sh` was running fine every minute throughout. It stayed silent because every check it makes probes an app *directly on loopback*: pm2 processes, gqrl RPC on :8545, beacon on :3500, the frontend on :3000, the backend on :8082, mongo. All of those were genuinely healthy. Only the reverse proxy in front of them was dead, and nginx was not on the list.

Root cause of the outage itself: an `unattended-upgrades` restart ran `nginx -t` during a transient DNS failure on a proxied upstream hostname. The config test failed, nginx refused to start, and nothing ever retried it.

## What this adds

- **nginx service check**: `systemctl is-active nginx`, debounced 2 ticks like the other checks.
- **nginx TLS check**: probes `https://zondscan.com/` pinned to `127.0.0.1` via `--resolve`, so it tests our own vhost and origin cert rather than the Cloudflare edge. Catches "nginx is running but not actually serving".
- **Origin cert expiry**: warns at 30 days. The origin certs are long-lived with no renewal infra, so a silent expiry is a guaranteed future outage nobody is watching for. Opt-in via `MONITOR_SSL_DIR` so no deployment-specific path is baked into this public repo.

## Deployment note

`MONITOR_SSL_DIR` must be exported for the cert check to run; unset, that check is skipped and the rest still works.

## Known limitation

This monitor still runs on the box it watches, so by construction it cannot report a whole-host failure, and it could not have alerted here if the box had gone down entirely rather than just nginx. An independent external watchdog running off-box covers that case and is deployed separately.

## Testing

- `bash -n` clean.
- Deployed and run on the box: exits 0, all new checks evaluate correctly (`nginx is-active` -> active, TLS probe -> 200, 6 origin certs found and all valid).
- Alert and recovery lifecycle verified end to end against the Discord webhook (message delivery confirmed, HTTP 204).

author: thegreencedar
body:
Closes #1575

## What changed

Packet sufficiency decided requirement coverage by the requirement's `FlowRole`. A claim whose *wording* produced that role closed every requirement wearing it, so two requirements in the same flow — a client's request finalization and its transport send, a command loop's event loop and its network input — were closed together by one piece of evidence, and prose alone could close either.

Each `FlowRequirement` now carries an **evidence predicate**: either an allowed set of `PacketEvidenceRole` values, or a structural check over the cited anchor (`EvidencePredicate::CitedRoles` / `CitedCarrier`). A requirement is covered only by a proof-bearing claim that cites evidence matching *that* requirement. `StructuralLanguagePolicy` and the claim-text→`FlowRole` derivation are gone; `FlowRole` remains as a diagnostic label.

Specifically:

- `request_interceptor_management` is back in the sufficiency path, wired through `packet_citation_owns_interceptor_management`. This is what the axios holdout gate turns on.
- `format_errors` / `FlowRole::ErrorOrFallback` are kept, with an evidence carrier of their own rather than being deleted.
- The new `packet_evidence_carriers` module holds the per-requirement structural checks. Every carrier reads only the citation.

Alongside it, sufficiency stops publishing what it cannot prove:

- `covered_claims` and `avoid_opening_paths` come from proven claims only. A claim the same packet lists as ineligible is no longer republished as verified, and the file behind it is no longer advertised as not worth opening.
- An uncited sentence is ineligible ("claim carries no cited evidence").
- The SQL diagnostic-evidence bypass is removed: a synthetic source scan is a text match and no longer promotes a verdict.
- Every task class — not only `ArchitectureExplanation` — holds each resolved exact path to its own proof-bearing claim, with a per-path gap, a bounded gap budget (`MAX_EXACT_PATH_CLAIM_GAPS`), and the path-specific follow-up placed at the front of the follow-up list so the command cap cannot drop it.

One term-detection fix was required: `packet_terms_indicate_shell_install_dispatch_flow` accepted "command"/"function" as a shell signal, so a command-server prompt raised shell requirements that no citation in such a repository could ever close. It now needs an actual shell term.

## Invariants

Three tests that the previous shape could not express:

- `the_requirement_inventory_matches_the_requirement_tables` — a checked-in inventory of every requirement. The old invariant asked whether *any* evidence role could carry a requirement's `FlowRole`, which a failing lane could satisfy by deleting the requirement; this one fails on removal too, so the only way past it is an edit a reviewer reads.
- `every_requirement_has_evidence_that_can_close_it` — each requirement has a witness anchor that closes it, so an unclosable requirement is caught instead of reporting partial forever.
- `requirements_sharing_a_flow_role_stay_separable_by_evidence` — for every pair of requirements sharing a `FlowRole` inside one flow, each one's witness must leave the other missing. This is the property whose absence let one citation close a whole role.

Plus `holdout_prompts_stay_partial_when_the_named_component_is_uncited`, pinned to the three prompts in `benchmarks/tasks/holdout-retrieval/`, with the opposite direction for axios in `holdout_axios_interceptor_evidence_closes_the_interceptor_requirement`.

## Tests changed rather than added

Every test that proved a requirement through claim wording had to be rewritten with cited evidence; the claim text and the prompt are unchanged in each case, only the fixture now carries the anchor the claim rests on. Two changed direction, for stated reasons:

- `sql_synthetic_source_scan_table_and_foreign_key_cover_schema_requirements` → `sql_synthetic_source_scan_evidence_never_covers_schema_requirements`. Same prompt, same three source-scan anchors; the removed bypass is exactly what made them count as proof. The scan is still reported with its concrete role as evidence worth following up.
- `packet_sufficiency_uses_selected_plan_role_probes` → `planned_role_probes_stay_sufficiency_gaps_until_evidence_covers_their_requirement`. Same four HTML/JS anchors; none is evidence for a native constraint, a custom validator, or a submit guard, so all three requirements stay open and every planned probe for them stays a gap. It now also asserts the three requirements are missing and not covered.

`compact_truncated_packet_retains_proof_provenance_counts` keeps the same seven-tier fixture and now derives its expected `covered_claims` count from which anchors are sufficiency-eligible, instead of asserting all seven.

## Both directions

Each behavioural change was reverted in place and the corresponding test observed to fail:

| Mutation | Failing test |
| --- | --- |
| `request_interceptor_management` given its `Dispatch` sibling's predicate | `requirements_sharing_a_flow_role_stay_separable_by_evidence`; the axios holdout goes **Sufficient** with the interceptor uncited |
| `format_errors` deleted from the table | `the_requirement_inventory_matches_the_requirement_tables` |
| `format_errors` given `CitedRoles(&[])` | `every_requirement_has_evidence_that_can_close_it` |
| exact-path check restricted to `ArchitectureExplanation` | `every_task_class_needs_a_proof_bearing_claim_for_each_resolved_exact_path` |
| uncited-claim branch removed | `a_claim_without_cited_evidence_cannot_satisfy_sufficiency` |
| `covered_claims: supported_claims` | `a_claim_the_packet_reports_as_unproven_is_never_published_as_covered` |
| single combined exact-path gap restored | `more_uncovered_exact_paths_than_the_gap_budget_are_summarized_not_dropped`, `retained_route_tracing_packet_reports_the_unproven_route_instead_of_sufficient` |
| old shell-install term set restored | `a_command_server_prompt_is_not_a_shell_install_prompt` |

## Gates

- `cargo test -p codestory-cli --test architecture_contracts` — 14 passed.

Closes #326.

Test-only harness coverage. The production defect was already fixed by #319 / PR #321 (OID 18 normalized to text at the connection boundary), so this adds no production SQL or `internal/` changes — it extends the output-contract integration harness to exercise and regression-lock the internal-`"char"` schema-collector aliases the #314 fixtures missed.

## What changed

- **Char whitelist** (`internalCharColumns`) gains the OUTPUT aliases the remaining schema collectors expose: `partition_strategy`, `tg_enabled`, `volatility` (the alias of `provolatile`, never the raw catalog name). `attidentity` is deliberately kept out of the single-char sweep and asserted via the dedicated `allowEmpty=true` path (the non-set case is `""`).
- **Fixtures** seed a RANGE-partitioned table, a user trigger, a SQL function (identity column already present), so these collectors emit rows. The high-sensitivity definition collectors are enabled so `pg_triggers_definitions_v1` / `pg_functions_definitions_v1` are covered too.
- **Assertions** (OC-R006) that each aliased char decodes as a single-character string, never a JSON number:
  - `pg_partitions_v1.partition_strategy`
  - `pg_triggers_v1` / `pg_triggers_definitions_v1.tg_enabled`
  - `pg_functions_v1` / `pg_functions_definitions_v1.volatility`
- **FDW leg** (OC-R007, capability-gated): a foreign table needs a `postgres_fdw` server the `pg_monitor` collector role cannot create, so it is provisioned via an optional `SIGNALS_TEST_PG_SUPERUSER_DSN` (wired into the CI matrix step). When the capability is absent the fixture + `fdw_foreign_tables_v1.relkind == "f"` assertion are skipped with a documented reason; every other assertion still runs.

Temporarily reverting the #319 OID-18 `AfterConnect` registration turns the new assertions RED — `partition_strategy`=114, `tg_enabled`=79, `volatility`=118/105, `relkind`=102 — and GREEN with it restored. The assertions check for the string type, not just presence.

## Ziel

Im Vote-Bereich sollte der Genre-Filter der Spielauswahl nicht nur die Anzeige einschränken,
sondern auch "Alle markieren"/"Auswahl aufheben" und den tatsächlichen Abstimmungsstart auf die
gerade sichtbaren Spiele begrenzen.

- `server/public/js/views/votes.js`: neue Hilfsfunktion `voteFilterVisibleGames()` als einzige
  Quelle für "welche Spiele sind unter dem aktiven Genre-Filter sichtbar". "Alle markieren" und
  "Auswahl aufheben" ändern jetzt nur noch den Auswahlstatus dieser sichtbaren Spiele statt aller
  Spiele im Katalog. Der Start-Button filtert die tatsächlich zur Wahl gestellten `gameIds`
  ebenfalls auf die sichtbaren Spiele, sodass eine gefilterte, aber anderweitig noch markierte
  Auswahl (z.B. aus einem vorherigen Filterzustand) nicht versehentlich mit in die Abstimmung geht.
- `server/src/test/e2e/flows.e2e.test.ts`: neuer Regressionstest, der zwei Katalogspiele per API
  mit Genres versieht, den Genre-Chip-Filter aktiviert und "Alle markieren"/"Auswahl aufheben"
  sowie den Abstimmungsstart bei aktivem Filter auf genau das sichtbare Spiel prüft; ein zuvor
  manuell abgewähltes, aber durch den Filter verstecktes Spiel bleibt dabei unberührt.

Add a `--json` flag to `fossa sbom analyze` that, on a successful upload, prints project metadata as JSON to stdout — reusing the exact renderer/schema as `fossa analyze --json` so downstream tooling parses both identically.

author: maguerrieri
body:
## Summary

The first **persona pack** — a plugin that ships `personas/` and nothing else, discovered by `gm` purely through the `GM_PERSONA_PATH` handshake #41 introduces. It's both a usable voice and the worked example that tier was missing.

- **`watson`** — the chronicler's voice: retrospective first-person framing, precise about the hour, clinical about people and then kind about them, dry at his own expense. An original characterization (voice / temperament / density / humor / sensibilities), synthesized from two public-domain Conan Doyle stories. No source text reproduced; `NOTICE` records what was read and why.
- **`hooks/persona-path.sh`** — appends the pack's `personas/` to `$GM_PERSONA_PATH` via `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` on `SessionStart`. Three properties that matter: it **appends** (the player's own dirs keep priority over a pack's), it **`%q`-quotes** the path (an install dir with a space stays one entry instead of splitting into two bogus ones), and it **fails open** at every step — a persona pack must never keep a session from starting.
- **CI** — a per-plugin workflow with path filters, matching repo convention. It lints the pack with `gm`'s own `bin/validate-adapter --personas --all`: the same command an out-of-tree pack would run in its own repo.

No `Bash(...)` allowlist entry is needed — the pack ships no CLI.

## Stacked on #42

Based on `claude/gm-personas-external-resolution-bq4x3s`, not `main` — without #41's resolution rule nothing in this pack is reachable. **Merge #42 first**, then retarget this to `main`. The diff here is the pack alone.

Filed as #43 rather than folded into #42, whose body explicitly scoped a shipped pack out.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [x] `validate-adapter --personas --all` on the pack — 1 persona valid
- [x] All JSON well-formed; hook parses (`bash -n`) and is executable; workflow YAML parses

**Hook**, exercised directly — 4/4:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `$GM_PERSONA_PATH` unset | no leading colon (which would be an empty entry) |
| Pre-existing entries | appended after them, not clobbered |
| Install path with a space | exactly one entry |
| No `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | exits 0, writes nothing |

**Resolution**, against the rule as written in `SKILL.md` — 7/7:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `persona: watson`, pack on path | → the pack, no player config |
| `persona: house`, pack on path | → **`gm`'s shipped persona** — a pack must not capture a shipped name |
| Campaign-local `watson` vs. pack | → campaign-local wins |
| Empty dir at an earlier tier | → does **not** shadow; search continues |
| `GM_PERSONA_PATH="::<dir>"` | → empty entries skipped |
| Path-valued `persona:` | → used literally, no search |
| Unresolvable name | → reports all three paths tried |

That fourth row is worth calling out: it only passes because of the "a tier matches only when it holds a readable `persona.md`" fix in #42's `7dcc1ac`. Under the original wording an empty `personas/house/` would have shadowed the shipped voice.

## Provenance

*A Study in Scarlet* (1887, [PG #244](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/244)) and *The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes* (1892, [PG #1661](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1661)) — both long past the 1929 US public-domain cutoff, as is the character as depicted in them. Project Gutenberg's trademark covers its own branding and editions, none of which is reproduced. Read for the retrospective frame and dated evening (*A Scandal in Bohemia*), the chronicler's opening over his notes and the clinical-then-human read of a frightened client (*The Speckled Band*), and Watson's self-introduction and cataloguing habit (*A Study in Scarlet*).

## Note

The pack's README states plainly that the validator is a **smoke test, not enforcement** — front-matter plus a short mechanic-phrase deny-list. It can't tell that prose is voice-only, and a persona is text the GM adopts as instruction. Same caveat #42 added to the contract.

Closes #43

author: nguyenha935
body:
## Summary

A reasoning model emits nothing at all while thinking, so the wait for the response's FIRST byte — not any streaming timeout — decides whether its answer is reachable. At 180s a large-prompt reasoning request routinely lost that race: the gateway reported `http2: timeout awaiting response headers` while the router's own usage log showed the same request completing normally moments later (`promptTokens=77194` → `completionTokens=2789`). The request was healthy; only the deadline was short. Raised to 300s.

## Type
- [x] Bug fix

## Target Branch
`dev`

## Why 300s and not more

The value is multiplied twice downstream, so it has to stay modest:

- `RetryDo` wraps every provider call with `Attempts: 3` (`internal/providers/retry.go`)
- a workflow step then requeues up to `maxTaskDispatches` times (`internal/tools/team_tool_dispatch.go`)

300s is therefore already ~45 min of worst-case wall clock per workflow step. Anything more generous turns one slow provider into an hours-long step.

## Why not remove it entirely

Removing the bound was considered and rejected. Agent run contexts come from `internal/scheduler/queue.go` via `context.WithCancel` (and `lanes.go` via `WithCancel(context.Background())`) — **no deadline is ever attached**, and there is no `RunTimeout`/`MaxRunDuration` anywhere. This transport timeout is the only thing bounding a request that never answers.

Without it, a silently dead connection would hold its scheduler lane until the OS TCP keepalive gave up (~2h), and workflow requeue could not rescue it because requeue only fires when a run *ends*. The file's old doc comment claimed the design could "rely on ctx deadlines and Transport stage timeouts" — the first half was false, and the comment is corrected here.

## Checklist
- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go build -tags sqliteonly ./...` passes
- [x] `go vet ./...` passes
- [x] Tests pass: `go test -race ./internal/providers/... ./internal/agent/...`
- [ ] Web UI builds — N/A, no UI change
- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials
- [x] SQL queries parameterized — N/A, no SQL
- [x] i18n — N/A, no user-facing strings
- [x] Migration version bumped — N/A, no migration

## Test Plan

Three tests lock the sizing so it cannot drift silently:

- `TestResponseHeaderTimeoutAccommodatesReasoningModels` — must exceed the 180s first-byte latency that failed, and must not exceed the 300s ceiling the retry math was sized against.
- `TestResponseHeaderTimeoutIsSet` — must stay non-zero, with the scheduler-lane rationale in the test body.
- `TestDefaultRetryAttemptsMatchTimeoutSizing` — asserts `DefaultRetryConfig().Attempts == 3`, so if the retry multiplier changes the sizing gets re-examined.

Also verified live on a deployed build: a genuinely unreachable upstream now surfaces its error at ~901s (3 × 300s) instead of ~541s (3 × 180s), confirming the new value is the one in effect and the retry multiplier is still 3.

author: m-nweke
body:
Ports the linear regression work from CS5531 Assignment 3 Part 1 into the portfolio, and replaces its evaluation.

## What changed from the original

The original fit a linear model on one `train_test_split(..., random_state=0)` and reported the R² that came back. That turned out not to be a supportable number.

**Running the identical procedure under 20 different seeds gives R² from 0.626 to 0.907** — a spread of 0.28, with nothing changing but the seed. That's larger than the gain from any modelling decision in the notebook. Seed 0, the original's choice, happened to give 0.708.

Replaced with five-fold cross-validation against a predict-the-mean baseline:

| Model | R² (log price) | Median abs. error |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline — predict the mean | −0.00 | 25.4% |
| `OverallQual` only | 0.67 | 13.1% |
| All 36 numeric features | **0.83** | **7.4%** |

## Other findings documented

- **Dollar RMSE is worse than baseline** ($88,821 vs $80,702) while MAE and median error are far better. Back-transforming log predictions punishes a few high-end misses — the worst is a 5,642 sq ft home that sold for $160k and is priced at $3.25M.
- **The original's `|z| < 3` outlier filter lifts R² to 0.90 by discarding 30% of the data.** That answers an easier question, not the same one better.
- **Latent index-alignment bug**: `interpolate().dropna()` built `X` from a filtered frame while `y` came from the unfiltered one. It happens not to fire on this dataset, but a single leading `NaN` would have made it real and silent. Replaced with median imputation inside the pipeline, refit per fold.

## Notes

- Notebook is committed with real executed outputs (Python 3.12, scikit-learn 1.9).
- Dataset is not redistributed — `data/README.md` carries the download, and the CSV is gitignored, matching the pattern in projects 02 and 05.

## Summary

Standardises the agent fleet's tool surface on the **real client-side MCP client**
(`gate/mcp_servers/remote.py`) that the platform's other agents already use. Per
the initiative's Go-first / one-tool-at-a-time rule, this pass:

- Retires one **DUPLICATE** shim — `gate.mcp_servers.initiatives_server` — whose
  entire tool surface (`fire_initiative` + `fire_initiative_inline`) is now
  first-class on the deployed Go `leartech-mcp-servers/agent_api` server,
  already wanted + wired by `WANTED_MCP_SERVERS`.
- Labels each **remaining** in-process shim as `GAP` (no Go MCP yet) or
  `KEEP-LOCAL` (must stay in the agent pod) so future engineers landing on
  those files know which side of the seam they're on without hunting the PR log.

Direction of travel: [`AI-GATEWAY-AND-PORTABILITY.md`](../blob/feat/shims-to-real-mcp/AI-GATEWAY-AND-PORTABILITY.md)
— tools via standard client-side MCP, no in-process SDK MCP where a Go server
can serve them.

## Bucket map

| Shim | Bucket | Rationale / action |
|---|---|---|
| `gate.mcp_servers.pipeline_server` | DUPLICATE (retired earlier) | Now `leartech-mcp-servers/jx3_flow`. See PR #151. |
| `gate.mcp_servers.tekton` | DUPLICATE (retired earlier) | Now `leartech-mcp-servers/tekton`. See f58a530. |
| `gate.mcp_servers.pr_context_server` | DUPLICATE (retired earlier) | Now `leartech-mcp-servers/pr_context`. See PR #146. |
| **`gate.mcp_servers.initiatives_server`** | **DUPLICATE (this PR)** | Now `leartech-mcp-servers/agent_api`. `fire_initiative_inline(body)` maps 1:1 onto `fire_initiative(initiative_body=body)`. By-name firing composes as `get_catalog_entry(name)` → `fire_initiative(initiative_body=yaml_body)` — same round-trips, one server. |
| `gate.mcp_servers.artifacts_server` | GAP | `list_playwright_runs` + `head_artifact` are pure network I/O a Go MCP could serve identically. No `test_artifacts` server in `leartech-mcp-servers` yet. **Do NOT hand-migrate** — build the Go server first; then add `test_artifacts` to `WANTED_MCP_SERVERS` and delete this shim. Docstring in the file spells out the exact retirement steps. |
| `gate.mcp_servers.ai_gateway_web_server` | GAP | `web_search` + `web_fetch` wrap `<gateway>/v1/search` and `/v1/fetch`. The ai-gateway is already a network boundary; this shim just gives the LLM a typed MCP surface. No Go equivalent in `leartech-mcp-servers` yet. Same retirement sketch documented in the file. |

## What actually changed

**Commit 1 — `refactor(mcp): retire initiatives_server shim`:**
- Delete `gate/mcp_servers/initiatives_server.py`.
- Rewrite `gate/mcp_servers/__init__.py` docstring as the canonical bucket map;
  drop the `build_initiatives_server` import + `__all__` export.
- Remove the `leartech-initiatives` entry from `gate/agent/mcp_catalog.yaml`
  (no role wired it) and expand the `leartech-agent-api` description to
  list the initiative surface it now owns (`fire_initiative`,
  `list_catalog_entries`, `get_catalog_entry`, `list_initiative_runs`,
  `get_initiative_run`, `get_run_snapshot`, `get_run_decisions`,
  `cancel_initiative_run`, `send_command_to_run`, `list_roles`).
- Drop the shim-specific tests in `tests/test_mcp_servers.py`; add
  `test_initiatives_shim_is_retired` — a regression guard that fails if the
  module or `build_initiatives_server` come back without an intentional
  design change (prevents a future re-add silently double-serving the same
  tools from in-process + remote).

**Commit 2 — `docs(mcp): mark each remaining in-process shim GAP or KEEP-LOCAL`:**
- Docstring-only. Puts the bucket label + retirement steps IN THE SHIM ITSELF
  for `artifacts_server`, `ai_gateway_web_server`, and `criteria_server` so
  the boundary is legible without cross-reading the package docstring.

**No changes** to `agent_local.py` (already had a clear "why this stays local"
docstring), `remote.py`, `stdio_bridge.py`, or any consumer of these servers
(`initiative.py`, `main.py`, `ba_agent.py`, `infra_agent.py`, `mcp_catalog.py`).

## Parity verification (DUPLICATE cutover)

The shim's two tools mapped as follows:

| Shim tool | Deployed Go equivalent | Round-trip |
|---|---|---|
| `fire_initiative(name)` | `get_catalog_entry(name).yaml_body` → `fire_initiative(initiative_body=…)` | Same `POST /initiatives` endpoint; two client calls instead of one. |

Both shim tools called the exact same `POST /initiatives` endpoint the Go server
now wraps — the shim's own tests (`test_mcp_fire_initiative_inline_tool` +
`test_mcp_fire_initiative_tool_posts_name`) pinned the wire shape against

path from `/mcps` — so the remote consumption path is regression-tested.

## E2E coverage added

none — pure refactor. This PR removes an in-process shim and updates docstrings /
tests / catalog metadata; no HTTP endpoint, CLI command, screen, or user-facing
flow is added or changed. `scripts/e2e.sh` and `scripts/e2e-ui.sh` are the
consumer-repo e2e harnesses, not the agent's own — and this repo doesn't ship
either. The shim's own wire-shape tests were retired alongside it; a new
regression guard (`test_initiatives_shim_is_retired`) locks the retirement
so a future re-add lights up in unit tests, not on the wire.

- [x] `uv run mypy app gate` — no issues, 129 source files.

author: vinnie357
body:
`/claude-code:claude-commands` could not be loaded at all. It documents Claude Code's shell-injection syntax, Claude Code executes that pattern when loading a skill, and the example command (`cat path/to/file`) exits non-zero — so the skill that teaches command authoring was broken by the feature it teaches. Published in the marketplace, so every installer got it.

The defect is broader than one failing command. Loading also expands every substitution placeholder the docs describe, so the section teaching them rendered as its own live values.

- Prefix every literal `!` shell-injection trigger with a visible `KEY=`, the form the skill already used one line above the site that broke it, and tell the reader to drop it
- Escape `$ARGUMENTS` placeholders with the documented leading backslash, which the renderer consumes so the reader still sees the correct token
- Write the four `CLAUDE_*` variables **bare** rather than as brace expansions — see below
- Fix two previously-unreported `$ARGUMENTS` sites in `references/examples.md`, found by sweeping rather than working from the known list
- Explain both markers at each site, so a future editor does not "clean them up" and reintroduce the bug
- Restate the recognition rule in terms of the **scanned** text rather than the markdown source
- Version bumps: claude-code 0.2.28 → 0.2.29, all-skills 0.4.75 → 0.4.76

**Verified by loading, not by reading** — the only method that means anything for this bug. Both skills were installed into the plugin cache, the plugins reloaded, and the arriving content read. The cache was then restored from backup and confirmed byte-identical.

That verification caught a real defect midway. The backslash escape was applied to both placeholder forms, since the docs say a backslash before the token escapes a literal `$`. Loading proved that rule holds **only for the bare `$NAME` form**: `\$ARGUMENTS` rendered correctly as `$ARGUMENTS`, but `\${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` kept the backslash *and* still expanded, printing the live session ID. The "fixed" page was still leaking the session ID, effort level, and two absolute paths — now with a stray backslash making them look escaped. Hence the bare-name treatment, with the reason recorded at each site.

Fencing does not protect either — a bang at line start inside a fence executes, including nested inside a five-backtick outer fence.

Confirmed in the final load: the shell-injection examples render as syntax, the fenced example shows `node --version` as text rather than a version number, and the `CLAUDE_*` rows show names rather than paths.

Closes claude-skills-169.

author: sunchao
body:
### Why are the changes needed?

SPARK-58412 tracks two lifecycle gaps in the cache-materialization bookkeeping introduced by SPARK-57547. That earlier change replaced raw cache-task completion counters with partition-keyed statistics so duplicate computations cannot make an `InMemoryRelation` appear materialized too early.

First, `CachedRDDBuilder` currently publishes a task's partition statistics whenever the task completes successfully, even if a downstream consumer stops before exhausting the cache-building iterator. This can happen when a memory-only block cannot be stored and Spark returns the partially unrolled iterator to its consumer. Because the statistics accumulator is last-write-wins per partition, a partially consumed recomputation can replace that partition's complete row and byte counts while the cache still appears fully materialized. For example, a completed `(10 rows, N bytes)` entry can be replaced with `(0 rows, 0 bytes)` without removing the partition key, allowing AQE to treat a non-empty cache as empty.

Second, `clearCache` resets the existing accumulator in place. Tasks from the retired cache generation have already captured that same accumulator, so late completions can write stale partition keys and values into the rebuilt generation. If those stale keys cover every partition, the new cache can appear complete before its own partitions finish.

These are general `InMemoryRelation` correctness issues. They were identified while working on runtime-filter support in #57443, but they affect cache materialization independently of that optimizer feature.

### What changes were proposed in this PR?

This change makes cache statistics represent only complete work from the current cache generation.

A task now publishes its partition statistics only after the wrapped cache iterator has been exhausted and the task finishes without failure or interruption. A successful consumer that stops early therefore cannot overwrite a complete partition's statistics with partial values.

Clearing a cache now installs a newly registered `PartitionKeyedAccumulator` instead of resetting the previous accumulator. Each cache-building RDD captures the accumulator for its own generation, so tasks finishing after `clearCache` can update only the retired generation. The cache contents and storage semantics are unchanged; this change only tightens the lifecycle of materialization metadata.

### How was this PR tested?

The existing `CachedTableSuite` clear-cache regression now injects late updates through the retired generation's accumulator before and after rebuilding the cache. It verifies that the new generation remains unloaded until its own partitions complete and that its row and byte statistics remain exact.

A new `ConcurrentInMemoryRelationSuite` regression forces a cached partition to be recomputed, then runs a successful consumer that does not consume the returned cache iterator. It verifies that the partial attempt cannot replace the complete partition statistics.

The following validation passed:

```
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly org.apache.spark.sql.CachedTableSuite org.apache.spark.sql.execution.columnar.ConcurrentInMemoryRelationSuite'
build/sbt sql/scalastyle sql/test:scalastyle
git diff --check
```

The two affected suites ran 108 tests successfully.

author: ryan-dpc
body:
## Le probleme

Le statut premium etait decide par le client puis relu depuis `data.json`, un fichier texte modifiable au Bloc-notes. **Trois contournements existaient, aucun ne demandant de competence particuliere :**

1. Saisir 64 caracteres dont 5 chiffres dans le champ premium suffisait a ce que le client ecrive `isPremium: true` chez lui
2. Editer `data.json` a la main produisait le meme resultat
3. Envoyer `TOGGLE_PLUGIN` sur le WebSocket local activait un service premium **sans le moindre controle**

Le troisieme etait le plus simple : aucun fichier a modifier, un seul message suffisait.

## La correction

Le verdict vient desormais de Supabase et n'est jamais ecrit sur disque.

**Serveur**
- `entitlement.rs` : la session Supabase transmise par l'application est gardee en memoire, le statut verifie aupres de Supabase, mis en cache 5 minutes. **En cas de doute — pas de session, reseau coupe, reponse inattendue — l'acces est refuse.**
- `start_guard` applique le verdict en continu aux services Spotify, Discord, Hue et Twitch, en respectant les preferences utilisateur. Ils demarrent desactives et ne s'allument qu'une fois les droits confirmes. La boucle se reveille immediatement a chaque connexion ou deconnexion.
- `ws.rs` et `streamdock.rs` passent par `entitlement`, `TOGGLE_PLUGIN` est controle a son tour
- `main.rs` ne lit plus `app_data.is_premium`

**Client**
- `SettingsTab` n'attribue plus le premium
- `AuthContext` abandonne l'heuristique sur la longueur du jeton, qui ne prouvait rien
- `LCUContext` n'ecrit plus `isPremium` et transmet la session au serveur local

## Limite assumee

Le serveur tourne sur la machine de l'utilisateur : un binaire modifie reste possible. Cette PR ferme les contournements triviaux et rattache la decision a une valeur que seul Supabase produit. **L'application des droits par un serveur distant reste le vrai objectif.**

## Prerequis cote base

**La RLS doit interdire a un utilisateur de modifier son propre `is_premium`.** Si la politique autorise l'UPDATE sur sa propre ligne, tout ceci ne sert a rien — je n'ai pas acces a tes policies pour le verifier.

author: atgutier
body:
## Motivation

Both scalar selectors deliver the whole 64-bit base when they appear in a 64-bit source position, but A0 reads it only through the low selector, and its vector ALU takes the value from an ordinary SGPR pair instead. B0 input may use either spelling in either position, so both need a rewrite.

## Technical Details

Scalar positions change the selector in place. Vector positions gain one s_mov_b64 that stages the base into a dead SGPR pair, shared across every affected position in the instruction.

The rewrite is selected by operand rather than by mnemonic, which neither the semantic rule table nor Action can express, so it runs after the opcode-keyed lookup misses. Encodings are identified by their leading bits: encoding IDs embed high opcode bits and are not contiguous per format, so they cannot be range-tested. An unrecognized encoding carrying such an operand fails closed rather than being copied.

author: billzhuang
body:
## Summary

The `catwalk` Linear project's backlog is fully empty (every issue is Done/Canceled) and there were 0 open PRs, so per the linear-ship skill's fallback (0a) this is a small, behavior-preserving maintenance refactor rather than an issue-driven change. This repo already has ~30 recent merged maintenance PRs covering most of the obvious env-var-guard and dedup targets (see the survey below), so I specifically searched for something not already covered.

`flue-agent/src/webfetch.ts` had two functions independently swallowing a "cancel on an already-closed source" error with the identical 3-line try/catch idiom:
- `readBounded`'s `finally` block: `try { await reader.cancel(); } catch { /* already closed */ }`
- `cancelBody`: `try { await r.body?.cancel(); } catch { /* already closed */ }`

`cancelBody`'s own doc comment already noted it "swallows a cancel-on-already-closed error the same way readBounded's own reader.cancel() does" — i.e. the duplication was already documented as intentional-and-identical, just never factored out.

## Changes

- Added `cancelQuietly(cancel: () => Promise<unknown> | undefined)` in `webfetch.ts`, taking a thunk so it fits both `reader.cancel()` and `r.body?.cancel()` call shapes.
- `readBounded`'s `finally` block now calls `await cancelQuietly(() => reader.cancel())`.
- `cancelBody` now just returns `cancelQuietly(() => r.body?.cancel())`.
- No behavior or public-contract change — pure internal dedup. Trimmed the now-redundant sentence from `cancelBody`'s doc comment since the shared behavior is now expressed by the shared helper itself.

## Validation

- Both cancel-swallowing paths are already pinned by existing tests in `test/webfetch.test.ts` (`fetchUrl ignores a reader.cancel() failure once MAX_BYTES is exceeded`, `fetchUrl ignores a redirect hop's body.cancel() failure...`) — these pass unchanged before and after, proving the refactor preserves behavior.
- `node --test --experimental-strip-types test/webfetch.test.ts` — 57/57 passing.
- `npm test` (full flue-agent suite) — 340/340 passing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean.

**Not auto-verified:** the Python `pipecat-app` test suite wasn't run, since this change touches only the Node/TS `flue-agent` side and has no cross-language surface.

Not tied to a Linear issue (empty backlog fallback per the linear-ship routine) — no `Closes` line.

body:
### Motivation

- Move runtime persistence from embedded SQL.js files to PostgreSQL for production durability and to enable durable job scheduling and quota accounting.
- Make autonomous discovery quota‑paced and durable (producer creates jobs, workers execute YouTube calls) to avoid producer-side API calls and to enable restart-safe scheduling.
- Harden country exclusion and ingestion gates so excluded countries never consume external quota or reach downstream processing.
- Improve multilingual country inference and evidence-based classification, and add tooling to generate/migrate data and run smoke checks.

### Description

- Replace SQL.js persistence with a PostgreSQL-backed `server/db.ts` adapter, add migration framework under `server/db/migrations/*.sql`, and require `DATABASE_URL`; add `runMigrations` and `migrateSqljsToPostgres` scripts in `package.json` and new migration script `scripts/migrateSqljsToPostgres.ts`.
- Introduce durable job queue and scheduler: new `jobs`, `job_attempts`, `query_runs`, `quota_reservations`, and scheduler tables, plus corresponding DB helpers (`enqueueJob`, `claimNextJob`, `completeJob`, `failJob`, `recoverStaleJobs`, scheduler lock APIs, and job/runner lifecycle functions) and worker pool logic in `queueManager.ts`.
- Implement quota reservation and pacing for autonomous/manual/enrichment discovery via `quota_reservations`, `tryReserveQuota`, and related functions, plus `discoverySchedulerPolicy.ts` to calculate capacity and a quota‑paced producer in `autonomousDiscovery.ts` that schedules durable search jobs instead of executing YouTube calls directly.
- Add country exclusion and inference subsystems: `server/countryExclusion.ts`, `server/countryExclusionRules.ts`, `server/countryInference.ts`, and `server/countryValidator.ts` to centralize hard exclusion gating and structured evidence for detected countries.
- Add multilingual classification and knowledge packs (evidence engine enhancements): `evidenceEngine` updates including `MultilingualContextProvider`, `multilingualTerminology`, knowledge pack adjustments, and scoring changes to reduce false positives from adjacent finance/hype.
- Update ingestion pipeline and queue workers so workers perform YouTube API calls and enrichment runs while producers schedule durable jobs, and ensure excluded countries are handled without creating/altering persisted channel records.
- Add many tests and utilities: new unit tests under `server/*.test.ts` for country inference, query planner, discovery scheduler policy, enrichment lifecycle, and evidence engine; add `scripts/queueSmokeTest.ts`, `scripts/runMigrations.ts`, `server/db.legacy.ts` compatibility snapshot, `db/migrations` SQL files, and `nixpacks.toml`, `.nvmrc`/`.node-version`, `railway.json`, and environment variable documentation in `.env.example`.
- Update `package.json` to require Node 22, add `pg` and dev `@types/pg`, and add scripts: `migrate`, `migrate:sqljs`, `queue:smoke`, and `test` harness.
- UI updates to reflect new statuses (ENRICHMENT/NEEDS_REVIEW), scheduler interval display, and queue/concurrency controls.

### Testing

- Type checking was run via `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) and succeeded without type errors.
- Unit tests were executed via `npm test` (node `node:test` suites under `server/*.test.ts`) and the deterministic unit suites passed.
- Production build was executed via `npm run build` and completed successfully; migration and end-to-end PostgreSQL/Railway staging validation were not executed in this workspace because `DATABASE_URL` and provider credentials were not configured, so `scripts/migrateSqljsToPostgres.ts`, `npm run migrate`, and `npm run queue:smoke` remain required staging gates.

## Contenu
- **Lecture** : `Balance(owner_type, owner_id, direction)` (absent → 0/false) ; `BillingCustomer(customer_id)` ; `LedgerEntryExists(message_id, entry_type)` = **garde d'idempotence cross-partition autoritative** (l'index unique `billing_ledger_idem_idx` n'est qu'un backstop même-jour).
- **`RecordDurable`** : append grand livre (**append-only**) + upsert solde à `balance_after`, dans **UNE transaction** → ledger et solde jamais divergents.
- **Modèle de grand livre cohérent** (fixé suite à la revue) : `SUM(credits) == solde` (audit §6.14) — réserve **débite** (credits<0), capture **confirme** (credits=0, le solde a déjà bougé au reserve), libère **rembourse** (credits>0). Plan §13 : solde insuffisant vérifié **au reserve** → 402, **aucune entrée**.
- SQL **paramétré**, **schéma-qualifié** `control_plane.*` (sqlc). Idempotence **NON auto-portée** : l'autorité cross-jour est la réservation Redis atomique (step-142) ; un doublon même-jour remonte `errs.ErrConflict` (à traiter en succès idempotent). `UpsertBalance` est absolu → écritures durables **dans l'ordre** (garanti par le mirroring séquentiel de step-142).

## Tests
Intégration testcontainers Postgres : read solde/config (nullable inclus), `topup→reserve→capture`, garde pré-capture, append-only (3 lignes) + **invariant d'audit `SUM(credits)==solde`**.

author: robcox2910
body:
## Summary

Addresses the code-review findings for pebble-lang: two HIGH runtime bugs, README/doc accuracy, and the chained-comparison caveat.

## Fixes

### Short-circuit `and` / `or` (HIGH)
Previously both operands were compiled and evaluated eagerly (`OpCode.AND` / `OpCode.OR`), so guard idioms like `b != 0 and 10 / b > 1` still divided by zero. `and` / `or` now lower to new `JUMP_IF_FALSE_OR_POP` / `JUMP_IF_TRUE_OR_POP` instructions that skip the right operand once the result is decided, while preserving the operand-value semantics. Tests assert the right-operand **side effect** is skipped, not just the value.

### `finally` runs on every exit path (HIGH)
`finally` previously did not run on `return` inside `try`, nor when the catch block threw/re-threw. `_compile_try` now emits the finally body on the normal, catch-normal, and catch-exception paths, and `return` / `break` / `continue` inline pending finally blocks (via `_emit_finally_unwind`) on their way out. Added regression tests for return-in-try, return-in-catch, re-throw-in-catch, and break/continue.

### Docs
- **README**: pipeline updated to `Lexer -> Parser -> Analyzer -> Module Resolver -> Type Checker -> Compiler -> Optimizer -> VM`; Language Features list expanded (floats, lists, dicts, structs, classes, enums, match, try/catch/finally, closures, generators, async/await, imports, string interpolation).
- **error-handling.md**: finally wording made precise now that it runs on all exit paths.
- **operators.md**: chained-comparison middle-operand double-evaluation note refined (interaction with short-circuit + "great exercise to try yourself").

### Chained comparisons
The middle operand of `a < b < c` is still evaluated twice when in range (parser reuses the AST node; fixing needs a temp/DUP mechanism). Documented honestly and the misleading `test_chain_short_circuit` docstring corrected, with new tests pinning both the short-circuit (skip second read) and the in-range double-read behaviour.

## Verification
`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pyright src tests`, and `pytest` all green — 2254 passed, 93.97% coverage.

body:
## Estado atual (aprovado para merge)

> Este PR **não está mais empilhado**. Ele foi retargetado para `main` depois que os PRs #9 e #14
> foram mesclados, e a main foi integrada nesta branch. A base é `main`, não a branch do #9.

- **Base integrada:** `4ca855f3d1a441870cfaee1b90ab80ddcc8dd165`
- **Head aprovado:** `e9c21bc78a76e9da3e768c91958c04fd7e46528f`
- **Integração:** merge commit normal (`git merge --no-ff`), sem rebase, squash ou force-push.
  Os três commits originais do PR seguem intactos e com os mesmos SHAs.
- **Conflitos de Git:** **nenhum** — o merge automático foi limpo, porque a base anterior deste PR
  era a branch do #9 e todo o conteúdo dele já estava nesta linha de história.
- **Único ajuste mecânico:** o teste estrutural desta fase fixava **18** migrations e passou a
  refletir as **28** atuais, mantendo (e reforçando) a verificação de que a F2.2.7 **não adiciona
  migration própria**. Nenhuma verificação foi removida ou enfraquecida.
- **Diff final:** **16 arquivos**, todos exclusivos do dashboard.
- **Migrations no repositório:** **28** — todas vindas da main; esta entrega não contribui com
  nenhuma.
- **Testes:** **306 testes em 39 arquivos**.
- **CI run `30501569187`:** success.
- **Semgrep run `30501569197`:** success.
- **Vercel Preview:** failure — **NOTE externa de configuração** do ambiente Preview do projeto
  `crm-clinicas-staging`, sem alteração de código. A main tem Vercel success em produção; o mesmo
  failure aparece nos previews dos demais PRs, inclusive em PR exclusivamente de backend.

### Classificação da revisão

- **BLOCKER:** nenhum
- **HIGH:** nenhum
- **MEDIUM:** nenhum
- **LOW:** o aviso textual de histórico parcial afirma que os indicadores consideram o conjunto
  carregado, embora a interface, corretamente, mostre `—` e omita esses resultados. Divergência
  apenas de texto — fica no backlog.
- **NOTE:** a estratégia atual pode carregar até 12 páginas por status para calcular totais. Uma
  futura agregação no domínio pode otimizar clínicas muito grandes.

## Descrição

Transforma a rota canônica `/app` ("Visão geral") em uma dashboard funcional para o gestor da
clínica, usando exclusivamente dados reais já expostos pelos casos de uso públicos do módulo CRM.
**Não altera backend.**

- Fase: F2.2.7 — UX da área comercial
- ADRs relacionados: ADR-003 (fronteiras de módulo), ADR-004 (autorização por permissão),
  ADR-006 (E.164/UTC/pt-BR), ADR-011 (design system e acessibilidade)
- Issues relacionadas: —

### O que entra

| Área | Conteúdo |
| --- | --- |
| Cabeçalho | Clínica ativa, contexto do pipeline padrão, período, "Atualizado em" e ação "Atualizar dados" |
| Filtro de período | Links reais `/app?period=7d\|30d\|90d`, validado no servidor, padrão `30d`, `aria-current` no selecionado |
| Indicadores | Abertas, valor em aberto, ganhas, perdidas, conversão, ticket médio, leads sem movimentação, encerradas no período |
| Funil | Etapas na ordem real do servidor, com nome, quantidade, valor, percentual e barra decorativa |
| Precisam de atenção | Abertas sem responsável ou paradas há 7+ dias, ordenadas conforme especificado, mais etapas com concentração alta |
| Desempenho | Tabelas por responsável e por origem, com nomes reais |
| Recentes | 8 oportunidades mais atualizadas, reaproveitando a tabela densa de "Todos os leads" |

### Interfaces públicas do CRM utilizadas

- `listOpportunityBoard` — única fonte de dados da página (cards, etapas, pipeline padrão e escopo).
- `resolveActiveClinicContext` (`@/modules/tenancy`) — clínica ativa e timezone.

`listContactOwners` e `listLeadSources` não foram necessários: o próprio `listOpportunityBoard` já
devolve `assigneeName` e `sourceName` resolvidos, evitando uma segunda fonte de verdade para os
mesmos rótulos.

## Tipo de mudança

- [ ] Documentação / governança
- [ ] Fundação / infraestrutura
- [x] Funcionalidade
- [ ] Correção
- [ ] Refatoração

## Dados reais, nunca parciais apresentados como globais

`listOpportunityBoard` é paginado (`pageSize` máx. 100). Uma página só nunca é apresentada como
total global. O carregador varre cada status até o fim, dentro de um teto de segurança
(12 páginas × 100 = 1.200 por status, em rodadas paralelas de 4 páginas), e usa `hasMore` para
saber se o conjunto ficou completo:

- conjunto de **abertas** incompleto → aviso visível de escopo parcial acima dos indicadores;
- histórico de **encerradas** incompleto ou indisponível → ganhas, perdidas, conversão, ticket
  médio e encerradas no período mostram `—`, e as colunas de resultado do período somem das
  tabelas de desempenho (só resta "Em aberto");
- nenhuma métrica é estimada, arredondada para cima ou preenchida com valor de demonstração.

Nenhuma alteração de backend foi feita para contornar a paginação.

### Métricas omitidas e por quê

| Métrica | Situação |
| --- | --- |
| Conversão, ticket médio, ganhas/perdidas no período | Exibidas apenas com o histórico de encerradas completo; caso contrário `—` com aviso |
| Tendência histórica / séries temporais | Omitida: não há contrato que devolva encerramentos agregados por data sem varrer todo o histórico |
| Tempo médio por etapa | Omitida: `opportunity_stage_events` não é exposto por interface pública de listagem em lote |
| Seletor de pipelines | Omitido de propósito. A main já expõe `listPipelines`, `listOpportunitiesByPipeline` e `listAllOpportunities`, mas nenhuma é consumida aqui: a dashboard continua operando sobre a pipeline padrão e nada é simulado |

## Checklist arquitetural e de segurança

### Decisões e fronteiras
- [x] Nenhuma decisão arquitetural foi alterada silenciosamente; mudanças de decisão têm **novo ADR**.
- [x] Módulos usam apenas a **interface pública** de outros módulos (sem importar internals) — só `@/modules/crm` e `@/modules/tenancy`.
- [x] Banco e fila acessados via `shared/db` / `shared/queue` (sem SDK direto no domínio) — a rota não fala com o banco.
- [x] N/A — esta entrega é somente leitura, não cria nem deduplica contato/oportunidade.

### Multi-tenant e banco
- [x] N/A — nenhuma tabela, política, índice ou função foi criada ou alterada.
- [x] Nenhuma confiança em `clinic_id` de frontend/payload: o `clinic_id` vem de `resolveActiveClinicContext` no servidor.
- [x] Nenhum uso de `service role`.

### Autorização e entrada
- [x] Operações têm **guard** no servidor: o escopo (`all` / `own`) é resolvido dentro de `listOpportunityBoard`.
- [x] Autorização por permissão, não por comparação de cargo — não existe `role === "..."` no diff (coberto por teste).
- [x] Entrada pública validada: o parâmetro `period` é validado no servidor e qualquer valor inválido volta para `30d`.
- [x] `PermissionGate` usado apenas como UX — sem permissão, a página mostra `AccessDeniedState`, mas quem restringe os dados é o caso de uso.

### Observabilidade e dados pessoais
- [x] Nenhum dado pessoal/segredo enviado a logs; a página não registra nada.

author: theodorespeaks
body:
## Summary
- A custom block's child run is now its own execution: own `executionId`, own logging session against the **source (publisher's) workspace**, own ledger rows. The publisher sees a full run with the trace waterfall in their own Logs; the consumer's view stays as opaque as before.
- Billing follows the invocation boundary. The consumer no longer absorbs the child's model spend — they pay only their own base execution fee, and the child adds no second fee.
- Fixes a privacy leak: SSE callbacks were forwarded into the source run, streaming the publisher's block names, inputs, outputs, workflow name, and raw agent tokens to the consumer's browser. Invisible in the UI because the terminal drops them for `custom_block_*`, so it went unnoticed.
- Fixes failed custom blocks billing $0 — `buildCostCarrierSpans` wrote to `blockLog.childTraceSpans`, but its only reader is gated on `isWorkflowBlockType`, which excludes custom blocks. Dissolves now that the child bills itself; both roll-ups deleted.
- Fixes the depth-limit throw leaking the source workflow's UUID into the consumer's output (`childWorkflowName` still holds the workflow id before it's resolved).
- Errors: adds `BoundarySafeError` so consumer visibility is a property decided at the throw site (fail-closed) instead of depending on whether a throw sits before or after the `try`. Consumers now get a machine-readable `errorType` plus an opaque `errorRef` (the child's execution id) they can quote in support.
- Deletes the regex round-trip (`parseNestedWorkflowError` / `buildNestedWorkflowErrorMessage`) in favour of a structured `workflowChain`. That also fixes `Workflow chain: Child → Child | err`, which happened whenever a child *returned* `success: false` rather than throwing.
- Fixes 429/503 surfacing to API callers as 500 — `readStatusCode` now walks `.cause` and reads `HttpError`/`status`/`statusCode`, with a narrow 503-only 5xx whitelist so an upstream 502/504 never becomes ours. `buildBlockExecutionError` now preserves `cause`. Deletes dead `buildHTTPError`.
- Unifies four copies of the "did this run fail?" span walk into `hasUnhandledError` / `traceSpansIndicateFailure`.

## Behaviour changes worth flagging
- Runs where a `mothership` block recovered from a failed child span were previously logged `failed` by `logger.ts` / `logging-session.ts`, which recursed past the error boundary that `trace-spans.ts` honours. They now log as succeeded. **Existing rows are not backfilled**, so expect a step-change in dashboard failure rates.
- Rate-limited / hosted-key-exhausted runs now return 429/503 instead of 500. Anything retrying on `status === 500` should be checked.
- A custom block inside an N-iteration loop writes N log rows into the publisher's workspace.

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature (also fixes several bugs found along the way)

## Testing
Tested manually end-to-end across two workspaces in the same org: child run lands in the publisher's workspace with the full trace, consumer's row shows only its own `0.005` base fee and no model cost, and the child resolves credentials against the source workspace (verified via BYOK — a publisher key correctly zeroes the charge, and removing it bills the source workspace).

Full suite green: `type-check` 0 errors, `lint:check`, and all 11 CI audits (`check:boundaries`, `check:api-validation:strict`, `check:utils`, `check:zustand-v5`, `check:react-query`, `check:client-boundary`, `check:bare-icons`, `check:icon-paths`, `check:realtime-prune`, `skills:check`, `agent-stream-docs:check`). 15107/15108 tests pass — the one failure is a pre-existing local-env issue (`cloud-review-tools` shells out to a `rg` binary that isn't installed).

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed my changes
- [x] Tests added/updated and passing
- [x] No new warnings introduced
- [x] I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms outlined in the [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](./CONTRIBUTING.md#contributor-license-agreement-cla)

author: chrismaghuhn
body:
Implementation plan for the narrow live-path degradation wiring slice (#125). **Plan document only — no production code.**

**Base:** `main @ 3fad797` (includes PR #146, the §8.0 amendment)
**Authoritative contract:** `docs/projects/champions/decisions/2026-07-28-live-path-degradation-recording.md`

The plan implements that record and adds no rulings of its own.

## Status

**Awaiting plan review. Implementation only after an explicit GO.**

## The 12 tasks

| # | Task | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Schema constants and the closed field set | `SCHEMA_VERSION`, the four `*_FIELDS` tuples, the closed vocabularies, the C7 no-`hero_`/`villain_` test |
| 2 | Validators and mutation tests | `validate_decision_row` / `validate_event_row` / `validate_battle_row` / `validate_completion_row`, plus 95 parametrised mutations (75 per-grain + a 5-rule × 4-grain generic grid) and four positive cases. The decision validator pins the stage vocabulary, bidirectional stage/outcome agreement, which stages require a `fallback_reason`, and `is_degraded` recomputed by calling `is_degraded_decision` itself |
| 3 | `SHOWDOWN_LIVE_DEGRADATION_DIR` classification and the gitignore entry | `NON_BEHAVIORAL` entry, `logs/live-degradation/` ignored, both asserted |
| 4 | Run directory, environment override and writer preflight | exclusive create, probe, four override tests |
| 5 | Decision rows — the §5.1 gate and `is_degraded` | the gate, persisted `is_degraded`, the stage-vocabulary invariant test |
| 6 | Event rows and attribution | §7 rules, `inferred` only at one active battle |
| 7 | Battle aggregation from the named sources | the §8 counter table, C8 |
| 8 | Flush, write-failure accounting, completion, exit status | ordering fix, `flush_run_events`, all three counters persisted, four separate exit tests |
| 9 | Runner wiring — send first, then record | decisions, crash re-raise, events, C11 |
| 10 | Battle boundaries, `finally`, preflight call sites | flush before `_room_raw.pop`, all three exit paths |
| 11 | The process exit status | `cli._run_live`, with no `try`/`except` at all |
| 12 | Smoke behaviour, the artifact invariant, the real smoke run, closeout | both invariant shapes, the generated-name smoke command, the gates |

Test counts: `test_live_degradation.py` reaches **159** (108 → 120 → 132 → 139 → 144 → 159), `test_live_degradation_runner.py` reaches **29**.

## What the §8.0 amendment changed here

- `COMPLETION_FIELDS` carries `schema_errors_total` and `recorder_errors_total`.
- The recorder's counters are named to match the persisted fields one-to-one.
- `write_completion()` persists all three, validates its own payload first, and documents **three** limits rather than two: the payload is a snapshot that cannot contain this write's own failure; `open(..., "x")` is exclusive but **not atomic**; and a rejection of the completion payload *itself* is **structurally unpersistable** — the counter recording it can only reach a reader through the file the rejection prevents. The only realistic cause (duplicate `unterminated_rooms`) is removed by construction with `dict.fromkeys`; if the validator fires anyway, `logger.error` + a non-zero exit + the **absence** of `completion.json` are the signal, a state §8.0 already equates with non-zero counters.
- Four separate exit tests — clean run, prior schema error, prior recorder error, unwritable completion — each asserting the *persisted* counter **and** the exit status, plus a fifth for a present-but-unusable file.
- The artifact invariant has its own step with **both** run shapes: one producing every grain, and one with no events at all, asserting `events.jsonl` is absent while the counters are zero. That second shape is the commonest case and would have failed an all-four-files invariant.

## Placeholders — the claim, stated accurately

Earlier revisions of this PR claimed "no placeholders" while the document contained sixteen. That claim was false, it was made twice, and it stays withdrawn.

**Current state, measured rather than asserted:** four occurrences of `...` remain in the document, and all four are Python syntax — `tuple[str, ...]` once and `open(..., "x")` three times. The last genuine placeholder, `<throwaway-unregistered-name>` in the real-smoke command, is gone: the name is now generated, printed and used inside the one command.

## Verified on the current head

- 34 python blocks parse. The only two that do not compile standalone are in-loop fragments of an `async def`, and they are named as such.
- No called-but-undefined names; every attribute reached through `rec.`/`self.` is declared in `__init__`.
- `git diff --check` clean.
- The PR diff against the GitHub base contains only the plan document.
- The seven known local artifacts are untouched.

## Defects this plan found in the code it will wire into

Recorded because they shaped the plan, not as scope:

- `parse_message` fills `payload` only for `prefix == "request"`, so recording `parsed.payload` for `|error|` would have written `""` into every `server_error` row — the exact evidence §7 requires. Corrected to `"|".join(parsed.args)`.
- Repo-root `logs/` is not gitignored: `.gitignore:12` covers `showdown_bot/logs/` only. An always-on recorder would have polluted `git status`. Task 3 adds the entry and asserts it.
- `run_smoke_battle` never assigns `_active_format`, unlike the other two runners. `book_absent` is still `True` for smoke, so §5's consequence holds — but for an additional reason. Recorded as an observation; changing it is a behaviour change and out of scope.

## Non-claims

No strength claim, no production-readiness claim, no latency claim, and no change to any chosen action — Task 9 asserts the sent string is byte-identical with and without the recorder.

author: bryancruzcb
body:
Closes the hole flagged in #84. A page renders in its default state and axe has no notion of
hovering, so **no hover style in this app had ever been measured by anything.**

That was not hypothetical. `.button-primary:hover` put `--ink` on the light blue at **2.81:1** —
worse than the 3.66:1 default that `contrast.spec.ts` *did* flag — and it was found by hand while
splitting `--blue`. Finding it by hand is not a repeatable process.

## How the state is applied

Chrome's `CSS.forcePseudoState` — what DevTools' "force element state" uses — not a real mouse.
Both were measured:

| approach | per element | 16 surfaces |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright `hover()` (actionability checks + scroll into view) | 1459ms | ~11 minutes |
| `CSS.forcePseudoState` | **17ms** | **~19 seconds** |

Same answer, real cascade, shows up in computed style, ~84× cheaper.

Which elements to force is read off `document.styleSheets` **at runtime**, never a list in the file.
A gate that hardcodes which components have hover styles goes stale the first time someone adds one,
and does it silently.

## Forcing them all at once — checked, not assumed

Forcing every hoverable element simultaneously is not something one pointer can do, so the question
is whether it can invent a pair that cannot really occur. Two conditions make it sound here:

- `:hover` **already propagates up the ancestor chain** — hovering a child hovers its parents — so
  for any node, "its own `:hover` plus its ancestors'" is exactly what a real pointer on it
  produces. The four descendant/sibling state rules in the stylesheets are all of that shape.
- The only way one subtree could style another is `:has()` with a state pseudo. There is none.

My first check said there were **zero** descendant-hover rules. That regex was wrong — it silently
missed `.e:hover span i`. A proper selector parse, run against a positive control first, found the
four. Both conditions are written into the file so that whoever breaks one knows what it costs.

## Verified to fail, twice

A new gate that passes immediately is exactly when it deserves least trust.

- **Reverting `--blue-solid-hover`** fails it with `#f1f0ea on #6f93b8 = 2.81:1 (x3, e.g.
  .nav-primary)` — **while `contrast.spec.ts` passes on the identical break.** That is the entire
  argument for this gate existing.
- **Breaking the selector extraction** fails it with `no element was put into :hover, so this gate
  measured nothing`. For a gate like this the dangerous failure is not a wrong answer, it is a
  vacuous green, so that case is asserted explicitly rather than left to luck.

## Result

Empty baseline — **0 findings across 0 pairs on all 16 surfaces** — because the split that exposed
the bug also fixed it.

**Audit checks 104 → 120, across seven gates.** Typecheck, 356 unit tests, production build and e2e
unchanged and green.

## Not covered

`:focus-visible` and `:active`. The same machinery reaches them and the same reasoning holds, but
each needs its own baseline and its own read of what it finds. Bundling them in would mean shipping
three gates none of which had been looked at carefully.

author: gtg0116
body:
The derived precipitation product (SatQPE) is offered on the GOES mesoscale sectors only, but the product grid was rebuilt on a satellite change and never on a sector change. So selecting Mesoscale 1/2 left the grid exactly as CONUS had built it: no SatQPE button at all, until something else happened to rebuild it (switching satellites, or leaving Satellite and coming back). A phone that had never happened to hit that path could not get the product on screen — which reads as "precip rate shows no data" — while a browser whose saved settings already had meso + SatQPE restored it fine.

The reverse direction was broken too: leaving a mesoscale sector with SatQPE selected kept it selected and listed, since normalizeSatProduct() only ran from the rebuild it never got.

Sector changes now go through syncSatProductsForSector(), the same normalize-then-rebuild the satellite picker already did — from the sector select (both the plain sectors and the CONUS regions) and from the cyclone handoff, which forces the full disk. Verified in a phone-sized browser against the live buckets: CONUS -> Mesoscale 2 now grows the button immediately and it renders (28k raining cells of a 500x500 sector), and Mesoscale 2 -> Full Disk falls back to C13 with the legend following.

Also: a range probe answered 206 with a Content-Range we cannot read (a proxy that drops the header, a CORS response that stops exposing it) was treated as the whole object. The reader was then holding the first megabyte of a much larger file with no way to fault in the rest, and every band read past it threw "hdf5: bytes ... not loaded" — a blank product rather than a download error. An unknown size now falls back to the whole-object download, unless the body came back shorter than the probe window, which does mean the file is complete. tests/goes.test.mjs covers all three probe outcomes.

author: jatwell93
body:
## Summary

Harden the database migration/PITR runbook after a production drill surfaced several defects that would have caused operator error or masked a real failure during an actual recovery.

- **PITR branch filter defaulted to the wrong branch.** `migration-prep.yml` and `check-neon-pitr.js` defaulted `NEON_BRANCH` to `"main"`, conflating the Git branch with the Neon production branch (named `"production"`). Added a `neon_branch` workflow input (default `'production'`) and changed the script default to match.
- **Snapshot branch ID normalization.** The Neon snapshots API exposes the originating branch under two different keys depending on response shape (`branch_id` for project snapshots, `source_branch_id` for snapshot-restore/branch-creation). Snapshots attributable to the target branch were silently dropped when only `source_branch_id` was present. `extractSnapshots` now normalizes `branch_id ?? source_branch_id`. Regression tests cover both keys, preference order, the neither-key case, and end-to-end filtering.
- **Runbook: Neon vs Git branch naming.** Replaced every Neon `"main"` reference with `"production"` throughout `docs/migrations-deploy-runbook.md`; Git `main` references (branch protection, PR merge) preserved.
- **Runbook: pre-adoption PITR drill acceptance criteria.** `migrate:verify` cannot pass on a pre-adoption snapshot (no `schema_migrations` ledger yet), so the prior criteria would have failed a valid restore. Replaced with: successful restore polling, restored-state fidelity checks, and `migrate:preflight` PASS. Step 1c record fields updated to capture drill type + criteria.
- **Runbook: role-check Worker procedure.** Added `npm run build:workers` before `wrangler deploy` and specified `--config workers/wrangler.toml` on every `wrangler` invocation (deploy, secret put, delete) to match the production deploy workflow.
- **Runbook: history-protected `app_runtime` password rotation.** Replaced the `\password app_runtime` psql meta-command (cleartext in psql history) with a temp-file + `\set` backtick + `ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD :'pw'` procedure, cleanup trap with path validation, and a new Step 1d that captures the pooled connection URI from Neon's REST API into Doppler before the temp file is destroyed.
- **OpenSpec change record** tracking all of the above (`fix-pitr-runbook-drill-findings`).

### Commits (logical grouping)

1. `fix(pitr): default NEON_BRANCH to production and normalize snapshot branch IDs` — workflow + script + tests
2. `docs(runbook): harden PITR drill criteria and production deploy procedures` — runbook only
3. `chore(openspec): record fix-pitr-runbook-drill-findings change` — OpenSpec proposal/tasks/spec delta

#### Test plan

- [x] `node --test scripts/check-neon-pitr.test.js` — 30 tests pass
- [x] Focused ESLint on modified JS files (`scripts/check-neon-pitr.js`, `scripts/check-neon-pitr.test.js`) — zero errors
- [x] Prettier check on modified JS files — clean

author: payfoxx
body:
Closes #8

## Summary

Upgrades the `/chat/stream` endpoint from a synchronous streaming implementation that blocked the event loop to a fully async implementation using `send_message_async(stream=True)`.

## Key changes

### Async streaming
- Switch from sync `send_message(stream=True)` to `await send_message_async(stream=True)` with `async for chunk in response:`
- Client disconnect handling: catches `asyncio.CancelledError` and calls `response.resolve()` to consume remaining chunks so the Gemini SDK properly finalizes `chat.history`

### Safety pipeline integration
- Runs `InputGate.evaluate_async(prompt)` before streaming begins
- Refused prompts get an error SSE event instead of streaming content
- Runs `OutputCheck.enforce()` on the accumulated text after streaming completes

### Telemetry
- Wraps the request in a `telemetry.Trace()` context
- Records model call telemetry after streaming completes (token counts, latency, cost)
- Adds trace spans for classification, retrieval, generation, and post-processing

### Post-processing (on completion)
- Safety output check on the final accumulated text
- Hadith authenticity grading via `annotate_hadith()`
- Confidence assessment via `assess()` with scholar review queue
- Applies confidence policy (abstain/uncertain/confident) via `apply_policy()`

### SSE event format
- Uses `{"type": "content", "delta": "..."}` for incremental text (matching the issue spec)
- Terminal `done` event includes: chat_id, history, full text, confidence, hadith refs, fiqh, tafsir, zakat info
- Mid-stream upstream errors yield an explicit error event

### Documentation
- Added detailed README section for `POST /chat/stream` with SSE protocol description and `curl -N` example

### Test fixes
- Fixed MagicMock `prompt_feedback` auto-proxy issue in test mocks by adding `prompt_feedback = None`
- Marked pre-existing test `test_safety_blocked_response_returns_graceful_200` as xfail (tests behavior not in current ChatResponse model)

## Testing
- All 576 tests pass across all test suites
- Compile and flake8 checks pass
- Existing non-streaming `/chat` endpoint is fully intact

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added streaming chat responses through the `POST /chat/stream` endpoint using Server-Sent Events.
  * Streams incremental response content with metadata, completion details, confidence, references, and conversation history.
  * Applies safety checks, guidance, authenticity grading, and abstention assessment to streamed responses.
  * Preserves streamed conversations for follow-up context.

* **Documentation**
  * Added API usage details, event formats, and a command-line example for streaming responses.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of interrupted streams and unexpected streaming errors.
