author: dwats250
body:
**GOVERNANCE CHANGE — opened as a DRAFT and held for Dustin (PRD-186, GOV-1).**
This PR changes a governance guardrail in `docs/PRD_PROCESS.md` (the Lane
Downgrade Prohibition and the GOVERNANCE CLASS-Matrix row), so it names itself
as governance and carries a visible hold.

## Why

Connector thread 3687825284 on #177 found PRD-272 violating the Lane Downgrade
Prohibition. The finding was correct, and verification showed it was systemic:
**every** MICRO/GOVERNANCE PRD in the tree trips the rule — 155, 156, 171, 202,
272. Dustin ruled 2026-07-30: fix the rule, not the PRDs.

Two independent defects produced that:

1. **`PRD_PROCESS.md` contradicted itself.** Line 57 declares registry and index
   bookkeeping implicit in every PRD lifecycle and "not enumerated in PRD FILES
   sections"; line 432 listed `docs/PRD_REGISTRY.md` as a GOVERNANCE HIGH-RISK
   FILE, making it a FILES-intersection trigger. A file cannot be both.
2. **No payload-vs-pointer distinction.** `PROJECT_STATE.md` is genuinely
   high-risk when a PRD rewrites it (queue authority — a wrong claim misroutes a
   fresh session, the exact failure PRD-272 existed to repair) and not when a
   closeout moves the active-PRD pointer one line. Treating both alike retired
   the MICRO lane for governance bookkeeping, against PRD-229 tiering.

## What lands

| R | Change |
|---|--------|
| R1 | `docs/PRD_REGISTRY.md` removed from the GOVERNANCE HIGH-RISK FILES cell (8 paths → 7) |
| R2 | Prohibition amended: intersection forces HIGH-RISK only for a **payload** touch; `PROJECT_STATE.md` pointer claims need a `(pointer)`/`(bookkeeping)` annotation |
| R3 | `_validate_lane_payload_prohibition` guard, bounded to PRD >= 276, +10 tests |
| R4 | STATED LIMITATION appended to PRD-171 (payload: the two templates) and PRD-202 (payload: `CLAUDE.md`) |

No lane is retro-flipped and no second-model disposition line is written: all
affected PRDs merged long ago, a pre-merge gate cannot be satisfied after merge,
and the waiver is the merger's positive act. PRD-155/156 are pointer cases
needing no edit; PRD-272's block landed at `bddb486` on #177.

## Mutation verification (PRD-198 invariant 4)

Each behavior was observed **red** before the guard landed:

- empty the payload-file set → payload test red
- annotation regex never matches → both annotated-pass tests red
- bound set to 0 → the pre-276 exemption test red
- **delete the call site → the wiring test red**

That last test exists because every other test passes even if the guard is never
called from `validate_repository`. Asserting the resolved, not the requested.

## Stated limitations (in the PRD, not hidden)

1. **The guard checks a declaration, not a diff.** An author can annotate
   `(pointer)` and rewrite the file wholesale. Payload-vs-pointer is a judgment
   about intent no static check resolves; the guard makes it explicit and
   reviewable instead of silent, and the fresh-context review is the real check.
2. **The FILES scan is line-oriented over the whole block**, so a parenthetical
   note mentioning a governance file counts as naming it. Left unfixed
   deliberately — it errs toward more ceremony, never less.

## Lane

`HIGH-RISK` / `GOVERNANCE`. `docs/PRD_PROCESS.md` is a GOVERNANCE HIGH-RISK file
and is this PRD's payload — the rule classifies the PRD that writes it.

## Verification

- `validate_prd_registry.py --skip-commit-resolvability` → exit 0
- `ruff check cuttingboard/ tests/ tools/` → clean
- Full suite → **3054 passed, 1 xfailed** (3044 baseline + 10 new)

A Godot HTML5 build (source: [gomyway1216/tomoshibi](https://github.com/gomyway1216/tomoshibi)) added under `/games/tomoshibi`, with its save mirrored to Firebase so a run can continue on another machine.

**Click-to-play.** The wasm is ~38MB, so nothing is fetched until the button is pressed. 41MB on disk, ~12MB over the wire after gzip.

**Why `public/`** rather than separate hosting: the page reaches into `iframe.contentWindow` to hand the game its two save functions, and that is only allowed same-origin. It also matches what this repo already does — `public/` ships three shogi `.bin` files.

`index.wasm` gets `Cache-Control: immutable` (engine template, identical across exports). The `.pck` changes every update and deliberately does not.

**Signed-in and signed-out visitors need no separate handling.** `ensureGameSignIn()` already returns the real user or an anonymous account, so the save keys off whichever uid comes back.

Two easy-to-get-wrong details:

- The bridge attaches in the iframe **ref callback** — inside an iframe `window` is the frame's own, which needs a document first.
- The save is fetched **before** the iframe mounts, because Godot reads `window.tomoshibiCloudLoaded` synchronously at startup and cannot await a fetch. On failure it mounts with `''`; the game still has its local save.

Nothing here throws — the local save is the real one. An empty save is the one exception to write coalescing: it means the run ended, and a player who just died may close the tab before a timer fires.

Needs [backend#58](https://github.com/gomyway1216/Yudai-new-portfolio-backend-ts/pull/58) for the endpoints; without it the cloud copy silently no-ops and the game plays normally.

Tests: 9 passing, tsc and eslint clean.

---

Replaces #675, whose first build commit carried a `.pck` exported while the game still used a third-party sprite pack that forbids redistributing the material. This branch is built fresh from `main` so that blob is not in its history.

author: techwithanirudh
body:
Ran `taze` recursively over every workspace and both pnpm catalogs, using the repo's own `taze.config.ts`.

## What moved

| Scope | Updates |
| --- | --- |
| `catalog:` (default) | `@eslint/js`, `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@types/node`, `cspell`, `eslint`, `prettier`, `tailwindcss` |
| `catalogs.react19` | `@types/react`, `react`, `react-dom` |
| root | `@changesets/cli`, `@commitlint/*`, `@turbo/gen`, `lefthook`, `taze`, `turbo`, `packageManager` → `pnpm@11.17.0` |
| `@repo/api` | `lightningcss-wasm`, `shadcn`, `browserslist`, `postcss` |
| `@repo/docs` | `next`/`@next/*`, `ai`/`@ai-sdk/*`, `shiki`/`@shikijs/*`, `@takumi-rs/*`, `mermaid`, `motion`, `lucide-react`, `import-in-the-middle`, `swiper`, `twoslash` |
| `@repo/style` | `lightningcss`, `browserslist`, `ora`, `postcss` |
| `@repo/ui` | `radix-ui` + `@radix-ui/*`, `@vidstack/react`, `lucide-react`, `motion` |
| `tooling/*` | `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-turbo`, `@next/eslint-plugin-next`, `@cspell/*`, `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`, `postcss` |

## Two deliberate holds

### TypeScript stays on 6.x

`taze` offers 7.0.2 and `taze.config.ts` explicitly permits typescript majors (`packageMode: { typescript: 'major' }`), but:

```
Error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.
    at typescript-eslint@8.65.0/dist/index.js:52:11
```

That kills all seven lint tasks. Held at `^6.0.3`, with a comment in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Revisit when typescript-eslint supports TS 7.

### The fumadocs family stays on its current versions

Two separate failures, both from version skew inside the family:

**1. Build** — `fumadocs-ui` 16.13.0 dropped `useTranslations` (and `I18nLabel`) from `contexts/i18n`, a breaking change in a minor release. Every `fumadocs-openapi` 10.x still imports it:

```
Export useTranslations doesn't exist in target module
  fumadocs-openapi/dist/ui/client/i18n.js:4
Did you mean to import useI18n?
```

Nothing flagged it at install time — `fumadocs-openapi@10.10.3` declares a peer of `fumadocs-ui ^16.9.0`, which 16.13.0 satisfies. The peer range is stale upstream.

**2. Docs lint** — pinning just `core` + `ui` fixed the build but left:

```
SyntaxError: Export named 'frontmatter' not found in module
  '.../development/apps/docs.mdx?collection=docs&only=frontmatter'
```

That query string is `fumadocs-mdx`'s loader contract, which `fumadocs-core` consumes. `fumadocs-mdx` 15.2.0 emits a shape `fumadocs-core` 16.9.0 doesn't read, so those two have to move together too.

Bumping the family piecemeal just relocates the failure, so all nine packages now sit on the versions `dev` already runs. **Pinned exactly, not with carets** — every caret here floats straight back into the incompatible range (`^16.9.0` → 16.13.0, `^15.0.7` → 15.2.0).

Upgrading the family as a coordinated set — including `fumadocs-openapi` 11.x, which requires `fumadocs-ui ^16.10.0` and restructures its UI entrypoints — is worth doing, but as its own PR rather than inside a routine bump.

## Incidental formatting

- `apps/docs/scripts/sync-changelog.ts` — prettier 3.9 lays out an arrow function with a return-type annotation differently.
- `apps/style/src/components/sidebar/_index.scss`, `_theme-switcher.scss` — already unformatted on `dev`; needed for `pnpm format` to pass. Same change appears in #63, whichever lands first.

## Verification

Green locally: `pnpm format`, `pnpm check:spelling`, `pnpm lint:ws` (sherif), and `pnpm lint` for all six non-docs packages.

For `@repo/docs`, `bun ./scripts/lint.ts` now passes (`collected 14 URLs, 0 errors`) and eslint reduces to the same 14 `no-unsafe-*` errors a clean `dev` checkout produces without a prior build — CI resolves those by running `pnpm build` first. The Vercel web preview built successfully on the previous commit, confirming the build fix.

author: asafgolombek
body:
This repository went public so npm would attest its releases — provenance requires a public source repo. That means it can now receive outside pull requests **with no contributor agreement in place**, and it was the only repo in the org without a CLA gate or code scanning.

## `cla.yml` — ported verbatim, deliberately

It is copied from `nimbus-sdk` rather than re-derived, because its comments record real incidents that a fresh implementation would have to re-earn:

- the job is named `cla-assistant`, not `cla`, because a job named `cla` publishes a check-run that collides with the required commit **status** of the same name — two things reporting under one required context;
- the concurrency key includes the head SHA, after PR #38 saw the newer commit's run dropped and the required `cla` status left missing for the head that mattered;
- the action's allowlist keeps both `bot*` and `*[bot]` forms, after removing one broke release PR #41 while PR #35 had passed with it — the reasoning for removal was sound and the behaviour disagreed;
- `allowlisted-status` exists at all because contributor-assistant *skips* allowlisted authors and posts no status, so a required `cla` check never appeared for the maintainer or the release bot.

The only repo-specific field is already dynamic: `repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }},.github`.

## `codeql.yml` — with stricter egress than `ci.yml`

`egress-policy: block` here versus `audit` in `ci.yml`, and that difference is intentional. `build-mode: none` means CodeQL reads the source rather than building it, so this job installs nothing from npm or the Bun registry — its endpoint list is small and stable enough to enforce. `ci.yml` runs `bunx tsc`/`bunx biome` and cannot make that promise.

`codeql-config.yml` ignores `dist` and `node_modules`. It deliberately does **not** ignore `fixtures/` — those are hand-written JSON specs that contribute no results anyway, and excluding a directory to quieten a scanner is how a real finding later gets excluded by accident.

## Two things still needed before these actually work

1. **`CLA_BOT_CLIENT_ID` and `CLA_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` must be granted to this repo.** They are org secrets with `visibility: selected`, currently scoped to the sibling repos only — the same trap that made the release workflow fail with an empty `private-key`.
2. **The `nimbus-cla-bot` App must be installed on this repo** (installation id `148691954`). Adding a repo to an App installation needs an Organization Owner; my token gets 403.

Until both are done the CLA job fails at the token-mint step. That is loud rather than silent, and it does not affect the other checks.

## Not yet required checks

Neither is added to the branch ruleset yet. Requiring a check that has never reported blocks every PR — they should be promoted once they have run green here.

author: cptkoolbeenz
body:
Fixes #744.

## The failure shape, not the failure

`scpi_printf` formats into a 192-byte stack buffer. On overflow it wrote `sizeof(buf) - 1` bytes — **dropping the last character** — with no log, no SCPI error, and a `void` return the caller could not check.

For `CONF:CAP:JSON?` that last character is almost always the **separating comma** between chunks. Losing it does not shorten one field: it makes the entire ~8 KB response **unparseable**, because the next chunk's members run together with no separator:

```
...,"clock_ok":false}"rate_model":{...
```

Clients render their UI from that query.

It already bit once. The `timing` chunk reached **189 of 192** bytes on the shipped build and **exactly 192** on the legacy 200 MHz build — it truncated in one supported configuration, and was caught by an adversarial audit doing the arithmetic across every rate, not by a test or a build warning ([PR #740](https://github.com/daqifi/daqifi-nyquist-firmware/pull/740) `c062ffee`).

## What this changes

Truncation now emits `LOG_E` naming the **format string** and the **length needed**, and the function returns vsnprintf's count so a caller that cares can check it. Output behaviour is unchanged, so no existing caller has to react.

## What it deliberately does NOT do

It does **not** make truncation impossible. Chunking through a larger buffer would, and that remains the option if the JSON surface keeps growing — I did not do it here because it changes every call site's cost, and this PR is the diagnosability fix.

Nor is this a live defect being repaired: **no shipped chunk overflows today**. Every capability chunk is fixed-length, with no device-controlled string that could be inflated to force one. This converts a *latent silent corruption* into a *diagnosable* one — the difference between a field report of "the app shows nothing" and a log line naming the chunk.

## Verification (E, board 7E2898F46200E8A7)

`CONF:CAP:JSON?` after the change: parses, **10 top-level keys**, **11 streaming keys**, zero truncation reports, error queue clean.

## Note on the companion test

**[daqifi-python-test-suite#128](https://github.com/daqifi/daqifi-python-test-suite/pull/128) does not fail on pre-#744 firmware, and I am not claiming it does.** With no reachable overflow there is no device behaviour that distinguishes fixed from unfixed. What it buys is detection from now on: the day a chunk crosses 192 bytes, post-#744 firmware fails the test naming the format string, where pre-#744 firmware would have returned corrupt JSON silently.

**Environment:** firmware `fix/744-scpi-printf-truncation`, XC32 v4.60 / MPLAB X v6.30, `-O3 -Werror`.

### Motivation
- Implement a transaction-oriented, atomic publisher for Phase 4 (Documentary Blueprint) that stages the complete artifact set, protects frozen upstream Phase 1–3 artifacts, and guarantees idempotent, recoverable commits per the Phase 4 publication contract.
- Ensure deterministic artifacts (aggregate + exact Long/Short projections), manifest merge, physical SHA-256 validation, and validation-record-as-final-commit semantics required by the Phase 4 lifecycle.

### Description
- Add strongly‑typed publication contracts, diagnostics, artifact entry and artifact/result DTOs in `Phase4PublicationContracts.cs` to represent requests, results, artifact inventory, and reason codes.
- Implement a transaction coordinator and publication service in `Phase4DocumentaryBlueprintPublicationService.cs` that performs preflight validation, acquires an execution-scoped lock, recovers stale transactions, stages all seven Phase 4 artifacts into a temporary directory, validates staged artifacts, prepares a merged manifest, atomically replaces the `04-blueprint` directory, commits the manifest and then writes `validation/phase-04-validation.json` as the final commit marker, and supports backup/rollback on failures.
- Provide infrastructure primitives in `Phase4PublicationInfrastructure.cs` including a deterministic JSON serializer, filesystem helpers with physical SHA-256, a process-scoped keyed semaphore lock, a conservative recovery service for stale temp/backups, and a manifest merger and published-authority validator that enforces Long/Short equivalence with the aggregate.

author: mooreli104
body:
The cover image gave the answer away three different ways. This fixes all three.

| Leak | Fix |
|---|---|
| The title is printed into the cover artwork | An offline ingest job detects and blanks it before storage |
| `ROUND_START` sent the raw `cdn.myanimelist.net` URL, so devtools showed the answer | The client now gets a bare `/image/{id}` served by our own backend |
| `startRound` picked via `Math.random()` with no memory, so rounds repeated | `Room` tracks `usedAnimeIds` for the length of a game |

## How it works

Covers are no longer fetched during a round. `gradlew ingest` downloads the MAL top 500, scrubs each title, and stores the result in Postgres; the game serves bytes from `GET /image/{id}`. The round path makes no third-party call and the URL leaks nothing.

`AnimeRepository` is the seam both the game and ingest talk to, with `PostgresAnimeRepository` (plain JDBC) and `FakeAnimeRepository` in the test source set — mirroring the existing `SessionSender` / `RecordingSender` split. `randomExcluding` deliberately does not select the image column, so starting a round moves a few hundred bytes and the picture travels separately.

## Why not Tesseract

Tesseract was tried first and is reverted in this branch (`623bd2e`, `ea100c1`). It found **zero** text on real covers — anime titles are stylised display logotypes, often light-on-light over busy artwork, not the document text Tesseract is built for. It therefore blanked random artwork and passed the leak straight through: the stored Fullmetal Alchemist cover had its title fully legible with Edward's torso blacked out.

Detection now runs in a Python sidecar (`backend/scripts/scrub_service.py`) using EasyOCR's CRAFT scene-text detector. Accept rate went from ~21% to **86%**.

Two design points worth keeping:

- **Only detection is used, never recognition.** We need to know *where* text is, not what it says. So the verify step re-runs *detection* on the scrubbed image and rejects if any region survives — a check that does not depend on the title being legible. A recognition-based verify cannot catch the failure that actually happens, which is exactly how the Tesseract version shipped broken.
- **Python decodes the cover**, so WebP works for free. About a quarter of MAL's covers are WebP and Java's `ImageIO` cannot read them at all.

Rejection rules: zero detections (means detection failed, not that the cover is clean), boxed area over 35% (too little picture left to guess from), or any text surviving verify.

## Verification

- **69 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped** — including 3 integration tests driving the real sidecar.
- Full ingest run: **433 of 500 accepted (86%)**; rejections were 43 "no text detected", 16 "boxed area too large", 8 "text region(s) survived".
- Visually inspected images pulled straight out of Postgres (Spirited Away, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, Fruits Basket 2nd Season, and others) — titles gone, artwork intact.
- Drove two full rounds over the real WebSocket protocol: `ROUND_START` carried `imageUrl=/image/46102` with no MAL URL, `GET /image/{id}` returned a valid JPEG, a wrong guess scored 0, a correct guess scored 993, the round ended early once all players had guessed, and `GAME_OVER` named the winner.

## Known limitation

CRAFT does not detect vertical CJK text, so a cover whose title runs vertically could still pass. Rotating 90° and re-detecting was tried and did not find it either, so that code was not shipped. Documented in `CLAUDE.md`. Tiny studio/copyright credits sometimes survive but are illegible at normal size and are never the answer.

## Reviewer notes

- Ingest needs `DATABASE_URL` and a Python with `easyocr` on `SCRUB_PYTHON`; tests needing either are `@EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable`-guarded so `gradlew test` stays green without them.
- `MAL_CLIENT_ID` is now read from the environment, but still has a hardcoded fallback — so the key remains in source and in git history. Removing it properly needs the fallback dropped plus a history rewrite.
- Javalin still has no SLF4J provider, so its logging goes to a no-op logger.

author: jakubmiasik
body:
Details were built on first view, so whoever opened an artifact first paid for several API calls and waited. The analysis run now collects them for every artifact and stores them, making the modal a database read.

## Shared builder

The details builder moves out of the workspaces route into `itemDetailsService`, so the run and the details endpoint assemble sections identically rather than diverging over time.

The endpoint still builds and stores anything the run did not cover — artifacts created since the last scan, or runs from before this change — so nothing breaks if a run hasn't happened yet, and existing behaviour is preserved as the fallback.

## Bounded, because it is expensive

Collection is the second-longest phase of a run (one or more API calls per artifact), so:

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ANALYSIS_COLLECT_DETAILS` | `true` | `false` skips the phase entirely |
| `ANALYSIS_DETAIL_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | Artifacts read in parallel |
| `ANALYSIS_DETAIL_MAX_ITEMS` | `2000` | Cap per run; anything past it loads on first view |

The phase reports progress per artifact through the run telemetry added in #43, honours cancellation, and a failure on one artifact never fails the run — failures are counted and reported in the activity log.

## OneLake is deliberately skipped during collection

The storage phase already lists the same OneLake paths. Repeating that listing per artifact would roughly double a run for no new data, so `includeOneLake: false` is passed during collection. It is still gathered when an artifact is opened directly, so nothing is lost from the view.

## Provenance

Cached rows record which run collected them (`run_id`), and the modal says *"Stored … during run #N"*, so you can tell scan-collected details from ones fetched on view.

## Testing

`npm run check` — 25 files, 40 tests passing. 5 new tests drive the builder with a stub service and cover: a lakehouse assembling metadata, tables, SQL endpoint schema and OneLake in order; a failing section being reported without losing the others; an unprovisioned endpoint being reported as not ready **and not queried**; dashboard tiles resolving report and model ids to names with a fallback for unknown ids; and OneLake being skipped when the flag is off.

## Note

The first run after this merges will be noticeably longer than previous ones — that is the cost being moved from view time to scan time. If it is too slow for your tenant, lower `ANALYSIS_DETAIL_MAX_ITEMS` or set `ANALYSIS_COLLECT_DETAILS=false` to return to lazy loading.

author: simonspies
body:
Type attributes gain a payload, so `[@spec ...]` can be written wherever a type can: the parser folds type parsing into the expression mutual block, since an attribute's payload is an expression, and elaboration turns the attribute into the specification on an `Untyped.Typ.arrow`. A data declaration's payloads are elaborated before any specification could be typechecked, so `[@spec]` is still rejected there — `Tests/spec_types/spec_in_type_decl.ml` pins that. The second commit takes an argument-less declaration's annotation as the declaration's own type, so `let rec f : T = fun x -> ...` is specified through the arrow it is annotated with.

Third of five PRs accepting `[@spec ...]` in any type position.

author: yspritanhyzygy
body:
Depends on #2243 — before that split, the key behind the sidebar entry also drove the Discord guild picker and the remote TTS card, so this rename would have hit both.

Chinese has two words here and they are not interchangeable:

- **服务器** is a server as a *machine* — a host, a box, someone else's computer.
- **服务端** is the *server side* — the serving half of a client/server pair, wherever it runs.

Osaurus's server is a process on the user's own Mac. It was called 服务器 everywhere, which reads as "a remote box you administer". The sidebar made that especially odd, because every sibling section names something you configure and that one named hardware:

```
通用 / 模型 / 智能体与自动化 / 服务器 / 隐私与安全 / 账户     (before)
通用 / 模型 / 智能体与自动化 / 服务端 / 隐私与安全 / 账户     (after)
```

Same inside `Server → Settings`, where the group header sits next to four aspect names and holds Connection / Global Proxy / Authentication:

```
服务器 / 生成 / 性能 / 能力 / 生命周期     (before)
服务端 / 生成 / 性能 / 能力 / 生命周期     (after)
```

The word also repeated four levels deep — sidebar section (`ManagementTab.swift:31`), the item inside it (`:171`), the page title (`ServerView.swift:100`), and that group header (`ServerSettingsSection.swift:105`) — so the same noun appeared four times on the way in.

## What changed

33 zh-Hans values: the sidebar and menu labels, the lifecycle states (`Server Running`, `Starting Server...`, `Server is locked`, …), the API-reference and Settings body copy, and the two strings that point at the navigation by name (`Manage keys in the Server → Overview tab.`, `Test endpoints from Server tab…`) — those had to move together with the label or they would name a tab that no longer exists.

It also removes `服务器端`, a clumsier way of writing "server-side" that appeared once, in `Verbosity of the server-side request log.`. The catalog's other `server-side` string already said 服务端, so the two now agree.

## What deliberately did not change

67 keys keep 服务器, because for them the machine sense is the right one:

| | |
|---|---|
| MCP servers and remote tool connections | `MCP server`, `This server requires OAuth sign in to provide tools.` |
| Discord guilds | `Server IDs`, `Invite the bot to your server` — Discord's own Chinese calls a guild 服务器 |
| Third-party endpoints | `OpenAI-Compatible Server`, `Custom Server` |
| Osaurus's cloud backend, the relay, a paired peer | `no requests are sent to Osaurus servers` |
| The local OAuth callback listener | `Could not start the ChatGPT sign-in callback server…` — a loopback listener, not the inference server |
| `Serverless open models` | 无服务器 is the settled rendering of "serverless" |
| The Insights `Server` / `Local` pills | that `Server` means the far end of the wire, i.e. the cloud provider |

`MCP server health check` stays 服务器 even though the endpoint is Osaurus's own: "MCP server" is a protocol role, and the catalog's other MCP strings all use that spelling. Renaming this one alone would trade a small inconsistency for a bigger one.

## Checks

- Only zh-Hans is touched. Compiling the catalog with `xcstringstool` before and after: `en` 0 changed, `de` 0, `ko` 0, `ru` 0, `zh-Hant` 0, `zh-Hans` 33 changed, 0 added, 0 removed anywhere.
- The diff is 33 insertions / 33 deletions, every line a `"value"` line — no key, `state`, `comment` or `extractionState` moves.
- `scripts/i18n/check.sh` is identical to `main`: 6473 keys, 686 stale, 3160 Swift localization keys referenced, `0 suspect literals`.
- `scripts/i18n/lint-zh-style.py --check`: `0 value(s) need fixing`.
- Afterwards no string contains both words, `服务器端` is gone, and the compounds that merely embed the characters — 中继服务器 (relay), 回调服务器 (callback), 无服务器 (serverless) — are untouched.

3 of the 33 have `extractionState: stale` with no call site (`Server settings moved`, `Configure the local API server for external integrations.`, and the `Port, network exposure, CORS…` banner body). They cannot be checked on screen. They are included because the last two are a title/body pair whose text names the navigation path, so if they are ever restored they should not point at a label that no longer exists.

author: zootimusmaximusbackup
body:
## What this is

A new page for clients at `/app/finance-os.html`, plus its own read endpoint at `/api/read/finance-os`. It lists every credit card we can see, the limit and balance on each, and how much of the card is being used — plus subscription tier and status, alerts, an on-demand credit refresh button, and the monthly optimization report.

W9 of the finance-os-banking batch. Shared board: `docs/workflows/finance-os-banking.md`.

## The rule that drove the whole design

**A missing credit limit is unknown, not zero.**

`tradelines` (migration 054) deliberately stores no utilization column, and `credit_limit_cents` is nullable. A credit report that lists a balance with no limit is completely ordinary. Showing that card as "0%" would tell someone their credit looks perfect when the truth is nobody knows — the kind of lie that looks like good news.

| Situation | What the screen shows |
|---|---|
| Limit missing | blank, plus "no credit limit on file" |
| Balance missing | blank, plus "no balance on file" |
| Limit is zero | blank, plus "credit limit is zero" (÷0 is undefined, not 0%) |
| Limit known, balance genuinely zero | **0%** — a true fact, not suppressed |
| Balance above the limit | **118%**, not clamped, and raised as a blocker |

Totals exclude any card with an incomplete pair **and say how many they excluded** — a total that quietly drops what it could not read looks authoritative and is short by an unknown amount.

## Two audiences, two fields

`data.js` collapses 401 and 403 into one "unauthorized" state, so this screen does its own fetch and classifies the raw status. But the four states are told apart by `code`, **not** by leaking engineer detail into the page:

- **`text`** — what a customer reads. Plain English. No filenames, no status codes, no jargon.
- **`detail`** — what an engineer reads. Goes to a `title` tooltip and a `[finance-os]` console line. Never rendered.

| State | Customer sees | Console gets |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | "Your session has expired. Sign in again to see your cards." | `401 on your cards` |
| 403 | "Your account does not have access to your cards." | `403 — role or principal kind not admitted` |
| 404 unrouted | "We are still building this. It will appear here when it is ready." | `unrouted: read/subscriptions — 075_subscriptions.sql has not shipped` |
| 5xx | "Something went wrong on our end. Try again shortly." | `server error 502 on your cards` |

A sweep test runs every branch across three section names and **fails if any banned token** (`.sql`, `.mjs`, a 4xx/5xx number, `client_id`, `not_found`, `/api/`) reaches customer copy — and checks every sentence is sentence-cased and ends in a full stop.

## Decisions made

1. **Two of the three named spec documents do not exist.** The wireframe and addendum are not on this account — `fundhub-docs/sources/` holds only `AIRTABLE-BASE-EXTRACT.md`, and HANDOFF.md:90 confirms it. The §8 field list from the task brief was used as the spec; layout grammar came from `client-portal.html`, an approved implementation that does exist. **No tile was invented to fill the gap.**
2. **The screen gets its own endpoint.** `/api/read/tradelines` is staff-gated and takes `client_id` from the query — correct for the Closer Dashboard, wrong for a client's own screen. `/api/read/finance-os` admits a `client` principal and takes the scope from the **session**, never the query string. `api/read/tradelines.mjs` is unchanged; no other lane's surface was touched.
3. **Gate:** staff (any named client) + client principal (own rows only). Affiliates and partners are not admitted. Staff must name a client; a firehose of everybody's balances is the kind of endpoint that becomes a breach.
4. **Rows only from the endpoint, no derived totals.** Utilization and the sums live in the view module the screen carries and that is unit-tested. Computing them server-side too would create a second answer that can disagree with the first.
5. **The optimization report is the `credit-optimization-roadmap` entitlement (032) — not `src/optimize/`,** which optimises ad spend and has nothing to do with a consumer's credit.

## Out of scope

- **W2** (`subscriptions`, 075), **W3** (soft-pull path), **W4** (`alerts`, 078) have not merged. Those sections render an honest unavailable state. When they land, the screen shows their data with no HTML change.
- **Bills, business-vs-personal, payment reminders, cash-flow projections** — no table behind any of them, so they appear **nowhere**, not even greyed out. `NOT_SOURCED` lists all nine refused fields and why.
- No migration. No new dependencies.

## Compliance

No flags outstanding. The earlier one — engineer wording on a consumer-facing screen — is fixed above rather than deferred, and a test now prevents its return. No credit-outcome claims are made anywhere; utilization is displayed as measured, never predicted.

## A bug found by running it, not reading it

`buildRoadmap()` first read `res.body.data`. `readHandler` endpoints answer under `items`; only the hand-rolled tradelines endpoint answers `data`. The tile found nothing against a perfectly healthy server. Fixed by `rows()` and pinned by four tests. A unit test against a made-up response would have stayed green forever — the AUDIT-FINDINGS.md shape exactly.

## Also: `npm run lint` now exists

CLAUDE.md §6 requires it and there was no such script — nor an eslint config. `scripts/lint.mjs` is a zero-dependency syntax gate over every `.mjs`/`.js` in the repo **plus every inline `<script>` in the HTML screens** — where this repo's browser logic lives, none of which any test imports, so a syntax error there renders a blank page under a green suite. **468 files parse clean**, so it is not a red gate. Mutation-checked both ways. Syntax only: `pg` and `inngest` are the only dependencies here and §8 forbids adding more without asking.

`npx tsc --noEmit` is still not possible — no `tsconfig.json`, no TypeScript anywhere. §6 should drop that line rather than have a dependency added to satisfy a checklist.

## Proof

- `npm run lint`: **468 files clean**, mutation-checked
- `npm test` with no database: **1774 pass, 0 fail, 195 skipped** — run 8 times after one non-reproducing flake, which was not in these files (they ran 20× clean)
- `npm test` against real Postgres 16: **zero new failing test names** vs the same suite with these changes stashed (names diffed, not totals)
- `node db/migrate.mjs` applies clean and **re-applies as a no-op**
- **92 tests added** — 82 unit + 10 endpoint (against the real router, written adversarially: a client naming another client in the URL gets their own rows and no leak)
- Real browser, real seeded session: **renders and does not bounce**. Exercised with a normal card, null limit, null balance, zero limit, real zero balance, over-limit card and an installment loan — all seven correct. Visible page text scanned: **zero banned tokens**, while console and tooltips carry the full diagnostic.
- **Mutation check, 11 deliberate breaks, all 11 caught:** unknown→0, zero-limit dividing, clamping over-limit, collapsing 403 into 401, dropping the `items` shape, unknown cards in totals, **client scope read from the query string (the cross-tenant leak)**, closed lines leaking, affiliate admitted, broken `.mjs`, broken inline script.

`finance-os.html` is in the `ALL` array in `shell.js` and `read/finance-os` is in the `ROUTES` map — a screen missing from the first bounces to command-center, a handler missing from the second 404s. Both have tests that fail if they go missing.

author: kstruck
body:
## What

The 2026-07-30 App Check outage was written down **nowhere in the repo**, which is how it happened. This records it, and corrects every document that called App Check a benign dormant warning — including one row that told you to do the exact thing that caused it.

**Nothing in this PR changes runtime behaviour.** Docs, skills, and one test file.

## The incident

**OBSERVED:** `VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` was set in the Coolify environment → rebuild → the site rendered nothing, permanent spinner, confirmed from two independent machines on two networks. The variable was deleted and the site redeployed → service restored.

**The operative instruction — do not set it — rests on that alone.**

⚠️ **The mechanism is an OPEN QUESTION, and this PR is careful to say so.** The first write-up asserted a causal chain (key flips `src/firebase.ts:25` → `ReCaptchaEnterpriseProvider` loads a script CSP refuses → App Check token never resolves → Firestore SDK, which blocks its first request on that token, goes offline). Codex holed it in round 1: `Dockerfile:15-27` declares `ARG`/`ENV` for six variables, all `VITE_FIREBASE_*`, and `.dockerignore` excludes `.env` — so that key has **no known path into the Vite build at all**, and a runtime variable cannot alter an already-built static bundle.

An unexplained way to kill production eight days before the pilot is worse than an understood one. Three candidates are recorded, none checked, with steps for Kevin.

## Why the docs were dangerous

`mmp-build-and-env`'s troubleshooting row for the `App Check is NOT active` warning said: **"Supply the key (Firebase console → App Check) for prod-like builds."** That is the action.

It looked safe because every callable runs App Check in `monitor` mode — a **true fact supporting a false conclusion**. Server-side leniency cannot rescue a client that fails before it issues a request. Same shape as #320's Sentry CSP gap: a transport-layer denial no application-layer allowance can see.

The 2026-07-06 attestation "App Check is ENFORCED in the Firebase console" was carried by **ten skills** plus three root docs and is contradicted by the code — `lib/validated.ts:94-97` defaults to `monitor`, and `functions/src` has **98 `validated()` declarations all on `monitor`, zero `enforce`**, plus **26 bare `onCall` sites** with no App Check option at all. Marked superseded and UNVERIFIED everywhere.

## Four blocking faults, all unfixed

| # | Fault | Verified how |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CSP omits `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/` + `https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/` from `script-src`, and the former from `frame-src`, on **all three** location blocks (`nginx.conf:33,52,82`) | Read in-repo. Inert while the var is unset |
| 2 | `src/firebase.ts:27` needs a reCAPTCHA **Enterprise** key; the key created is **v3** | Provider verified in repo; *which key exists is Kevin-attested* |
| 3 | The web app was never registered in the console's App Check section | *Kevin-attested*; contradicts the 2026-07-06 attestation — one is wrong |
| 4 | `Dockerfile` declares no `ARG` for the key, so the build cannot receive it | Read in-repo — **found by codex reviewing this record** |

Fault 4 is why fault 1 is not worth "fixing while we're here": adding the `ARG` is what would make the key dangerous.

## Files

`HANDOFF.md` (STOP POINT), `PICKUP-PRESEASON-PILOT.md` §0, `PRESEASON-READINESS-CHECKLIST.md` (G3 closed as accepted risk — it was scheduled for **this week**), `PHASE0-DEPLOY-CHECKLIST.md` Step 4 (marked VOID), and ten skills: `mmp-architecture-contract`, `mmp-build-and-env`, `mmp-change-control`, `mmp-config-and-flags`, `mmp-debugging-playbook`, `mmp-deploy-and-operate`, `mmp-diagnostics-and-tooling`, `mmp-docs-and-writing`, `mmp-failure-archaeology`, `mmp-superadmin-surface`.

## Guard

`tests/docs-state-invariants.test.ts` +12 tests: `src/firebase.ts` must keep exactly one `initializeAppCheck` call **inside** the site-key conditional and keep its non-DEV warning; HANDOFF must keep the do-not-set record.

**Mutation-tested, 5 mutations, 5 killed:**

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Conditional replaced with `if (true)` | ✅ failed |
| Second unguarded `initializeAppCheck` call | ✅ failed |
| Non-DEV warning reworded away | ✅ failed |
| HANDOFF stops naming the variable | ✅ failed |
| **Empty conditional + call moved just below it** (codex's r1 refactor) | ✅ failed — `expected 1359 to be less than 1205`. **Passed before the fix.** |

## Cross-model review — 5 rounds, 8 findings, all valid, all absorbed, none rejected

| Round | What it caught |
|---|---|
| 1 | **3 × P2** — the mechanism is impossible through the tracked Dockerfile; "98/98 callables" overstated coverage (bare `onCall` sites exist); **the new guard was ordering, not containment** — an empty `if` with the call moved below it passed |
| 2 | **2 × P2** — round 1's own fixes left `mmp-debugging-playbook` S7 stating the holed mechanism as fact with "three faults"; and `mmp-config-and-flags` still listed `VITE_API_KEY` as consumed by `AdminPanel.tsx:222` while a note told operators to sync it into Coolify — **`grep -rn VITE_API_KEY src/` returns nothing**, so following it would have put a Gemini key into the public bundle for a feature that does not exist |
| 3 | **1 × P1 + 1 × P2** — HANDOFF asserted the sweep was complete when three surfaces still reported enforcement as done, worst of them `mmp-docs-and-writing:283` inside a block headed *"must never be contradicted when editing docs"* |
| 4 | clean |
| 5 | clean |

**Self-review found three things codex did not**, which is why a clean round is not the review:

1. Two remaining "three faults" phrasings.
2. `PHASE0-DEPLOY-CHECKLIST` Step 4 — an unchecked operator checkbox resting on three separately false premises, whose remedy was "finish App Check config". Marked VOID.
3. ⚠️ **A conflicting account of WHEN the outage happened.** The incident report places its two rebuilds right after #321 — which would make them the `D1wLGiMy → C31xivRN → CR5oJEHh` transitions — but HANDOFF lines 41/44 already attribute those exact two moves to **#322** and **#324**, each verified against prod HTML at the time. Both cannot be right. Recorded as an open question; **do not reason about this incident from bundle hashes until the Coolify deployment history is read.**

## Plan gate

**Not plan-gated.** No money, authorization, production data, or scoring. Docs, skills, and one test file. Closest trigger is authorization — App Check is an attestation layer — but this PR changes no code path, no rule, and no callable option; it records an outage and deletes false guidance.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm --prefix functions run build` | pass |
| `npm --prefix functions test` | 1170 pass |
| `npm --prefix functions run test:emulator` | 250 pass, 2 expected fail, 10 skipped |
| `npx tsc -b` | pass |
| `npm test` | **468 pass** (456 baseline + 12 new) |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 1110 warnings |
| `npm audit` root / functions | 5 / 3 moderate — pre-existing, no package file touched |

⚠️ **One functions-suite run reported `1 failed | 1169 passed`. I did not capture which test.** Two subsequent runs were 1170/1170. Consistent with the known `opsAlertDispatcher` flake, but **I am not asserting that** — the name was not recorded.

## Deploy

**Nothing owed.** No `src/`, `functions/`, `shared/`, or rules files. The only non-doc file is `tests/`, which Vite never emits — so the bundle hash will not move, and per HANDOFF's own note an unmoved hash is inconclusive rather than a failed rebuild. No rebuild required.

## NOT verified

- The Firebase console App Check page was not read this session.
- Faults 2 and 3 are Kevin-attested, not repo-verifiable.
- The true root cause of the outage. It is open.

body:
## Founder editing for startup pages

Closes the gap between what the public startup page (`/startup/[slug]`) renders and what a founder could actually set from their admin. Before this, the edit form wrote **only to localStorage** and covered 7 flat fields; the rich `details` JSONB that drives most of the page had no writer, and two cards (Documents, Social) were hardcoded on every page.

After this PR, **every field the public page renders is founder-controlled**, persisted to Supabase, with an instant local-store preview.

## Phases

| Phase | Scope |
|---|---|
| **1** | Wire the edit form to Supabase (base columns) + real logo upload to Storage |
| **2** | Team, Services, Funding editors → `details` JSONB |
| **3** | Updates, Open Roles, Stats, Traction |
| **4** | Reviews, Documents (data-driven), Social profiles (data-driven) |
| **5** | Founded year, Team size, Business type |

### Phase 1 — persistence + logo upload
- Edit form now persists `name, tagline, about, website, city, topics` to Supabase via `persistStartup` (drop-empty, so re-saving never blanks fields set elsewhere).
- Real **logo upload** → `startup-assets` Storage bucket → public URL, with preview / remove / 2 MB image guard. URL box kept as manual fallback.
- Rehydrate round-trips `tagline` + `industry` (were dropped on a fresh browser).

### Phase 2 — team / services / funding
- New **Edit content** editor (`/dashboard/startup/content`): repeatable Team + Services rows, Funding block.
- `persistStartupDetails` merges into `details` so editing one section never drops another. Local store mirrors it for instant own-page preview.

### Phase 3 — updates / roles / stats / traction
- Added Recent Updates, Open Roles, Stats, and a Traction growth chart (numeric points).
- Repeated row markup collapsed into one generic `RowList`.
- Links dropped — nothing renders them. Template fix: the updates engagement line hides when zero.

### Phase 4 — reviews / documents / socials
- Reviews editor (client, company, rating, quote, optional video).
- **Documents** card is now data-driven from `details.documents` (was a hardcoded 5-item list), hidden when empty.
- **Social Presence** is now data-driven from `details.socials` (was five dead `href=\"#\"` links on every page); each icon renders only when its URL is set.

### Phase 5 — founded / team size / business type
- Founded year + Team size → base columns (`founded_year`, `team_size`).
- Business type → `details.overview.type`; `overview` is **deep-merged** in both mappers so it never wipes base facts (founded / HQ / website).
- Sign-in rehydrate now also restores the `details` JSONB, so a returning user's content editor prefills.

## Design notes
- Editors collect **only fields the public template renders** — no invisible inputs that silently drop on save.
- Cover image intentionally skipped: `coverImage`/`bannerClass` aren't rendered on the startup company page.
- Both persist and upload **no-op safely** when Supabase env is absent, so the local mock flow still works.

## Migrations / SQL to run
Two are needed on the Supabase project (idempotent):

\`\`\`sql
-- Phase 1: logo/image storage bucket + owner-folder RLS
-- (full policy set in supabase/migrations/20260731000000_startup_assets_bucket.sql)

-- Phase 2: ensure the details JSONB column exists (init shipped it as \`rich\`)
alter table public.startups add column if not exists details jsonb not null default '{}';
\`\`\`

The bucket migration is in `supabase/migrations/20260731000000_startup_assets_bucket.sql`; run its SQL in the Supabase SQL editor.

## Verification
`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean. Each phase verified in-browser end-to-end (editor → local store → public `/startup/[slug]` render). The one pre-existing ESLint error (`studio-enquiry.tsx`, set-state-in-effect) is unrelated and untouched.

author: khanshifaul
body:
## Summary

This PR sets up the @srcroot/ui project for proper continuous delivery. It adds a 12th design theme (Twenty CRM's tokens), makes the CLI fail loudly when peer dependencies are missing, and wires up GitHub Actions with release-please for automatic version bumps.

## What's in here

### New theme: \`twenty\`

- \`src/registry/themes/v3/twenty.css\` (Tailwind 3, bare HSL triplets)
- \`src/registry/themes/v4/twenty.css\` (Tailwind 4, \`hsl()\`-wrapped + \`@theme inline\` block)
- Derived from twenty-ui's THEME_LIGHT / THEME_DARK token tables
- Source values were authored in \`color(display-p3 ...)\` and converted P3 -> sRGB -> HSL programmatically
- Neutral grays, inverted primary (near-black on light, near-white on dark), indigo-blue accent, 8px radii
- Registered in ThemeService.THEME_METADATA so \`srcroot-ui init --theme twenty\` works end-to-end

### Peer-dep warnings on init/add

Previously the CLI silently swallowed install failures. Now:

- \`add\` prints "Peer dependencies required by the selected components:" with the install command before attempting install, and a second time on failure
- \`add\` exits 1 on install failure; \`--yes\` skips the confirmation prompt but still aborts
- \`init\` uses \`stdio: \"inherit\"\` so install output is visible, exits 1 on failure with the manual install command

### CI/CD pipeline

- \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` — runs \`pnpm typecheck && pnpm build\` + smoke tests on every PR and tag push. Concurrency-cancelled per ref.
- \`ci.yml#publish\` — runs on \`v*\` tag push. Verifies tag matches \`package.json#version\`, then \`pnpm publish --provenance --access public\`. Needs \`NPM_TOKEN\` secret.
- \`.github/workflows/release-please.yml\` + \`release-please-config.json\` — on every push to main, opens/updates a Release PR with conventional-commits-driven version bump. Needs \`RELEASE_TOKEN\` PAT.

## Required secrets

- \`NPM_TOKEN\` — npm automation token (publish)
- \`RELEASE_TOKEN\` — PAT with \`contents: write\` + \`pull-requests: write\` (release-please). \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` won't work for this; PAT is required for the tag->publish chain.

## Verification done locally

- pnpm install (210 packages, exit 0)
- tsc --noEmit exit 0
- tsup build -> 42.60 KB dist
- \`node dist/index.js init --theme twenty\` writes the twenty theme to globals.css
- \`add chart --yes\` with bad install -> exits 1, prints \`npm install recharts\` twice
- \`init --yes --theme twenty\` in TW4 project -> applies theme, fails loud on npm error
- Both workflow YAML files parse, release-please-config.json validates as JSON

## What's intentionally NOT here

- No registry type-check in CI — registry files use \`@/lib/utils\` and \`@/components/ui/*\` aliases that only resolve in consumer projects
- No CHANGELOG.md checked in — release-please generates the first one with the next Release PR
- No .d.ts for registry components — consumers own their copies

author: shreypaharia
body:
Release PR: `next` -> `main` (fast-forward; `main` has no commits `next` lacks).

## Highlights

- **workers rename** — `agents` -> `workers` (per-task tmux worker) and
  `agent_configs` -> `agents` (persistent conductor agent). Forward-only DB
  migration; back up `~/.octomux/data/tasks.db` before upgrading.
- **configurable schedules** — dialog-based creation with a frequency + time
  trigger builder, per-schedule model/timeout/prompt overrides, route
  validation and an effective-prompt endpoint.
- **plugin-only skills + JSON kind presets** with a UI-editable config surface.
- **slack-watcher** rolling open-set digest with one-tap-copyable replies.
- **reviews** — no more permanently-stuck `reviewing` runs or misleading inbox state.
- **perf** — task-creation latency sweep.
- **OIDC trusted publishing** replaces the decommissioned npm tokens (see below).

## Publishing changed — read before tagging

The npm automation tokens were decommissioned, so `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is gone from
`publish.yml` and `build-binaries.yml`. Auth is now npm **trusted publishing**:
GitHub Actions mints a short-lived OIDC token that npm exchanges against a
trusted publisher registered on each package.

**This must be configured on npmjs.com before the `v1.3.0` tag is pushed, or the
publish job 401s.** Per package -> Settings -> Publishing access -> GitHub Actions:

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| Organization or user | `ShreyPaharia` |
| Repository | `octomux` |
| Workflow filename | `publish.yml` (root) / `build-binaries.yml` (tmux packages) |

Packages needing it: `octomux`, `@octomux/tmux-linux-x64`, `@octomux/tmux-darwin-arm64`.

`@octomux/tmux-linux-arm64` and `@octomux/tmux-darwin-x64` have never been
published so they have no settings page — they already fail to publish today.
`npm trust` (npm >= 11.10.0) can register a publisher without a placeholder publish.

## Release steps

1. Configure the trusted publishers above.
2. Merge this PR.
3. `git tag -a v1.3.0 -m "octomux 1.3.0 — ..." && git push origin v1.3.0 --no-verify`

author: danverimbue
body:
## Summary

Replaces per-group pytest discovery (N separate `pytest --collect-only` runs) with a **single collection pass** partitioned per group by a bundled pytest plugin. This preserves each group's exact test selection while collapsing N collections into one.

Linear: [OFFLOAD-5](https://linear.app/imbue/issue/OFFLOAD-5/single-pass-test-discovery-partitioned-per-group)

## How it works

Each group filter is a sequence of narrowing set-intersections (`-k`, `-m`, `--deselect`, `--ignore`, `--ignore-glob`). Because intersection is associative/commutative, collecting once with the components common to every group hoisted, then post-filtering each group with its full filter set, yields identical items.

- **`src/framework/pytest_filter.rs`** — parses each group's filters into typed components (`Mark`/`Keyword`/`Deselect`/`Ignore`/`IgnoreGlob`/`Unknown`) and computes exact-value common-component hoisting.
- **`scripts/offload_partition.py`** — a thin bundled plugin that partitions the collected items per group by delegating to pytest's own `Expression`/`KeywordMatcher`/`MarkMatcher`, verbatim `--deselect` prefix matching, and `pytest_ignore_collect`-equivalent path/glob checks. It only evaluates filters and writes `{groups: {name: [nodeids]}}` JSON — no decision logic.
- **`src/framework/pytest.rs` / `pytest_single_pass.rs`** — wire it into `discover_all_tests`: groups with unsupported tokens fall back to legacy per-group collection (with a warning); the rest form a single-pass pool collected once (`--collect-only -q <hoisted> -p offload_partition`, config via a temp file). Any partition-path failure falls back to legacy per-group collection, so the run never fails where the old path would have succeeded. Non-pytest frameworks are untouched.

## Correctness

- **Parity is the acceptance criterion.** `tests/offload_discovery_parity.rs` runs BOTH paths (legacy per-group `discover` vs single-pass `discover_all_groups`) against `examples/tests` across `-m`, `-k`, `-m`+`-k`, `--deselect`, `--ignore` (subdir), `--ignore-glob`, empty filters, common-filter hoisting, and an unsupported-token fallback, asserting byte-identical sorted per-group IDs.
- Hoisting normalizes each pool group's `-m`/`-k` to pytest's last-wins semantics first, so a common-but-non-last mark/keyword can never pre-narrow the shared collection.
- `tests/offload_partition_plugin.rs` exercises the plugin directly against real pytest and pins its partition output.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run` (**406 passed, 0 skipped, ~11s**), and `ratchets check` all pass. Rebased onto current `main`; integrates cleanly with main's `env`/`prepend_path`/`discovery_args` discovery refactor (legacy `discover` behavior unchanged).

## Known follow-up

- **code-ksar (P2):** the single-pass `collect_pool` path does not yet apply `env`/`prepend_path`/`discovery_args` (the legacy path does). Narrow blast radius — no committed `offload-pytest-*.toml` sets those fields, and single-pass collection failures fall back to legacy per-group discovery. Tracked for a follow-up that also adds a parity scenario covering those fields.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Azure async handler turned task cancellation into a 500
- Cancelled calls kept running and hit Router fallbacks
- Cancellations counted as Azure deployment failures (cooldowns)

How it solves it:

- Re-raise `asyncio.CancelledError` instead of `AzureOpenAIError(500)`
- Keeps the existing post_call logging for observability
- Adds a regression test that fails without the fix

## Relevant issues

Fixes #35329

## Linear ticket

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

`asyncio.CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so swallowing it and raising a provider 500 makes the cancellation invisible: Python delivers cancellation once, and once the handler consumes it the coroutine keeps running. With a Router fallback configured, the abandoned request happily completes on the fallback deployment and the caller is billed for a completion it explicitly cancelled

Repro used here: an Azure deployment pointed at a socket that accepts the request and never answers (so the request is genuinely in flight when it gets cancelled), with a real Anthropic deployment as the fallback. No mocks; the fallback leg is a real, billed `claude-sonnet-4-5` call. Azure only needs to be slow for this, not reachable; the bug is in the exception handler, not in the response path

```python
router = litellm.Router(
    model_list=[
        {"model_name": "primary", "litellm_params": {"model": "azure/dep", "api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:8124", ...}},
```

author: avifenesh
body:
Closes #1277.

The issue reported one bug and a comment added a second. Investigating turned up three distinct defects.

## 1. `[[overrides]]` had no effect on any skill rule

Reproduced on Linux from the reporter's exact config, so the Windows path-matching theory in the issue was a red herring - the platform was incidental.

`SkillValidator::validate_per_file` receives a `PerFileLintConfig`, but its internal `ValidationContext` declared the field as `&'a LintConfig`. Deref coercion silently converted it at the construction site, dropping the per-file override layer before any `is_rule_enabled` call. Since `is_rule_enabled` is the *only* method that differs between the two types, this was invisible at the call sites.

Effect: every AS-* and CC-SK-* rule ignored `[[overrides]]` on all platforms, with no way to suppress one for a single file. Global `[rules].disabled_rules` was unaffected, which matches the reporter's observation that it kept working.

The field now holds the per-file view, with a comment on why it must not be widened back.

## 2. Server-only MCP form was rejected

Per the [permissions reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), `mcp__puppeteer` and `mcp__puppeteer__*` are equivalent ways to name every tool from one server. The [sub-agents reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) documents the same for `tools` and `disallowedTools`: "Both fields accept MCP server-level patterns in addition to exact tool names: `mcp__<server>` or `mcp__<server>__*`".

`is_valid_mcp_tool_format` required the second `__`, so `mcp__playwright` errored while `mcp__playwright__*` passed. Both forms are now accepted.

The reporter was right that rejecting a glob in the server segment is correct - the same doc requires a rule to name a specific configured server - so `mcp__supabase-*` and `mcp__*` still fail. Tool-segment globs (`mcp__github__get_*`) still pass.

An existing test caught a real regression here: `mcp__bad name` initially started passing as a server-only form. The server segment now also rejects whitespace.

## 3. Stale known-tools lists

`Workflow` is in the [built-in tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools) but was missing from CC-SK-008, along with `Artifact`, `ReportFindings`, `SendUserFile`, and `EndConversation`.

CC-AG-009/010's list was much further behind - 26 documented tools absent, including the `Cron*`/`Task*` families, `PowerShell`, `LSP`, `ToolSearch`, and the worktree and MCP-resource tools - so a subagent declaring any of them failed validation.

Both lists are reconciled against the docs table by diffing rather than reading release notes. One judgment call: tools subagents never receive (`AskUserQuestion`, `Workflow`, `ScheduleWakeup`, …) stay in the agent list, because the sub-agents doc says Claude Code filters those from the resolved pool rather than rejecting the name - flagging them as unknown would be wrong. That reasoning is recorded in a comment on the constant.

## Tests

- End-to-end `validate_project` regression for the override leak, with a baseline assertion so it can't pass vacuously
- Server-only MCP form accepted in `allowed-tools`, `tools`, and `disallowedTools`
- Glob in the server segment still rejected
- Newly recognized built-in tools accepted for both rule families
- Updated `test_cc_ag_009_mcp_tool_invalid_formats`, which asserted the now-valid `mcp__server` was invalid; `mcp__supabase-*` replaces it so the count still covers four genuinely invalid forms

Full suite: 5039 tests across 37 binaries, zero failures. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean. Rule bookkeeping, locale sync, and rule-count checks pass.

## Notes

- Diagnostic messages and the `es`/`zh-CN` locales: only `en` documents the MCP format, so only it changed. All four locale copies re-synced via `scripts/check-locale-sync.sh`.
- `verified_on` for the three rules advanced to 2026-07-31 with the tools and permissions references added as evidence URLs.
- `schemas/cross_platform.rs` has its own `KNOWN_TOOLS`, left alone: it feeds prose-mention detection for XP-005, not a validation gate.

author: zootimusmaximusbackup
body:
## COMPLIANCE REVIEW REQUIRED — estimates shown to a consumer

`recordReminders()` composes sentences quoting **projected** figures and **predicted** dates for a client of a regulated consumer-finance product. Two rules are enforced by tests, and both survive mutation testing, so neither can be edited out for brevity without the suite failing:

1. **Every body carrying a number says "estimated" or "projected".**
2. **No body makes any claim about a credit score or a credit outcome.**

Flagged, not blocked: this produces rows, and no row reaches a person until somebody builds a surface for it — a separate decision.

## What this does, in plain language

Works out day by day what a client's bank balance will look like over the next few weeks, and uses that to say **when to press the button** on a credit-card payment so it lands safely. It shows its working: for every day you can see exactly which bills and which incoming money produced that number.

**When it does not have enough information to be sure, it says so and gives no date.** It never guesses.

## The two ways this could cost real money, and what stops each

| Failure | What stops it |
|---|---|
| A recommended date that **overdraws** the account | Feasibility is tested on the pessimistic balance, always, and across the whole stretch from the payment date to the end — not just the payment day. A payment that leaves the account healthy on Tuesday and overdrawn on Friday is still an overdraft. |
| A refusal that pushes a card payment **late** | A bill nobody has confirmed is carried on a separate track rather than treated as certain, so the window is not tightened by money that may never leave. Every feasible date is returned, not just one. |

## The thresholds — 088

The model holds no operator number and never did. The finding was that there was **nowhere to put one**. `088_cashflow_settings.sql` creates `cashflow_settings`, following the pattern `052_config_defaults.sql` set: one file, so reverting to unconfigured is a single `git revert`, and every value carried with `signed_off_at IS NULL` so `v_cashflow_config_gaps` reports it as provisional until a human confirms it.

**These three are not equally risky, and which direction each hurts in is the whole story:**

| Threshold | Value | Basis | Which way it hurts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settlement_lead_days` | **3** | `[DERIVED]` | **Asymmetric.** Too high costs a little float. Too low costs a late payment — a fee and a credit-report mark. **Errs high on purpose.** |
| `min_buffer_cents` | **0** | `[SPEC]` | **Asymmetric the other way — the trap.** A bigger buffer sounds safer and is not: it refuses MORE payment dates, pushing the payment later, risking the same missed payment. |
| `confidence_floor` | **0.800** | `[PLACEHOLDER]` | **Cannot affect safety at all.** Both sides of the floor land in the pessimistic track `paymentWindow()` tests against. |

**Why 3 days.** A card payment pushed from a bank account is an ACH debit, and standard ACH settles on the *next banking day* — not instantly, and same-day ACH is a separate opted-into product that cannot be assumed. Three things push the realistic figure above that floor: banking days are not calendar days (a Friday start settles Monday at the earliest — three calendar days for one banking day); the issuer still has to post it against the card, a second step on its own cycle; and a payment started after cut-off is tomorrow's payment, which a module with no clock cannot detect. Three covers the Friday case, which is the common one a one- or two-day figure gets wrong.

⚠️ **This is a property of a payment rail, not a universal fact.** Paying on the issuer's own site with a debit card often posts same day; a mailed cheque takes a week. If a rail is ever wired in, re-derive from its documented timing. Carried unsigned until somebody confirms which rail this describes.

**The payoff:** the payment reminder now surfaces on the day somebody has to press the button, not the day the money must land. A reminder that arrives on the landing date arrives too late to act on. With no lead time known it falls back to the landing date and *says so plainly* rather than implying same-day posting.

## NULL means unset. It never means zero.

The single most important line in `settings.mjs`. A NULL `settlement_lead_days` reaching the model as `0` would assert that payments post same-day — a claim about payment rails that is often false and whose cost is a missed payment. So a NULL column produces an **absent key**, and an explicit zero survives as a zero. Both directions are mutation-tested.

## Nothing transmits

No `fetch`, no email, no SMS, no push anywhere in `src/banking/`. `cashflow_reminders` has no `sent_at`, no `channel`, no `status`, no retry counter, no scheduler and no activation flag. A pg test asserts the absence of all twelve of those column names, so adding one later fails the suite rather than shipping quietly.

## Proof

```
Migrations 087 + 088
  apply clean on a database that already had 50 files          PASS
  re-apply through migrate.mjs as a no-op (0 applied)          PASS
  raw SQL applied directly a 2nd and 3rd time                  PASS  no-op, no dup row
  all files apply from scratch on a virgin database            PASS

npm test, no DATABASE_URL
  full suite                           2037 tests, 0 fail, 239 skipped

npm test, against real Postgres 16
  src/banking/cashflow.test.mjs         106 tests, 106 pass, 0 fail
  src/banking/reminders.pg.test.mjs      28 tests,  28 pass, 0 fail
  src/banking/settings.pg.test.mjs       16 tests,  16 pass, 0 fail
  failing test NAMES vs the same suite with src/banking removed:
                                       BYTE-IDENTICAL (28 pre-existing, all in
                                       the creative / partner modules, none in
                                       src/banking)

Mutation testing        59 deliberate defects injected, 59 killed, 0 survived
  cashflow.mjs   37/37  both sides of every boundary, the pessimistic-track rule,
                        the blind-spot refusal, each threshold being filled in
                        with a picked number, the shortfall attribution, the
                        start-date reminder, and BOTH compliance-wording rules
  reminders.mjs  12/12  org scoping on all three reads, first-acknowledgement-wins,
                        the due-at-exactly-asOf boundary
  settings.mjs   10/10  a NULL threshold becoming a zero, an explicit zero being
                        dropped as though unset, the driver's strings passing
                        through unconverted, org scoping on both reads

npm run diagrams:check                 up to date (12 files)
```

**Zero new test failures** — verified by removing `src/banking/` and re-running the whole suite against the same database, then diffing failure *names*, not totals.

## Out of scope

Plaid calls (W5), liability ingestion (W6), recurrence detection (W7), delivery of any reminder, a scheduler, an HTTP endpoint, a UI screen (W9/W10). **No existing file outside `src/banking/` was modified.** No handler added, so `ROUTES` is untouched and `src/http/routes.test.mjs` still passes 14/14. 088 seeds only the default org; other orgs read as unset and the gaps view reports them.

## Findings

1. **RESOLVED in 088** — the thresholds now have a home and values, all carried unsigned and reported by `v_cashflow_config_gaps`.
2. **`WORKFLOW-AUTONOMY.md` does not exist** — not in the working tree, and `git log --all --diff-filter=A` finds it in no branch's history. Proceeded on the decision rules inlined in the directive.
3. **`docs/journeys/` does not exist.** CLAUDE.md §4 describes eight tracked journeys and a changelog; `docs/` contains only `diagrams/` and `workflows/`.
4. **CLAUDE.md §6's first two gates cannot run here.** No `lint` script and no eslint config; no `tsconfig.json` and no TypeScript. Both attempted. `npm test` and `npm run diagrams:check` do run and

author: scxttk
body:
Reported on 2026-07-30: system dark, app set to **Hell**, and for about a second the wrong appearance stood there before it flipped.

## The backlog's suspicion was right but incomplete

It said `overrideUserInterfaceStyle` lands after the first frame. True — but that does not explain a whole *second*.

`AppearanceWindowBridge` set the style inside a `DispatchQueue.main.async` block and bailed out with:

```swift
guard let window = view.window, window.overrideUserInterfaceStyle != style else { return }
```

On a cold start there is no window at that moment. So the block **fell through with no effect, and nobody tried again**. The style was applied on the next SwiftUI pass — that is, whenever some content happened to finish loading.

Not one late call. One that never happened, plus a coincidental one later. That is the second.

## The fix

`didMoveToWindow()` is exactly the moment a window exists — not one runloop turn later, and not on a guess. Retrying becomes unnecessary because nothing can fall through any more.

## Proven by mutation, not by assertion

Six unit tests attach a probe to a `UIWindow` and assert **immediately**, without letting the runloop turn once. That is the point: they measure the *moment*, not just the result.

Wiring the old `async` path back into the new type fails three of them:

- `testTheChoiceIsOnTheWindowTheMomentTheViewIsAttached`
- `testSystemGivesTheWindowBackToTheSystem`
- `testTheVeryFirstApplicationIsImmediateAndNotFadedIn`

So the fix is demonstrably the **timing**, not the refactor around it. A test that waited a second would only have been slow and would have proven nothing.

## What this does not fix, stated plainly

The launch screen generated by iOS (`INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation`) follows the **system** appearance, not the app setting. That cannot be changed per user — `UIUserInterfaceStyle` in Info.plist is a build-time constant, not a preference.

So a brief dark image before the first app frame may remain. What goes away is the second after it. **Worth checking on the device** — I can measure the code path but not the launch screen.

## Tests

**260 unit + 37 UI, 0 failures** (was 254 + 37).

## Note on merging

This branch, #18 and #19 all branch from `a89eab2` and all add a test file, so all three touch `ios/LeChariot.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`. Expect a conflict there on the second and third merge. Do **not** merge it by hand — the file is generated:

```
cd ios && xcodegen generate
```

body:
Implements the ctrl half of the contract frozen in #320. Closes the provider side of #311; the learn consumer half follows in its own PR (providers before consumers).

## Problem
Three event IDs cycled the same `UnknownSourceTypeRetry: Unknown source_type='unknown'` up to 20× each with no terminal classification — recurring workflow capacity burned, genuinely new failures buried, and queue-health metrics that could never converge.

## What landed
| Surface | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `stream_event` | `+failure_count`, `+last_error`, `+dead_lettered_at`, `+dead_letter_reason`; `INGEST_FAILURE_BUDGET = 5` |
| `POST /events/:id/failure` | `non_retryable` dead-letters immediately; `retryable` dead-letters at budget. Re-reporting an already-dead-lettered event is an idempotent no-op, not an escalation |
| `GET /events/dead-letter` | operator-visible poison queue with reason, failure_count, provenance |
| `POST /events/:id/requeue` | clears terminal state; idempotent |
| `GET /events/pending` | excludes dead-lettered rows; reports `pending` and `dead_lettered` counts separately |

## The part worth reviewing
**The column retrofit, not the routes.** `ingest-schema.sql` is CREATE-only-idempotent and ingest.db has **no migration runner** (unlike state.db). Without a guarded `ALTER TABLE` at open time, every already-provisioned tenant would open a `stream_event` lacking all four columns and 500 on the first pending-feed query — simultaneously, fleet-wide. The schema file is updated too, so fresh tenants get the columns at CREATE.

Also: `GET /events/dead-letter` is registered **before** `/events/:id`, or the router reads `"dead-letter"` as an event id.

## Smoke evidence

`tsx` is not installed locally, so the TS test harness cannot run here (CI runs it). I validated the risky retrofit path standalone against `node:sqlite`, seeding a **pre-#311 tenant database** and opening it twice:

```
$ node --experimental-sqlite retrofit_check.mjs
  pass 1: columns present, legacy row intact, failure_count backfilled to 0
  pass 2: columns present, legacy row intact, failure_count backfilled to 0
  pending feed excludes poison; counts pending=1 dead_lettered=1
ALL RETROFIT CHECKS PASSED
```

That covers: the ALTER fires on a legacy table, it is idempotent across reopens (a second ALTER would throw), the in-flight row survives, `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` backfills `failure_count` (otherwise every count read is NaN), and the pending predicate parks poison while still counting it.

Deployed-tenant confirmation that the new routes are genuinely additive — on home, running the **pre-merge** ctrl-api build:
```
GET /api/v1/ingest/events/dead-letter -> 404      (route does not exist yet)
/matters -> 200  /decisions -> 200  /vault/index -> 200  /settings -> 200
ctrl-api errors since restart: 0
```

`tests/ingest-dead-letter.test.ts` pins the same behaviour in the CI harness.
