## Summary

- Replace authoritative directory-keyed workspace customization with a recovery journal keyed by `Workspace.stableId`.
- Keep each session snapshot as the per-workspace baseline while preserving title and color mutations made before the next autosave, including explicit clears.
- Treat `workspaceDirectoryCustomizations.v1` as migration-only. Promote a legacy directory record only when exactly one restored workspace owns that directory, then remove ambiguous and orphaned legacy data.
- Cover both full-session restore and closed-workspace history restore with same-directory title and color behavior tests.

## Regression provenance

Version `0.64.20` predates this regression. https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/8841 introduced the directory-keyed record in commit `f5af960e01` and made it authoritative on restore in commit `25a1ed8ba4`. https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/9027 later stopped applying the record to fresh workspaces but retained the colliding write and restore paths.

## Verification

- Commit `69087f964e` adds the failing same-directory restore regressions first.
- Commit `9f586e4574` adds the stable-ID implementation and migration coverage separately.
- The tagged cloud Debug build passed and launched from merged HEAD `d47c1fe0c0`.
- `./scripts/lint-pbxproj-test-wiring.sh`
- `./scripts/check-pbxproj.sh`
- `python3 scripts/check-workspace-package-groups.py --check`
- `python3 scripts/check-package-resolved-policy.py`
- `git diff --check`
- No local `xcodebuild` tests or XCUITests were run. CI is the test execution gate.
- Current `origin/main` does not contain `.github/swift-file-length-budget.tsv` or `scripts/swift_file_length_budget.py`. Every new Swift file is under 500 lines, and neither budget TSV is changed.

Closes https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/issues/9267

author: bowenliang123
body:
## Related Issue

No linked issue — the problem is explained below.

## Problem

The web UI's static assets (served by kap-server's web-assets routes) are sent with only `Content-Type` and `Content-Length` — no `Cache-Control`, no `ETag`, no `Last-Modified`. Browsers therefore receive no caching guidance at all and fall back to per-browser heuristic caching, so repeat visits to `kimi web` re-download JS/CSS bundles unnecessarily (or behave inconsistently across browsers).

## What changed

One focused change in `packages/kap-server/src/routes/webAssets.ts`: `serveWebAsset` now stamps a `Cache-Control` header based on the file's location relative to the assets root:

- **`assets/` files** (Vite's content-hashed build output, e.g. `index-abc123.js`) → `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Content changes produce a new filename/URL, so caching them for a year is safe. This is the actual win: repeat visits load JS/CSS/fonts straight from disk cache with zero network requests, including on manual refresh (`immutable`).
- **Everything else** (`index.html`, SPA fallback responses, favicon, ...) → `Cache-Control: no-cache`. The entry document must be revalidated every load so a new release is picked up immediately and starts referencing the new hashed assets.

This is the standard "entry no-cache + hashed assets immutable" deployment pattern; the distinction is trivially reliable here because Vite always emits hashed files under `dist/assets/`.

## Measured benefit

Built the real web UI (`apps/kimi-web` → dist) and served it through this route twice — once with the old code, once with the new — in a real Chrome instance, measuring transferred bytes via the Resource Timing API:

| | cold load | refresh (warm) |
|---|---|---|
| before | 2.03 MB | **2.03 MB** — every byte re-downloaded, nothing cached |
| after | 2.03 MB | **20.8 KB** — main bundle (1.53 MB), CSS (360 KB), and fonts (114 KB) all served from disk cache with zero requests |

So each repeat visit / refresh saves ~2 MB of transfer (~99% reduction; larger over the wire than these uncompressed localhost numbers since the same applies to gzipped bodies). Load time on localhost is dominated by other factors, but on any real network the difference is proportionally larger.

The remaining ~20 KB on warm loads is the `index.html` revalidation plus the root-level `favicon.ico` (17 KB, intentionally `no-cache`); adding ETag/304 support for root files could shrink that further but is out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] I have linked a related issue, or explained the problem above.
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my feature works.
- [x] Ran `gen-changesets` skill, or this PR needs no changeset.
- [x] Ran `gen-docs` skill, or this PR needs no doc update.

author: logbie
body: ## Summary Fixes issue #671: the analyzer failed to report mutations of constants via `add ... to`, `remove ... from`, and `clear` statements. These statements parse to `AddToListStatement`, `RemoveFromListStatement`, and `ClearListStatement` (not `Assignment`), and the analyzer never checked their targets for constness. A program mutating a constant five ways (via `change`, `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`) received only four error reports. ## Key Changes - **Analyzer constant tracking** (`src/analyzer/mod.rs`): - Added `constant_bindings: HashSet` to track symbols declared with `store new constant`. This is deliberately *not* the `mutable: false` flag, which is overloaded — action parameters, container-method parameters, loop variables, `try`/`when` error bindings, predefined globals, and REPL parent-scope variables are all immutable without being constants. Keyed by binding rather than by name so an inner-scope shadow is not mistaken for the constant. - Populate the set in `VariableDeclaration` when `is_constant` is true. - Added `report_constant_mutation()` to check bare-name mutation targets against the set and emit the same message as the assignment path, applied to the `AddToListStatement`, `RemoveFromListStatement`, and `ClearListStatement` arms. - Carry the marker across scope merges: a constant declared on both arms of a `check` is re-defined into the parent scope under a new binding key, so `promote_constant_marker` moves the marker with it. Without this, `change` still reported while `add`/`remove`/`clear` went silent — #671 again, one scope up. - Guard against over-reporting: parameters, loop variables, and container members remain unaffected, with negative tests for each. - **Documentation** (`Docs/03-language-basics/variables-and-types.md`, `Docs/06-best-practices/naming-conventions.md`): - Replaced the stale "true constants are planned for future versions" text with the real `store new constant` syntax. - Enumerated the mutation forms that are actually rejected, with an explicit known-gap callout for `push with and ` (#673) and a note that a constant fixes the binding, not the contents reached through an alias. Both were flagged in review as overclaims and corrected. - **Tests** (`tests/constant_mutation_analyzer_test.rs`, `tests/diagnostics_fixtures_test.rs`): - Nine tests: single `add` rejection, all five mutation forms, list mutations, branch-merge promotion (scalar and list), and negative assertions for parameters, loop variables, and container members. - `constant_mutation_is_rejected_for_every_mutation_form` landed with #672 pinning `>= 4` reports and a comment pointing at #671; with the gap closed it is now an exact `== 5`. - **Documentation examples** (`TestPrograms/docs_examples/basic_syntax/`): - `constants_01.wfl` (executable) and `constants_immutable_01.wfl` (error example, carries the `// CI-SKIP:` directive the CI sweep requires). Both registered in the manifest and validated. - **Dev Diary** (`History/dev-diary/2026/2026-07-31-issue-671-constant-mutation-reports.md`). ## Compatibility No shipped program mutates a constant. The one genuine behavior change is constant *lists*: `add`/`remove`/`clear` on one previously succeeded silently at runtime — the interpreter mutates the `Rc>>` in place, so `Environment::assign`'s constant check was never reached — and is now rejected at analysis time. That is the documented meaning of `constant`, and no shipped example relied on it. **Risk class: R3.** An earlier revision said R1 on the grounds that this only adds a front-end diagnostic; that was wrong. `testing.md` §5 places backward compatibility in R3 outright and forbids lowering the class, and the constant-list change above is a backward-compatibility change. §11.3 does not apply — no concurrency, cancellation, lifecycle, streaming, untrusted input, or crypto. The applicable evidence is failure-path and negative coverage, listed in the dev diary. ## Testing Figures are for the current head, after merging `main` twice — #672 (Repository Hygiene and Layout Policy) and then #675 (its CI follow-ups). - Red→Green TDD: `constant_mutation_analyzer_test.rs` added as a test-only Red commit (`1be7188`, ancestor of the Green `29c9ddf`). - `cargo test --all --no-fail-fast` — 151 test binaries, 0 failures. - `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. - CI program sweep over `TestPrograms/` against the release binary — 142 passed, 0 failed, 49 skipped. - `python scripts/validate_docs_examples.py --force` — 21/21. - `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/tooling` — 33 passed; hygiene static and working-tree both exit 0. CI is green on `ed3b36d`: 17 checks passed, 1 correctly skipped (`Bump Version` does not run on PRs). ## Note on scope Intermediate revisions of this branch also carried CI repairs (Windows `setup-python`, the extension lockfile version, and archive-manifest CRLF drift). #675 landed equivalent fixes on main while this was open, so the merge dropped all of them in favour of what is already merged — including removing the `.gitattributes` approach this branch used, since main instead hashes the staged blob in the checker. The diff is analyzer-only again. ## Follow-up filed #673 — `push with CONST and value` still mutates a constant list. `PushStatement` carries its target as an `Expression` rather than a bare name, so the check added here has nothing to resolve; fixing it needs write-target resolution through expressions. https://claude.ai/code/session_01H9AnrAH4d8sTni73GWgkjR --- ``<img src="https://static.devin.ai/assets/gh-open-in-devin-review-light.svg?v=1" alt="Open in Devin Review">`` ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Constants now prevent reassignment and `add`, `remove`, and `clear` mutations across supported scopes, including conditional branches. * Added examples demonstrating constant declarations, usage, and invalid mutation attempts. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved diagnostics when attempting to modify constants. * **Documentation** * Expanded guidance on constant behavior, naming conventions, and list-content considerations. * **Chores** * Improved repository hygiene checks and cross-platform test consistency.

body:
Three entries in `docs/PROGRESS.md` still read "landed, unmerged" for branches that
merged tonight — #53, #54 and #58. Each PR carried its own in-flight claim through the
squash, so the claim outlived the work.

That list is the claim registry. `CLAUDE.md` sends every session to it before touching
code, precisely so two sessions don't collide on one branch — a stale claim tells the
next reader a merged branch is still live, which is the one failure mode it exists to
prevent.

**Kept, because it outlives the entry that carried it:** every "quota is the binding
constraint" figure in the file describes the pre-2026-07-30 system, since the passes that
produced those figures were spending nothing at all. That is now its own note, with the
residual the review measured (`--score-limit` is still not a pure quota budget: an LLM
screen-discard and a thin-JD row each consume a slot while spending nothing), and it
stands until the first normal pass on the fixed code re-measures it.

Docs only.

author: code-yeongyu
body: ## Summary The `Check and test` CI job's Test step took **25.5 min** (coding-agent suite: 1364s, of which **818s was per-file module import** — the single biggest cost). This PR is the measured fix: run the CI vitest pool on **two forks instead of one**, and unflake the MCP idle renewal test that contributed to the original single-fork workaround. Expected Test-step wall time drops to roughly half. ## Changes - **`packages/coding-agent/vitest.config.ts`** — under `CI`, `maxWorkers: 1` → `2` (forks pool kept). Two forks keeps the subprocess-heavy suites isolated in separate processes (no shared-event-loop contention, bounded CPU/IO on the 4-vCPU runner) while halving the re-import wall. The config comment documents the measurement. - **`packages/coding-agent/test/mcp/idle.test.ts`** — renewal test `idleTimeoutMin: 0.001` → `0.02`, matching sibling tests whose comments already document 0.001 (60ms) as known-bad on loaded runners (the idle timer could fire before the renewal was observed). ## QA & Evidence - **Measured bottleneck (before):** CI run 30604890958 — Test step 25.5min; coding-agent `Duration 1364.23s (import 817.87s, tests 449.41s)`. Local parallel (no `CI`) full suite: `real 2m52.6s`. - **Renewal test determinism:** `vitest run test/mcp/idle.test.ts -t "keeps the idle timer paused"` ×10 → **10/10 PASS**. - **Whole idle suite:** `test/mcp/idle.test.ts` 7/7 passed after the fix. - **CI proof (this PR):** the `Check and test` run on this branch is the acceptance evidence — Test step should be well under 12 min (from 25.5). ## Risks & Residuals - **Reintroducing the historical fork-pool hang:** mitigated by keeping the `forks` pool (not default pool), `maxWorkers: 2` (not unbounded), `teardownTimeout` retained, and this PR's own CI run as the live proof. If a hang reappears, the revert is a one-line change back to `1`. - **Local release parity:** `scripts/release.mjs` runs its gate with `CI=1`, so it picks up the same two-fork behavior; PR #2 (release gate skip) builds on this. ## Related Second PR in this series: skip the duplicated local release test gate when HEAD already carries a green `Check and test` CI run. --- ## Summary by cubic Speed up CI `vitest` by running two forked workers instead of one, and deflake the MCP idle renewal test. Test step time should drop from ~25.5 min to well under 12 min. - **Performance** - In CI, run `vitest` with `pool: "forks"` and `maxWorkers: 2` to cut per-file re-import cost while keeping subprocess isolation; `teardownTimeout` unchanged. - Applies to CI and the local release gate (`CI=1`); plain local `npm test` stays with the default pool. - **Bug Fixes** - MCP idle renewal test: increase `idleTimeoutMin` from 0.001 to 0.02 so the idle timer doesn’t fire before the renewal is observed on loaded runners. Written for commit 1e11304cff81b37a1ebbc3ebe825a803165e38af. Summary will update on new commits.

author: antoinedc
body:
## BET-422 — Spacing-scale trim + off-grid rounding

Split from BET-407 step 5. PM sign-off confirmed: 11-step scale locked, zero-visual-diff constraint relaxed (review for intended rounding only, no catastrophic collapses).

### What changed

**Tailwind config** (`tailwind.config.js`):
- `theme.spacing` **replaced** (not extended) with the 11-step scale: `0, px, 1(4px), 2(8px), 3(12px), 4(16px), 5(20px), 6(24px), 8(32px), 10(40px), 12(48px)`.
- `theme.width`, `theme.height`, `theme.minHeight`, `theme.maxHeight` **decoupled** from `theme.spacing` and set to the full default Tailwind scale (+ `full`/`screen`/`min`/`max` for min/max-height). This preserves every dimension utility in use: `w-64`, `w-48`, `w-16`, `h-64`, `h-52`, `h-40`, `h-32`, `max-h-32`, `max-h-64`, etc.
- `colors`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize` stay in `theme.extend` (unchanged behaviour).

**Off-grid migration** — every pure-spacing utility (`p*`, `m*`, `gap*`, `space-*`, `inset*`) with an off-grid value rounded to the nearest step:

| Off-grid value | Pixels | → Nearest step | Pixels |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.5` | 2px | `px` | 1px |
| `1.5` | 6px | `2` | 8px |
| `2.5` | 10px | `3` | 12px |
| `3.5` | 14px | `4` | 16px |
| `7` | 28px | `8` | 32px |

(`9` and `11` were not used in any spacing utility.)

Tie-breaking: half-values equidistant between two steps round **up** (to the larger step), except `0.5` (2px) which is genuinely closer to `px` (1px, diff 1) than to `1` (4px, diff 2).

**31 `.tsx`/`.ts` source files** updated (5 under `src/renderer/mobile/`), plus `mobile.css` (stale `py-0.5` comment → `py-px`) and `tailwind.config.js` (spacing scale + dimension decoupling) = **33 files total**.

**Dimension utilities with off-grid values are deliberately preserved** — `w-1.5`, `w-3.5`, `h-0.5`, `h-1.5`, `h-2.5`, `h-3.5`, `w-7`, `h-7`, `w-9`, `h-9`, etc. are NOT migrated because width/height are decoupled from the trimmed spacing scale.

### Changed files

33 files changed, 250 insertions(+), 175 deletions(-):
- `tailwind.config.js` — spacing scale + dimension decoupling
- 31 `src/renderer/**/*.{tsx,ts}` files — off-grid spacing rounded
- `src/renderer/mobile/mobile.css` — stale comment fix

### Verification results

- **PR branch** (`multica/BET-422-spacing-trim` @ `102a2dc`):
  - typecheck: exit 0. Errors: none. log sha256: `00a5b657…`
  - test: exit 0, 1200 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip. log sha256: `3a3c22e2…`
- **Base** (`main` @ `5043faf`):
  - typecheck: exit 0. Errors: none. log sha256: `00a5b657…` (identical)
  - test: exit 0, 1200 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip. log sha256: `2d24c497…`
- **Conclusion:** 0 new failures, 0 pre-existing failures. Both branches green.

Logs cached at `/tmp/typecheck-pr.log`, `/tmp/typecheck-main.log`, `/tmp/test-pr.log`, `/tmp/test-main.log`.

### Grep confirmation

No off-grid spacing utility remains in `src/renderer/`:
```
$ grep -rEno '\b(p|px|py|...|gap|space-y|inset)-(...)-(0\.5|1\.5|2\.5|3\.5|7|9|11)\b' src/renderer/
(no output)
```

Base: origin/main @ 5043faf



### Duplication-gate note (advisory, not required)

The `duplication-gate` CI check flagged 3 clones in changed files (ContextBar.tsx ↔ SessionHeader.tsx, PairStep.tsx ↔ mobile/SetupScreen.tsx). These are **pre-existing structural patterns** — every diff line in these 4 files is pure className rounding (`gap-1.5`→`gap-2`, `py-0.5`→`py-px`, `mb-1.5`→`mb-2`, etc.), no new structural duplication was introduced by this PR.

author: andrewboudreau
body:
Stacked on #2. Retarget to `master` as the stack merges.

`readable.py` counted `unk_<offset>` anywhere in a file, but counted a real name only after `->` or `.`. A promoted method uses implicit `this`, so:

```cpp
mAngleY = mPrevAngleY;      // two invisible references
unk_08e = unk_094;          // the same two, counted
```

Naming a field could therefore **shrink the reported total**. That is exactly what happened in #1: named went 674 → 758, but the denominator fell 6,331 → 6,121, because 210 references left the count entirely instead of moving from one column to the other. That is what surfaced the bug.

3,492 bare member references in `folded/` were never being seen. The asymmetry penalised precisely the most readable form in the tree — a real C++ method with named fields and no explicit `self->` — and flattered the least readable one.

## The fix

The two patterns are symmetric now. `\w{2,}` after the capital keeps single-letter locals like `mF` (14 occurrences, all local declarations) out; no name in `mined/names_*.json` is shorter than four characters, so nothing real is excluded.

## Corrected figures

**No file in any tree changed.** Only the counter did.

| | parent `src/` | `source/` | `folded/` |
|---|---|---|---|
| raw offset | 99.9% | 12.0% | 47.5% |
| `unk_<offset>` | 0.0% | 49.2% | 29.4% |
| named | 0.1% → was 0% | **38.7%** → was 36% | **23.1%** → was 4.5% |

Named share of the fields that have a member form at all: **10.6% → 44.0%** (4,216 of 9,579) in `folded/`.

The README and HANDOFF both say plainly that this is a measurement fix and not progress — the 5,363 references that still read `unk_<offset>` are unchanged, and field naming is still the biggest gap in the tree.

author: bobert600
body:
## What

An organisation's owner is now recorded **inside the event that creates its identity**, and adoption founds an organisation directly rather than creating one and giving it an owner afterwards.

Implements ADR-032 (included), which supersedes the central decision of ADR-030.

## Why it matters

An organisation has no mind. It can't decide, consent, or answer for anything — and in law that isn't a technicality, it's why a company needs a person behind it. Companies don't spontaneously come into being.

So an organisation's identity **can't be self-owned**. If the software running one holds the only key to it, the organisation owns itself and there's nobody it ultimately answers to. That isn't an organisation; it's an unattended key.

The implementation had drifted into exactly that — identity created first, owner recorded afterwards in a file. Three consequences, all reachable:

| | |
|---|---|
| **A window with no owner** | nothing required the second step to ever happen, and an unowned organisation was *indistinguishable* from one that deliberately owned itself |
| **Ownership could be silently replaced** | a file can be overwritten. The first owner was left listed as an administrator with no cryptographic standing — a name in a table |
| **Ownership was invisible** | nobody outside that machine could verify who owned an organisation |

## The fix

The owner goes in the inception event's own seal field. A self-addressing identifier is the digest of that event, so **the owner is part of what the identity is**.

Proven rather than asserted, against real keripy:

- same keys, **different owner → different identifier**
- same keys, **owner removed → different identifier**
- same keys, same owner → same identifier (derivation stays deterministic)

So ownership can't be added, removed or altered afterwards without producing a different organisation.

## Adoption founds it

Two ways to be adopted, and which is right depends on whether the thing can ever change hands.

**A person's agent is delegated.** Its delegator is named inside its own inception — right for a relationship permanent by nature. Your computer doesn't stop being yours.

**An organisation is not.** A delegation cannot be transferred, only destroyed, so a delegated company could never be sold without killing its identity and every credential and relationship it ever had. It incepts its own identity and names its owner in that event, so ownership changes by rotation and the company survives its owner.

The owner is required, and the refusal happens **before anything is created** — otherwise an organisation answering to itself is reachable again through the front door.

## The organisation keeps its own key

This is what separates the decision from ADR-030's *"an organisation IS its owners' key set"*. An organisation built that way can't act without them — it can't hold a relationship, serve discovery, or keep its own address current, because each of those is a signature.

Here the organisation does its own day-to-day work. What the owner controls is **the identity itself**.

## Reading is strict in two directions

- **Only the inception is consulted.** A later event can't introduce an owner where there was none, nor replace one — either would put back the silent overwrite this removes.
- **An owner seal naming nobody is an error, not an absence.** A broken organisation and an unowned one need different answers.

An identity with **no** owner seal stays valid: a person's agent is a delegated identity whose delegator is already named in the event.

`ownerAuthority()` now consults the log before falling back, and **refuses** if an identity names an owner it can't resolve — falling through there would mean an organisation whose owner is unresolvable quietly starts answering to itself.

## Notes

ADR-030 is marked superseded-in-part, with a note on which of its decisions still stand and are implemented.

The founding-ceremony commit sits on this branch rather than a second pull request: it calls `CreateOwnedInception`, which only exists here. Stacking a second review on an unlanded first is how a chain of PRs gets orphaned when the base branch is deleted.

16 tests (6 driver, 10 Go). `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` clean; all driver suites pass.

## Decision provenance

**Decision ID(s):** `N/A`

**Why N/A is safe:**

This changes only how approved parchment artwork is extracted and rendered behind card content. It does not alter card identities, canonical text, deck legality, faction colors, or artwork assignments.

**Approved direction:**

All seven grid panels were loading, but the browser was scaling and positioning the entire 3 × 3 grid on every card. - applies source-specific contrast normalization around each panel's own average paper color;
- leaves Inquisition unadjusted and keeps Neutral deliberately restrained;
- preserves full opacity, original paper coloration, and the plain parchment fallback behavior;
- adds regression coverage and updates the rendering documentation.

author: robbes
body:
Answering **"did anything change on e2e?"** — no, nothing broke. **And that is itself the finding.**

## What e2e actually touches

I enumerated it rather than assuming:

```
${BASE_URL}/status          ${BASE_URL}/deletions   ${BASE_URL}/healthz
${BASE_URL}/verify          ${BASE_URL}/moves       ${BASE_URL}/failures
${BASE_URL}/mappings/{id}/run
${BASE_URL}/mappings/{id}/deletions/{hash}/apply
${BASE_URL}/mappings/{id}/failures/{hash}/accept
${BASE_URL}/mappings/{id}/moves/{hash}/keep
```

**It never calls `GET /` or `POST /mappings/{id}/start`** — its fixtures arrive already active. Those are the first two things a real user touches, and both changed under ADR-0026:

- `/` went from rendering HTML to redirecting to `/ui/confirm`
- `start` went from `303 See Other` to JSON

Both deliberate, neither broke anything — but **nothing was watching either**. `/status` gaining `migrationStatus` was additive, and the queue bodies are byte-identical, which is why everything stayed green. The gap is the story, not the green.

The 303 is worth restating: **`fetch` follows redirects silently**, so the React start button would have "worked" while navigating somewhere nobody asked for. That's precisely the class of bug this coverage exists for.

## Now covered

Against a **real appliance over real HTTP** — no container, because PGlite makes starting one cheap enough to do in a test:

- a mapping starts `paused`, so nothing copies before somebody says so
- `start` answers JSON (not a redirect) with `activated: true`
- a second click answers `activated: false` rather than pretending to have done work
- the mapping is **genuinely** `active` afterwards, not merely reported so
- an unknown mapping 404s instead of inventing one

## The Restart-Resume gate can now drive PGlite

`deploy/selfhost/compose.pglite.yml` runs the appliance with **no Postgres container at all**, and the gate takes `SELFHOST_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE`:

```sh
SELFHOST_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE=deploy/selfhost/compose.pglite.yml pnpm test:e2e
```

That gate is the right home for it: **restart-durability is a genuinely different claim** when the database is a directory inside the app's own container rather than a separate service. The T0 spike said "survives restart"; this makes it something our own gate can assert.

Validated with `docker compose config` (Docker is available in my environment even though the e2e runner isn't): only `app` starts, `depends_on` is reset, `SELFHOST_PERSISTENCE=pglite` and `SELFHOST_PGLITE_DIR` are set.

One honest wart, documented in the file: `DATABASE_URL` still appears in the merged config. Compose merges maps key-by-key and an override **cannot remove a key** — the `postgres` service is excluded via an unused `profile` for the same reason. The appliance ignores the URL on this path, and saying so beats appearing to unset something that isn't unset.

## What this does NOT claim

**The e2e itself has not been run.** It needs a runner with Docker; I made it runnable, not proven. If you kick off a PGlite run, the interesting failure modes would be restart-durability of the data directory and whether the `row_security` re-assert survives a container restart — both new surface.

## Gates

Typecheck `0`, lint `0`, **1106 unit tests** `0`.

author: andrewchen5678
body:
## Summary

Auto-resize and audio were per-session runtime toggles that started **off** on every connect, so getting either meant re-enabling it after each pick, per target. This makes each a **single remembered preference** — one value with two editors (the target picker and the existing in-session control) — applied to a new connection only where the target can honour it. "… if compatible" is a fixed caption, never a per-target capability check: the picker never learns a target's capabilities, so the toggles are intents applied against the `connected` handshake's `resize`/`audio` flags.

- **Browser:** two `localStorage` keys shown as picker checkboxes; the FloatingMenu toggles write the same value. Audio's AudioContext needs a click gesture, so `connect()` primes one inside the picker click and `handleConnected` adopts or releases it.
- **macOS:** two `ViewerPreferences` fields + `AppModel` observables with the same one-value-two-places wiring; seeded on `.connected` (resize every connect, audio only on a user-initiated pick/takeover so a silent reattach never un-mutes) and deferred to `.displays` for rxa's owned-display gate.
- **In-session title marker:** a `🔊` on the window title (macOS, suffix) and tab title (browser, prefix) while sound is playing — the one persistent surface, since the toggle is a menu item. Desktop only.

## Known limitation documented (not fixed)

Connect-time auto-resize on **RDP** needs a manual window nudge: a `Viewport` request that reaches the gateway before RDP's Display Control channel is ready returns `Asked::NotReady` and is dropped with no retry (unlike a density change). Recorded at the `Viewport` arm in `src/rdp.rs`, in `docs/roadmap.md` (Planned), and as a user-facing caveat in `docs/macos-viewer.md`. VNC and rxa are unaffected.

## Tests

- Swift: 350 pass — persistence, compatible/incompatible seeding, the rxa display gate, the silent-reattach guard, live-control write-back, and the title speaker. Two tests asserting the old per-session "forgotten on reconnect" behaviour were updated to the new inherit-the-default semantics.
- Frontend: bun tests, `tsc -b`, biome clean; `bun run build` run so `dist` is current.

## Deferred to a human (per project rules)

- Manual GUI QA of the macOS app (no automation for the GUI).
- Browser QA against a live gateway.

body:
## Intent

Closes #58. Slice 1 (`pyvista-headless-ci`) of the `field-visualization`
Arc — gates every other rendering Slice in that Arc (not #61,
`field-array-persistence`, which only needs bare `mx-viz`). Nothing
downstream should assume headless PyVista rendering works in this
repo's actual CI until this proves it.

## What changed

- `tools/viz/pyproject.toml`: new `[project.optional-dependencies]`
  extras group `3d` (`mx-viz[3d]`) — PyVista + Plotly together (both
  needed by near-term Slices, no reason found to split them). This
  repo's first use of PEP 735 extras, distinct from the existing
  `[dependency-groups] dev` mechanism.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `Sync workspace` changed to `uv sync
  --all-packages --all-extras` — the explicit, justified CI-workflow
  change the parent Design Charter's CPU-only-and-unchanged-unless-
  justified constraint requires; without it the `3d` extra would never
  install in CI. **A real finding, not just a config change**: the
  Arc Charter's own research claimed VTK >= 9.5 needs no Xvfb/OSMesa
  build for headless rendering — this did **not** hold up against the
  actual `ubuntu-latest` runner. First push segfaulted
  (`vtkRenderingOpenGL2`'s `render()`, no GPU and no software OpenGL
  driver present at all). Fixed with a new `Install headless rendering
  system packages` step (`libgl1 libglx-mesa0 libxrender1 libxext6
  xvfb`) and wrapping both `Test` steps in `xvfb-run -a` — exactly the
  fallback the issue itself anticipated for this case.
- `tools/viz/tests/test_pyvista_headless.py`: constructs a PyVista
  `Plotter(off_screen=True)`, renders a sphere, asserts a real
  (non-uniform, i.e. not blank/crashed) screenshot array comes back.
  Skips via `pytest.importorskip` when the `3d` extra isn't installed,
  so it doesn't change the required-dependency footprint of the default
  `uv run pytest` collection.
- `CONVENTIONS.md`: new 2026-07-31 entry recording the extras mechanism
  and the on-the-record license check (PyVista MIT, Plotly MIT, VTK
  BSD-3-Clause — already cleared at the Design Charter level, not
  re-derived here per the issue's own instruction).

author: openclassware
body:
Der erste Lauf von *Deploy Demo* auf `main` ([Run 30573287849](https://github.com/openClassware/elternsprechtag/actions/runs/30573287849)) ist im Test-Gate rot geworden:

```
Connection to localhost:5432 refused.
… Unable to determine Dialect without JDBC metadata
ElternsprechtagApplicationTests.contextLoads » IllegalState Failed to load ApplicationContext
```

## Ursache

`ElternsprechtagApplicationTests` ist ein `@SpringBootTest` ohne Overrides — es startet den echten Context und damit die Default-Datasource aus `application.properties` (`jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/elternsprechtag`, `myuser`/`mysecret`). Lokal bedient die Entwickler-Postgres aus `compose.yaml` sie, auf dem Runner niemand. Die übrigen 46 Tests laufen gegen H2 und waren nie betroffen.

## Fix

Ein Service-Container `postgres:17` im Test-Gate-Job mit genau den Werten aus `compose.yaml`, plus `pg_isready`-Healthcheck, damit Maven nicht startet, bevor die DB Verbindungen annimmt.

## Warum nicht H2 im Testprofil

Laut Spec (#1, „Testing Decisions") ist genau dieser Test der Seam, der belegt, dass die auf `${ENV:default}` umgestellte Konfiguration ohne gesetzte Umgebungsvariablen auflöst und der Context startet. Ein H2-Override im Testprofil würde diese Zusicherung aushebeln — der Test liefe dann gegen eine Konfiguration, die in Produktion nie verwendet wird.

## Verifikation

- `actionlint` ohne Befunde.
- Lokal (mit laufender compose-Postgres) grün: 47 Tests, BUILD SUCCESS.
- Der Runner-Fall lässt sich erst mit dem nächsten Lauf auf `main` beweisen.

author: grey275
body:
## What

The layer table's row disabling was computed inside the layers query, from `UsersClient.fetchLoggedInUser()`. That returns the raw react-query result, so it never passed through `Sel.loggedInUser` — the selector that folds the permissions dialog's simulation in. Simulating away `queue:force-write` left out-of-pool rows selectable and clickable in the Add Layers dialog, which is the one thing that simulation exists to show.

Every other force-write consumer already went through the selector, so the Raw Input toggle greyed out correctly while the rows next to it did not.

## How

The query now reports pool membership alone (`isOutOfPool`), and the force-write question is answered in `LayerTablePrt.Sel`, which takes the user and the rbac store as sources:

- `rowSelectionStatus` returns `{ isUnselectable, isSelected, blockedByPool }`
- `selectAllStatus` replaces the inline select-all computation that lived in the header component

This also fixes staleness the old shape would have had even if it had read simulated perms: row disabling was baked into a query result, so toggling the switch could not have updated it without a refetch.

Also drops `useLoggedInUserBase`, which had no callers and was the same unsimulated footgun sitting one line above the simulation-aware hook.

## Not affected

Real enforcement. A user who genuinely lacks force-write has it missing from their perms either way, and `layer-queue.server.ts` gates the write regardless. The two existing pool-filter e2e tests, which cover exactly that, pass unchanged.

## Testing

- New e2e test `simulating away force-write disables out-of-pool rows`: a user who holds force-write simulates losing it, and the out-of-pool row stops arming Submit. Positive control turns simulation back off and confirms the same row selects, so the assertion cannot pass for the wrong reason.
- Full suite green: 1174 unit, integration, 56 e2e.

## Dev instance

Run `pnpm dev` from the `force-write-sim-check` worktree (already initialised, port slot 27), then open http://localhost:3371/?login=petevdp

To see the fix: user menu -> Permissions, switch Simulate on, untick `queue:force-write`, then Add Layers -> turn the pool control off and try to select an out-of-pool layer. Before this change the row selected and armed Submit; now it refuses.

author: fmguerreiro
body:
A `context_mode: 'group'` scheduled task resumed the group's session but never saved the id the container came back with, so the next tick started fresh and orphaned the transcript the last one wrote. A cron-only group never recovers on its own: there is no human message to reset it.

`src/session-tracker.ts` now owns the session policy, and both `runAgent` and `runTask` feed it every container output. It writes the in-memory map and the `sessions` row together when a run establishes an id, and clears both when the run reports it could not resume. The tracker remembers what it cleared, because the agent keeps echoing the id it was told to resume on later output and would otherwise write straight back the id just dropped.

That also fixes the interactive path, which only looked for the stale-session error in the final result. A streaming run reports it mid-stream and then resolves clean.

Isolated-context runs share no session with the group, so they still track nothing.

Tests: `src/session-tracker.test.ts` covers the tracker directly, `src/task-scheduler.test.ts` covers the scheduler paths. The fake runner splits what a run streams from what `runContainerAgent` then resolves, since production never resolves the streamed marker itself; deleting either `track` call fails exactly one test. `npm test` 1589 green, typecheck and prettier clean.

Not in this PR:

- sagri-tokyo/sagri-ai#637 nothing ages out a pinned transcript
- sagri-tokyo/sagri-ai#638 the stale-session pattern can false-positive on model prose
- sagri-tokyo/sagri-ai#639 a container that fails to resume keeps using the dead id for the rest of the run

Fixes sagri-tokyo/sagri-ai#633

author: anzalkhan16
body:
## Problem
Currently, updating our npm packages and GitHub Actions dependencies is a manual and time-consuming process. Without automated dependency management, we risk falling behind on important security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements, which increases our technical debt over time.

## Solution
This PR introduces automated dependency management by configuring GitHub Dependabot for the repository.

## Changes Introduced
- Added a `.github/dependabot.yml` configuration file.
- Enabled automated dependency tracking for:
  - **npm** (scanning the root `/` directory)
  - **GitHub Actions** workflows
- Configured a `weekly` schedule to check for new versions.
- Implemented `groups` for both ecosystems so that related dependency updates are batched into single pull requests (reducing PR noise and CI load).
- Enforced limits on the maximum number of open pull requests (10 for npm, 5 for actions) to prevent the repository from being overwhelmed.
- Targeted updates to the default `master` branch.

## Benefits
- **Enhanced Security:** Critical vulnerability patches in our dependencies will automatically be surfaced as PRs.
- **Reduced Maintenance Overhead:** Maintainers no longer need to manually check for updates or run `npm update` manually.
- **Always Up-to-Date:** Ensures our GitHub Actions and project libraries remain on supported, modern versions.

author: ishledo
body:
The UI companion to [CON-150](https://linear.app/ogen/issue/CON-150/support-for-multiple-same-platform-accounts-per-profile-per-tenant) §13. The backend landed in [ogen#84](https://github.com/ogen-app/ogen/pull/84); the ticket is `backend`-labelled and its §4 scoped the composer picker out to a follow-up that was never filed.

Without this, a second LinkedIn account makes every auto-publish post on that platform unschedulable: the server refuses to guess which account to publish as, and nothing in the UI could express the choice.

## Built against the merged code, not the PRD

Two places where ogen#84 differs from what CON-150 described, and this PR follows the code:

- The gate ships **only on the auto-publish path** (`checkAccountSelection` runs under `if autoPublish` in `schedule.go`), not on every write as FR-4/FR-5 described. The client blocker is scoped to the `scheduled` edge to match — gating manual publish would invent a requirement the API doesn't have.
- `account_not_found` and `account_inactive` collapsed into **`account_unavailable`**. Shipped reasons: `account_selection_required`, `account_unavailable`, `account_platform_mismatch`.

## What changed

**The picker** (`PostQuickSettingsBar`) takes the three shapes the server distinguishes: nothing connected keeps its warning, exactly one stays plain text (the submit worker auto-selects it, so a one-item menu would be a fake decision), two or more is a required choice. `SCHEDULE` blocks without one, so the 422 is the race case rather than the normal path — and those machine codes now translate to prose instead of surfacing as `account_selection_required` in a toast.

**`usePublishingAccount` stopped guessing.** It resolved "first active account wins", mirroring a backend that no longer guesses either. The rule set moved to `lib/publishingAccount.ts` with tests named after the Go cases in `account_gate_test.go`.

**Two judgement calls worth a reviewer's eye:**

- The account set is deliberately **not** filtered by `is_active`. The server counts `deleted_at IS NULL` rows (`ListActive`); `is_active` is a separate flag mirrored from Zernio. Filtering on it would let the UI see one account where the schedule endpoint sees two — the picker would never appear and the schedule would 422.
- The choice is **locked once scheduled/published**, same reasoning as `canEditScheduledAt`: the Zernio submission already names the account, so a later edit would change the display and nothing else.

## Second commit: the Connect Platforms counter

Found while checking the multi-account flow end to end. The tile caption and the connect modal's success check both read `connectedPublishers.length`, but the server sets a publisher's `connected` from `len(accounts) > 0` and Zernio is the only publisher — so that count is 0 or 1 however many accounts a platform holds.

Three LinkedIn accounts read "1 connected", and connecting a *second* account compared `1 > 1` and never flipped the modal out of polling. The account landed fine underneath; the UI just never said so. Both now count accounts through one `connectedAccounts(view)` helper, which also replaces the same flatMap open-coded in `PlatformsSection` and `usePublishingAccount`.

## Verification, and its limits

`tsc` clean · 133 tests pass · production build succeeds · dev server boots.

**The ≥2-account path has never run against a live backend.** It needs two real accounts OAuth'd into a Zernio profile plus a local API at `main` with the migration applied. Everything below one account is inference from the merged Go code, not observation — a design harness (`design/*`) would be the way to eyeball the states before merge if you want that.

`eslint` couldn't run: no config is committed in this repo (pre-existing, per CLAUDE.md).

## Related gap, not addressed here

CON-150 raises the cost of having no disconnect endpoint. `/api/integrations/zernio/*` has no DELETE — accounts leave Ogen only when the reconciler notices they're gone on Zernio's side, which is why `DisconnectButton` renders permanently disabled. With one account per platform that was tolerable; with three, a stale connection is a permanent extra row in every picker and a billable Zernio account nobody can remove from inside Ogen. Tracked as [CON-133](https://linear.app/ogen/issue/CON-133/api-endpoint-for-disconnecting-zernio-account), still Todo.

body:
## 주요 변경

- **배포 빌드를 박스 밖으로 이전** — 7/29 배포 프리즈 사고의 근본 원인은 박스 내 Gradle 빌드의 피크 RSS ~2GB 가 유발한 스왑 스래싱으로 계측 확정됐다(docs 35 §11). t3.medium 승급 후에도 "박스에서 빌드하는 구조" 자체가 리스크로 남으므로, GitHub 호스팅 러너가 이미지를 빌드해 ECR 에 올리고 박스는 **pull + 컨테이너 교체만** 하도록 바꾼다. 배포 중 박스 빌드 부하가 0 이 된다.
- **불변 태그 + 즉시 롤백** — 이미지에 `sha-<12자리>` 불변 태그와 `staging`/`prod` 이동 별칭을 부여(docs 36 §5-5). 롤백은 빌드 없이 직전 태그로 컨테이너만 교체(1~2분). 이후 블루-그린(36 방안 1)의 전제 조건.

## 변경 사항

API·스키마 변경 없음. 배포 파이프라인만 변경.

| 파일 | 변경 |
|---|---|
| `deploy-staging.yml` / `deploy-production.yml` | **build**(ubuntu-latest: OIDC→ECR 로그인, buildx+GHA 레이어 캐시로 push) + **deploy**(self-hosted: `compose pull` → `up -d`, 기존 헬스체크·timeout 래핑·post-mortem 유지) 2-job 구조로 재작성 |
| `rollback.yml` **신규** | workflow_dispatch(환경 choice + `image_tag`) → pull/up 만. 배포와 같은 concurrency 그룹으로 경합 방지 |
| `docker-compose.staging.yml` | backend `build:` → `image: ${BACKEND_IMAGE:?...}` — 워크플로가 셸 env 로 sha 태그 주입(셸 env 가 `.env` 보다 우선), 수동 조작 기본값은 박스 `.env` 한 줄이 제공 |
| `Dockerfile` | 기능 무변경 — 낡은 주석만 현행화(테스트 CI 신설·off-box 반영) |

이미지 정리도 보존 기반으로 교체: 박스 로컬은 sha- 이미지 **최근 3개 유지**(GitHub 불능 시 오프라인 롤백용), 레지스트리는 **ECR lifecycle policy(최근 10개)** 가 담당. `docker builder prune` 스텝은 박스 빌드가 사라져 제거.

## 구현 메모

- **레지스트리 ECR 선택 근거**: ① pull 인증이 기존 인스턴스 롤(`bce-ec2-ssm-role`) 정책 1개 attach 로 끝나 박스에 자격증명 0개 유지 ② push 는 OIDC 롤이라 GitHub Secrets 에도 장기 시크릿 0개 ③ GHCR 은 free 플랜 private 패키지 한도(저장 500MB·전송 1GB/월)를 즉시 초과하고 기본 지출한도 $0 라 push 실패 리스크. ECR 비용은 월 $0.3 수준.
- 백엔드 이미지는 env-agnostic(런타임 `.env` 주입)이라 리포 1개(`bce-backend`)를 두 환경이 공유. 별칭만 `staging`/`prod` 로 분리.
- deploy job 의 rsync·헬스체크·post-mortem 스냅샷·OS 레벨 timeout 은 기존 그대로 유지(사고 안전망 존치). timeout 예산만 빌드→pull 기준으로 재산정(8m/3m).
- 테스트는 test.yml(#88)이 PR 에서 전체 실행 — 이 빌드는 기존대로 DocsTest 만 돌려 OpenAPI 스펙을 굽는다.
- 클라 레포도 같은 구조의 PR 별도 생성(프론트는 NEXT_PUBLIC 빌드타임 베이크 때문에 환경별 이미지).

## ⚠️ 배포 체크리스트

스키마·env 변경 없음. 단, **머지 전 아래 사전 준비가 완료돼야 한다** (미완료 상태에서 머지하면 build job 이 ECR 로그인에서 실패한다 — 상세 절차는 루트 docs/38):

1. ECR 리포 `bce-backend`·`bce-frontend` 생성 + lifecycle policy (AWS 콘솔/CloudShell)
2. GitHub OIDC provider + IAM 롤 `bce-gha-ecr-push` 생성
3. `bce-ec2-ssm-role` 에 `AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly` attach
4. 박스 2대에 `amazon-ecr-credential-helper` 설치 + `~/.docker/config.json` 설정
5. 박스 2대 `.env` 에 `BACKEND_IMAGE=<ECR>/bce-backend:staging`(prod 는 `:prod`) 기본값 1줄 추가
6. 머지 후 staging 검증: 배포 중 박스 `free -h` 부하 0 확인 → **rollback.yml 리허설**(직전 sha → 원복) → prod 는 별도 승인

author: oddharsh
body:
Found while looking for render parallelism in the 2026-07-30 cold HAR. The server side is already parallel (`handlePhotoGrid` and `swrKV` both use `Promise.all`), so I went looking at what the client waits on — and found the homepage isn't getting an Early Hints 103 at all.

Cloudflare Early Hints harvests **only** the `rel=preload` entries out of a Link header. `/` had none.

```
/whoareyou  →  HTTP/2 103
               link: </a/luna.*.css>; as=style; rel=preload,
                     </a/nav.*.js>; as=script; rel=preload

/           →  link: (ten discovery links, no preload)
```

### Why this is backwards

`shell-assets.js` singles the homepage out in its own comment: it's no-cache and revalidates every visit, so it always pays worker think-time before its 200, which is exactly the window a 103 exists to spend. Every page that needed it least was getting it.

### It was lost to a refactor, not a decision

`lib/security.js` still exported `withHomepageDiscoveryHeaders`, which composes precisely this pair. Nothing had imported it since `/` moved to `serveStaticPage` + `HOMEPAGE_HEADERS`.

That's why nothing read as broken — the behaviour was still written down, just disconnected from the route, so the file describing it looked correct. Deleted rather than rewired, along with `HOMEPAGE_LINK` and `appendVary` (no other callers). Two places describing one header is how this hides.

### The test is the part that was actually missing

It ties the header to `HOMEPAGE_HEADERS` **at the route** rather than to a helper that can drift out of the call graph, and it matches definitions rather than mentions so the comment explaining the history can stay.

### Verified

On a booted worker, `/` now emits both preloads ahead of the discovery links, identical in shape to `/whoareyou`'s.

**Worth re-measuring after deploy rather than assuming.** Gotcha 15 says the payoff scales with the 103-to-200 window, and on the cold capture that prompted this the homepage's server think-time was 103 ms — real, but not the ~280 ms window that preloaded fully when this was last measured. Read fetch **duration**, not `startTime`, and do it without a CDP session attached.

75 contract tests (1 new), 78 routes with 0 hard failures, perf budget, build green.

author: semkeijsper
body:
Opening a video that exists in the audio language but **not** in the persisted subtitle language parked the player dialog in a permanent half-loading state: the subtitle picker rendered the raw locale `nl`, the cast button spun forever, and the transcript button was disabled *and* spinning.

Repro: English catalog + persisted `subtitleLanguage: 'nl'` + `pub-jwbvod26_29_VIDEO`, which is released in English but not Dutch.

## Root cause

Two symptoms, one trigger.

`/media-items/O/<lank>` answers `{ "media": [] }` for a language a video was never translated into, so `fetchMediaItem` returns `undefined` and the `if (media)` guard in `useMediaItems` left `subtitleMedia` `null` for good — while `subtitleLoading` flipped `false` anyway. `null` meant both "not fetched yet" and "there is nothing to fetch", and both buttons read it as the former (`:loading="!subtitleMedia"`).

The raw `nl` was separate: `VideoDialog` already filtered both pickers to the video's `availableLanguages`, which excludes `O`, so the model value matched no item and Vuetify fell through to rendering the raw string.

The same hole existed on the **audio** side and was worse — a `null` `videoMedia` leaves `v-if="loading || !videoMedia"` spinning with no player at all.

## Approach

`Video.availableLanguages` is already on every catalog item (`VideoDialog` consumed it for the picker), but nothing reconciled it with the store — so the app could always tell *before fetching* that a language would come back empty. New pure util `resolveAvailableLanguage` (`app/utils/mediaLanguage.ts`) does that reconciliation, and `useMediaItems` now owns both the picker's item list and the resolved languages. The doomed request is never made.

**The store is untouched.** The preference survives to the next video, and an explicit pick still writes it — one English-only video no longer wipes a Dutch subtitle preference.

Where the preferred subtitle language is unavailable the picker shows the fallback and names the missing language underneath, via jw.org's own **`MsgNoContent`** key — a real translation key, so it arrives pre-translated in every language and needed only an `en` fallback entry, no per-locale translation work.

Two supporting changes:

- `!media` no longer stands in for "loading" on `CastButton`/`TranscriptButton` (both now take a `loading` prop and drop `subtitleMedia`), so even a failed fetch degrades to "no subtitles" instead of an eternal spinner — the bug *class* is closed, not just the reported trigger.
- `usePlyrPlayer` labels its `<track>` from the resolved language rather than the raw preference; otherwise Plyr's captions menu would read "Nederlands" over an English `.vtt`.

## Verification

Built the app, served it GitHub-Pages-style, seeded the `app` cookie with `subtitleLanguage: 'nl'`, and opened `/en/pub-jwbvod26_29_VIDEO` in a real browser against the live jw.org API:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| subtitle picker | `nl` | `English` |
| hint | — | *Dutch — This content is not available in the selected language.* |
| cast button | spinning forever | resolved |
| transcript button | disabled + spinning | enabled, opens with English cues |
| `/media-items/O/…` | requested → `media: []` | never requested |

Preference survived: opening a Dutch-available video snaps back to "Dutch (Nederlands)", requests `O/…`, shows no hint, and the cookie still reads `subtitleLanguage: "nl"`.

`pnpm test` 76/76 · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm build` (with `typeCheck`) clean.
New specs: `test/unit/mediaLanguage.test.ts`, `test/nuxt/composables/useMediaItems.test.ts`.

## Notes

- **A released language with no `.vtt` is deliberately untouched** — French and ASL are both like that for this same video. `subtitleMedia` is non-null and `subtitleUrl` is `null`; that path is already correct and covered by `test/e2e/player.test.ts`, so no fallback fires and no hint shows. Say the word if that case should explain itself too.
- **`pnpm test:e2e` was not run** — it needs the browser to reach jw.org directly, which the sandbox proxy blocks for Chromium. Worth a local run before merge.
- A hard *network* failure on the audio-language fetch can still leave the player frame spinning (`VideoDialog.vue:24`). Pre-existing and a different trigger; fixing it means designing an error+retry state, so it is flagged rather than folded in here.

body:
## Summary

Hotfix for a compile error introduced by the localization pass (#34).

`REMINDER_OPTIONS` in `AddEditEventScreen.kt` was migrated to `@StringRes` ids (`List<Pair<Int?, Int>>`), but the reminder `FilterChip` still passed the raw `Int` id to `Text()`, which has no overload for `Int`:

```
e: AddEditEventScreen.kt:1065:35 None of the following candidates is applicable:
   fun Text(text: String, ...)
   fun Text(text: AnnotatedString, ...)
```

Fixed by wrapping the id in `stringResource(labelRes)` (already imported, called in composable context). The `MlKitReceiptTextRecognizer.kt` "unresolved reference" errors in the same log were collateral from the aborted module compilation and clear once this real error is fixed.

## Verification (no Android SDK in this env — static checks)
- Repo-wide: **0** dangling `R.string.*` references, **0** missing `stringResource`/`R` imports, **0** illegal `stringResource` calls in non-composable scope.
- The `@StringRes`-id-list → unwrapped-`Text` pattern occurs only at this one site; all other `forEach` labels are `String` literals.

⚠️ Please run `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` locally to confirm — this environment cannot compile Kotlin.

## Known follow-up
The event-form agent stopped early during #34, so `AddEditEventScreen.kt` still has some hardcoded English literals (field labels, Mom/Dad, event-type & recurrence options). They compile fine (English is the base language) but aren't translated yet — tracked as a follow-up.

body:
## Summary

- report scheduler-independent `smg_http_admission_*` lifecycle counters and gauges from the priority scheduler path
- preserve the existing concurrency limiter semantics by sharing the same RAII accounting guards
- publish live scheduler concurrency and aggregate queue capacity through the generic admission gauges
- cover received, admitted, rejected, queued, active, completed, and capacity behavior with an end-to-end scheduler test

## Why

Comet's request-flow viewer consumes the generic HTTP admission lifecycle metrics. With `--priority-scheduler-enabled`, SMG reported scheduler-specific diagnostics but never updated that generic contract, so an active gateway appeared to receive zero requests.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p smg --lib`: 1357 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored
- focused priority scheduler admission telemetry test passed
- full scheduler integration suite passed except one transient mock-worker health timeout; the same existing test passed immediately when rerun alone
- scoped strict Clippy passed for SMG library and tests; exclusions cover pre-existing workspace warnings
- `cargo fmt --all` and `git diff --check` passed

author: jmromeroes
body:
## Summary

The `slim-image/release` Jenkins job has been failing the `Lint` stage on hadolint since build #91 (1.205.1), and again on #92 (1.205.2). Same 3 findings in every Dockerfile (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.slim`, `Dockerfile.rh`, `Dockerfile.alpine`):

| Rule | Severity | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| DL3066 | NORMAL | `USER root` | `# hadolint ignore=DL3066` above |
| DL3066 | NORMAL | `USER nexus` | `# hadolint ignore=DL3066` above |
| DL3025 | HIGH | `HEALTHCHECK CMD curl … \|\| exit 1` | Convert to `HEALTHCHECK CMD ["sh", "-c", "curl … \|\| exit 1"]` (JSON form, same shell semantics) |

`USER root` / `USER nexus` are intentional named users created by shadow-utils inside the image; DL3066 is a portability warning that does not apply.

`HEALTHCHECK CMD` in JSON form runs without a shell, so `||` short-circuit would not work as-is. Using `["sh", "-c", "..."]` preserves the exact behavior with zero semantic change.

## Verification

Ran the same hadolint image the Jenkins Lint stage uses:

```
docker run --rm -i hadolint/hadolint:latest-alpine   hadolint --trusted-registry sonatype.repo.sonatype.app - < <file>
```

Result: 0 issues on all four Dockerfiles.

## Failed Jenkins builds this unblocks

- [slim-image/release #91](https://jenkins.ci.sonatype.dev/job/insight/job/insight-brain/job/docker/job/slim-image/job/release/91/) — nexus-iq-server-slim-1.205.1
- [slim-image/release #92](https://jenkins.ci.sonatype.dev/job/insight/job/insight-brain/job/docker/job/slim-image/job/release/92/) — nexus-iq-server-slim-1.205.2

Rerunning the release job after merge should get past the Lint stage.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → slim-image/release rerun passes Lint stage
- [ ] Downstream main-image, rh-image, alpine-image release jobs pass Lint stage as well

author: starquake
body:
> 🤖 **Pull Request by Claude** (AI pair-programmer working with @starquake) — opened through @starquake's account.

Closes #347.

## Where to look

- **The diagnosis is that the monitor is edge-triggered and a queue is level-triggered.** Every signal it watches fires on a *change*, so none of them can see work that is simply waiting. That is why #318 and #333 could sit in `Build` for a session without anything noticing — and why adding another edge signal would not have helped.
- **The priority rule is the half that actually changes behaviour.** The heartbeat makes the queue visible; without "standing work outranks new work", visible is not the same as done. Reactive work won every time precisely because pre-emption was the unstated default — so the exceptions (red `main`, `ready to merge`, a direct request) are now written as *named* exceptions.
- **Every ~30 cycles is a judgement call.** Often enough that a parked lane resurfaces within the hour; rare enough not to be a nag; silent when the lanes are empty. Say if you would rather it were louder.

Verified the heartbeat's lane extraction both ways — names `#318 #333` when the lane holds them, emits nothing when it is empty.

---

*Mechanically verified — skip unless curious.* `make check` green. Docs-only, `.claude/skills/` — no product code.

author: aagamratadia
body:
## What

All three corner buttons sat in the top-right. The hamburger moves to the top-left; account and search stay put and close up the gap it leaves.

```
before                              after
┌──────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────┐
│           🔍  👤  ☰      │        │ ☰            👤  🔍      │
└──────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────────┘
```

Branches off `main`, independent of #24.

## How

`navSlots.ts` gains a **side**. Each corner numbers its slots from its own edge, so the hamburger no longer has to be counted by the buttons beside it:

- `navSlotOffset(side, index)` returns `{ left }` or `{ right }`; `NavButton` takes a `side` prop defaulting to `'right'`.
- The panel's close ✕ moves with it, so the control that opens the menu is the control that closes it.

That drops a bit of coupling as a side effect. `hasHamburger()` existed partly because hiding the menu on article pages shifted the other two buttons outward — `SiteSearch` was `slot = hasHamburger(pathname) ? 2 : 1`. With the hamburger on its own edge, account is slot 0 and search is slot 1 on **every** page, neither needs `usePathname`, and only `MegaMenu` still asks the predicate (to decide whether to render at all).

`ArticleNav`'s `navSlotsReservedRight(2)` is unchanged — two buttons reach into the right corner on article pages either way.

## The one page that needed clearing

`/tbs-nights` draws its own `TBS NIGHTS` label and `← Back` link in the top-left of the wizard sidebar — exactly where the button now lands, and the button is `position: fixed` so nothing pushes back against it.

The sidebar now reserves that corner through a new `--nav-slot-reserve` in `globals.css`, applied with `max()` so it only ever increases the existing padding. It mirrors `navSlotsReservedRight(1)` for layouts that reserve the gutter in CSS rather than TS; both files carry a note to keep them in step.

At `--px-page: 44px` the reserve is 104px and the button occupies y 44→88. At the 20px floor it is 80px against y 20→64. Sixteen px of clearance either way.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; frontend build passes.

author: nicosandller
body:
Your suggested framing — a checkbox — for the first half of #55.

## What it does
**Only when active** on a device: while its entity is inactive, the live card simply doesn't render it. A room packed with devices then shows only what's actually doing something.

- "Active" is the **same domain-aware test the badge highlight uses** (`entityIsActive`), so a lock counts as active when *unlocked* and a vacuum while *cleaning* — hiding agrees with the rest of the card rather than inventing a second notion of "on".
- **Fails hidden**: `unavailable` / `unknown` / a missing entity count as inactive. A device that asked to appear only when active shouldn't reappear because its integration dropped out.
- **The editor always draws it**, at 40% opacity with a dashed badge. An element invisible in *both* views would be unselectable and unfixable — the config would be the only way back.

## Scope
This is the "hide if not truthy" half. The issue's other half — *"a bank of elements that will stack vertically or horizontally"* — is a layout feature (reflowing active elements into a list), not a visibility flag, so **#55 stays open** for it. Worth noting the reporter never sent the screenshot you asked for, so I deliberately built only the part that's unambiguous.

## Verification
`tsc` clean, **474/474 tests** (+3: the on/off pair, the domain-aware cases, and the fail-hidden cases). Harness: with the light on the card renders both devices; with it off, only the ordinary one — while the editor still shows the hidden one dimmed (`opacity: 0.4`, dashed border) and selectable.

One thing the tests caught worth mentioning: my first cut let a device with **no entity** count as active if a stray state string reached the helper. It now returns "hidden" for an unbound device, matching the documented rule.

## Backwards compatibility
Absent field = today's behavior; no rendering changes for existing configs.

author: demtario
body:
T6 of the DEV-2027 redesign — [DEV-2160](https://app.clickup.com/t/9015210959/DEV-2160). Targets `feat/DEV-2027-redesign`, not `master`.

The body grid was fixed at `240px minmax(0,1fr) 50%`: the preview held exactly half the window and no one could trade space between the panes. Frames `85:9970` and `85:16935` show the drag state — a 3px blue seam running the full height of the body. (Those two labels are the other way round in the ticket and in the plan doc — `85:9970` is the dark frame. The plan doc also described the grid as `220px 1fr 1fr`. Both corrected here.)

## What changed

`s.body` becomes `240px minmax(0,1fr) 1px var(--hot-split, 50%)`. The 1px track **is** the splitter, so `s.column`'s `divided` branch and the editor column's `borderRight` are gone — one line, not two.

The ratio stays a fraction of the *whole body*, sidebar track included. That is what T2 measured (the preview starts at x=864 of 1728 with the sidebar both open and collapsed), and it is what keeps the seam still when the sidebar is toggled — asserted in the spec.

`splitterActive` is a new token pair rather than a reuse: light is plain `accent` (`#1A42E8`), dark is lifted to `#4669F6`, which is neither `accent` nor dark `accentHover` (`#3b5cf0`). Both frames are the drag state only, so the accent shows on hover, focus and drag — never at rest.

The handle is a `role="separator"` with `tabIndex=0`: arrows move the seam 2%, `Home` and double-click restore the designed 50%. Nothing in the design covers keyboard access to it, and without this there is none.

## Two decisions worth review

**The ratio reaches the DOM two ways, deliberately.** React renders it as an inline custom property, so a restored ratio is correct in the first paint; the drag then writes that same property straight onto the node, because a render per `pointermove` would walk the keyed CodeMirror instance (ADR-0016) and the preview pane. State and `localStorage` are touched once, on `pointerup`.

A `useLayoutEffect` was the first attempt and **silently no-oped**: React commits bottom-up, so a child's layout effect runs before its ancestor's `ref` is attached and `bodyRef.current` was still `null` on mount. Drags worked (by then the ref was live) and only a reload lost the ratio. Written up as open item 18 in the plan doc, since the next subtask would have hit the same edge.

**The drag survives the preview iframe** through `setPointerCapture` *plus* a `position: fixed` overlay mounted for the duration. The overlay also stops CodeMirror selecting text under the drag and holds the `col-resize` cursor across both panes.

## Verification

- `demo-runtime` build, `editor-shell` and `authoring` typechecks: clean.
- Default `playwright test`: 14 passed, 85 skipped (the gated matrix/live specs). New `e2e/splitter.spec.ts` adds four — drag over the iframe, persistence across reload, seam stability under the sidebar toggle, double-click reset.
- Rendered pixels match both frames exactly: 3px `#1A42E8` light / `#4669F6` dark while dragging, the 1px `border` token at rest.
- **Live Tier-1**, not only the empty frame the spec drags over: `?example=react` on the dev server with Sandpack booted and a Handsontable grid rendered inside the cross-origin iframe. The seam tracked the pointer through it (599 → 798 across four measured steps), dragged back, left the grid alive and the preview `ready`, selected no editor text, and survived a reload.
- Tier-2 was **not** exercised — it needs Docker and the API worker. The shell code is engine-agnostic and the frame is the same element.

## Known gap

Nothing re-clamps the split after the drag that set it. The 320px-per-pane minimum is enforced from the rect a drag measures, so a drag can never starve a pane, but shrinking the window or opening the sidebar afterwards can. Deferred to T9, which owns narrow viewports — there is no breakpoint frame anywhere in section 18.1 to clamp toward. Logged as open item 19.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core shell layout and drag/pointer behavior across CodeMirror and cross-origin preview iframes; persistence and clamp edge cases are documented but resize/sidebar-after-drag reclamp is intentionally deferred.
> 
> **Overview**
> **T6 (DEV-2160)** replaces the fixed 50% editor/preview layout with a **draggable vertical splitter** between the panes.
> 
> The body grid becomes `240px minmax(0,1fr) 1px var(--hot-split, 50%)`: the 1px track is the handle, so the editor column’s `borderRight` and `s.column(divided)` go away. The split is a **fraction of the full body width (sidebar included)** so toggling the sidebar does not move the seam.
> 
> New **`SplitPane.tsx`** (`useSplitPane` + `SplitHandle`): pointer drag writes `--hot-split` on the body node without re-rendering per move (avoids churning keyed CodeMirror); React inline style restores **`localStorage`** (`hot-split`) on first paint. Drag uses pointer capture plus a full-screen overlay so drags work over the preview iframe and without editor text selection. Keyboard (`role="separator"`), double-click/Home reset, 20–80% bounds and 320px pane minimums; new **`splitterActive`** theme tokens for the accent bar.
> 
> **`e2e/splitter.spec.ts`** covers drag-over-iframe, persistence across reload, sidebar stability, focus/hover accent behavior, clamp/reset on narrow viewports, and double-click reset. The redesign plan doc is updated with shipped notes and open items 18–19 (layout-effect ref gotcha; no post-resize reclamp — deferred to T9).

author: hyper-ff
body:
## Why I'm doing:

BadStatusOrAccess is thrown by an unguarded StatusOr::value() and is caught nowhere in the codebase, so every occurrence is a bug. Identifying it requires the stack at the throw site: __cxa_throw is already wrapped to capture one, but the white list only covers `std::` by default, so starrocks::BadStatusOrAccess was silently skipped. The only trace left then comes from the catch handler, by which point the throwing frames are unwound and the stack shows the catch site alone -- which is what happened on a CN that lost its whole connector-scan thread pool to escaped BadStatusOrAccess, leaving no way to identify the offending .value().

Keep it an exact type rather than a bare `starrocks::` prefix: that prefix would also match starrocks::RuntimeException, which exists specifically to opt out of this stack printing because it is thrown per row on hot paths such as cast failures.

Verified end to end on a live BE: with an unguarded value() injected into ProjectOperator::push_chunk, the query logs the throwing frame (ProjectOperator::push_chunk -> PipelineDriver::process -> _worker_thread) along with the query id, where previously only the catch handler's own frames survived.

## What I'm doing:

author: wobkobi
body:
Moving a link deletes the original, so the tail left in the source channel is the only trace of it
there - and it named the poster only. A message that tagged someone lost that on the way across,
leaving the people it was aimed at with nothing to follow.

The tail now repeats them:

```
<@poster> SENT SLOP TO <@a> <@b> https://discord.com/channels/1/2/3
```

and reads exactly as before when the message tagged nobody.

- Mentions come off the original content rather than the rewrite, which only swaps the URL.
- They keep the order they were written in, are deduped, and drop the poster, so a self-mention
  cannot render as them sending slop to themselves.
- Role (`<@&...>`) and channel (`<#...>`) tokens are not people and do not match.
- `allowedMentions` stays empty, so the names render without pinging - the original post already
  notified them.

Five new smoke checks cover the pointer with none, one, and several tags, plus the ordering, dedupe,
poster-exclusion and role/channel cases.

## Also in here

- The pm2 ecosystem config goes, with its readme section and the pm2 mentions in the `DEV_GUILD_ID`
  notes.
- File-level comments that had outgrown what they explain are trimmed: `words.ts` carried a JSON
  sample of the format `data/readme.md` already documents in full, and `smoke-test.ts` spelled out
  exit codes 0 and 1. Their `@file` tags go, along with the one on `transform.ts`.
- Lockfile refresh: `@types/node`, `acorn`, `brace-expansion`, `discord-api-types`, `flatted`,
  `minimatch`.

2.8.0 - naming tagged users on the tail is a user-facing feature, and the rest is chores.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run smoke` (130 checks) all pass; the pre-commit and
pre-push hooks ran them again on the way out.

author: leihaowen
body:
Moves artifact distribution off Aliyun OSS onto AWS S3, and brings this repo to
zero CJK text ahead of open-sourcing.

## Distribution

- 8.7 GB dependency mirror migrated to S3 (5 objects, byte-verified against the source)
- Artifacts live under their own `nimoos/` prefix. The original bucket is shared with
  an unrelated OTA system that owns `releases/`; sharing that prefix meant a CDN could
  not publish our artifacts without also publishing its firmware, version manifests
  and per-device upgrade logs.
- `setup-s3-cdn.sh` (CloudFront + Origin Access Control) and `setup-s3-public.sh`
  (interim, direct-from-S3) are a **sequence, not alternatives** — the CDN script takes
  the bucket private again, so `DOWNLOAD_DOMAIN` must move in the same change. Both
  scripts say so. CloudFront is currently held behind an AWS account verification.
- Download path verified anonymously, with no credentials in the environment:
  8 objects return 200; the old bucket's OTA data, out-of-prefix keys, and anonymous
  bucket listing all return 403.

## Defects found while doing this, all fixed here

| Defect | Effect had it shipped |
|---|---|
| `Install_Docker` piped a third-party domain into root's shell | supply-chain exposure on every China install |
| Upload prefix `releases` vs download prefix `NimoTech` | every stack component 404s on the first real release |
| `NIMO_UNINSTALL_URL` pointed at a prefix nothing uploads to | install aborts under `set -e` |
| 9 hardcoded old-bucket domains, 5 of them live fallbacks | update and stack install both 403 |
| Two conflicting `STACK_VERSION` defaults, 4 releases stale | `curl \| bash` installs the wrong version |
| `fetch-ttyd.sh` mirror base was a placeholder domain | mirror branch could never succeed |
| CDN grant was `bucket/*` | would have published another system's database backups |
| App store rewrite was inherited dead code | store pointed at a 404 if the pattern ever matched |

## English pass

Zero CJK characters, zero personal paths, zero LAN addresses. All 20 shell scripts
pass `bash -n`. Comments explaining non-obvious mechanics were translated rather than
dropped. `DEV_DEPLOY.md` also gained the five systemd units it was missing and lost a
hardcoded home directory.

## Behaviour changes, deliberate

- `clone_all.sh` clones over HTTPS into the parent of this checkout, so an outside
  contributor can actually use it and the layout matches what every `go.mod` replace
  directive needs. `NIMO_GIT_SSH=1` restores SSH remotes for pushing.
- `update-host-agent.sh` defaults its pip index to pypi.org; `NIMO_PIP_INDEX` overrides.

author: armaxri
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 step 5c: cut the in-flight **workflow-run** state machine (#1852 / #1865) over to the shadow `WorkflowRunStore` (PR #2256). The last of #2206's three machine cuts.

- **Render cut** (flag on by default): the Workflow Manager's per-workflow "running" badge and the inline run-output panel's live **status** now render from the projected `workflow-run@<clientId>` region **when it faithfully mirrors `appStore`**, else fall back to `appStore` verbatim — a declarative hook (`useProjectedWorkflowRun`), the direct analog of the monitors/agents render cut. Byte-identical to the pre-cut path (the mirror gate guarantees agreement).
- **Mutation cut** (flag on by default, instant-revert): `runStarted` / `stepAdvanced` / `outputOpened` / `runCompleted` / `runCancelled` / `runFailed` / `dismissOutput` dispatch `workflow.*` intents so the backend store is authoritative. The `appStore` run reducers are **retained as the parity-safe fallback** — a dispatch failure is logged and the local mutation continues, so a backend hiccup can never break a run.
- Both flags are independent and dispatched under a shared `shouldMirrorWorkflow()` gate (restore-cohort's model), so the render cut is independent of the mutation flag. Runtime-flippable via `window.__TERMIHUB_WORKFLOW_RENDER__` / `__TERMIHUB_WORKFLOW_INTENTS__` (or the matching `localStorage` keys) for rollback.
- **Kept frontend** (per the shadow's boundary): the streamed output `lines` / `exitCode` / `timedOut`, and the transient progress toast (a side-effect notification threaded through the run's async loop, not durable projected state). Recorded as Decision #4/#6 in the bridge module docs.

Maintainer decision: **proceed-on-tests**.

## Tests

- `workflowRunBridge.test.ts` — flags, region id, faithful-mirror gate (progress/status/args divergence, null-vs-undefined error, streamed content excluded).
- `appStore.workflowRunCut.test.ts` — cut-vs-local parity: drives the real `appStore.runWorkflow` against an in-memory twin of the Rust store and asserts the reconstructed region matches `appStore` at every settle (send-command, mid-run progress, run-local-process status seam, failed run, dismiss); both-flags-off dispatches nothing; render-on/intents-off still populates the region.
- `useProjectedWorkflowRun.test.tsx` — render-cut hook: flag-off returns `appStore`; flag-on renders from the projection when it mirrors; diverged region falls back; frontend-owned streamed content kept from `appStore`.

Full frontend suite (4914) green; `cargo fmt`/`clippy -D warnings` and the `workflow_projection` Rust tests green.

Part of #2206

Closes #2243

body:
## Summary

- restore `pull-requests: write` in `pr-status-labels.yml` and upgrade `pull-requests: read` to `write` in `pr-review-status-labels.yml`

#245 narrowed both label workflows to `issues: write` only. GitHub scopes the `GITHUB_TOKEN` permission check to the target resource, not the API route: adding/removing labels on a **pull request** via the `/issues/{number}/labels` endpoint requires `pull-requests: write`, and `issues: write` alone yields `HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration`. Since #245 merged (2026-07-30 02:39 +0800):

- every PR created after it (#274 onward) has no status label — the `pull_request_target` runs that actually attempt a write all fail (e.g. runs 30604978090, 30605327515); the interleaved "success" runs are early-exit no-ops, not real writes
- the new privileged review workflow 403s the same way on its first real write (run 30608729025), so the fork review-label sync #245 set out to fix still doesn't work

The two-stage `workflow_run` privilege-separation design from #245 is kept as-is; this only fixes the token scope.

## Related Issue

N/A (regression from #245).

## Test Plan

- `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/pr-status-labels.yml .github/workflows/pr-review-status-labels.yml` — all hooks pass
- parsed both workflows with PyYAML
- verified the root cause from Actions logs: with `issues: write` only, every real label write fails `HTTP 403`; pre-#245 the same script with `pull-requests: write` labeled PRs correctly for three weeks (#180)
- verified `gh pr view --json reviewDecision` returns real values on this repo (e.g. #266 `APPROVED`), so the `workflow_dispatch` bulk reconciliation is safe to run
- end-to-end Actions verification requires the workflows on the default branch; after merge, run `gh workflow run pr-review-status-labels.yml` once to backfill labels for the ~10 PRs opened since #274

## Compatibility / Risk

CI-only change; no application code touched. Widens the two workflows' token from `issues: write` to also allow PR writes — both run repo-side scripts only and never check out or execute pull-request-controlled content, so the #245 security boundary is unchanged.

## Reviewer Notes

Root-caused and implemented with Claude Code assistance; the diff was reviewed before publication. Duplicate-work check: #237 is the superseded predecessor of #245 (suppresses fork writes instead of fixing them) and can be closed independently; no other open PR touches these workflows.
