Two gaps in `AGENTS.md`, both raised on the promotion PR [#227](https://github.com/vnedyalk0v/react19-simple-maps/pull/227) and both verified against the repository. ## Release promotions could not follow the branch rule `AGENTS.md` required every task to branch from `dev` and open a PR into `dev`, with no exception. That contradicts the documented branch model in `docs/ci-cd.md`, where releases are promoted from `dev` to `main`, and an agent following it literally would open a no-op PR back into `dev` instead of the intended promotion. Promotions are now called out as the one exception: straight from `dev` to `main`, no task branch, no new commits. Valid review findings on a promotion PR are fixed on a normal task branch into `dev`, which the promotion PR then picks up automatically — the flow this PR itself follows. ## The review gate implied it governed automated sync PRs `.github/workflows/sync-main-to-dev.yml` creates a `main` -> `dev` sync PR on every push to `main` and enables auto-merge, and branch protection requires only the `ci` and `dependency-review` checks. Nothing waits for the automated reviews, so a sync PR can merge while they are still pending — meaning the gate as written described behavior the repository does not enforce. The gate now states its scope explicitly: every PR you open, into `dev` or `main`, excluding the automated sync PRs and Changesets release PRs, which their workflows own. ## Validation - `npm run check-format` passes. - Local pre-commit review gate returned no findings. body:
Closes #196

## 배경

매출분석 워커 5종 검증 3번째(behavior)에서 발견한 3건 수정. 핵심 문제인
purchaseComplete 0 집계의 근본 원인은 BE(집계 쿼리의 product INNER JOIN)에
있어 별도 이슈로 분리했고(toss-delta-final/jarvis-backend#62), 이 PR은 BE
수정 배포 전까지의 방어 + 구조 개선 + 계약 명시화다.

## 변경 1 — purchaseComplete 오검출 방어

FE 가 purchase_complete 를 productId 없이 발사(주문 단위, `properties.orderId`만)
→ `behavior_events.product_id = NULL` → I-13 의 product 조인 스코프에서 탈락
→ **실구매가 있어도 상품별·합계 0**. 워커가 "조회 많음·구매 전무" 가짜 패턴을
검출할 위험이 있다.

- `_BEHAVIOR_AUTHORITY_NOTE`(tools.py): "0 집계 가능 — '구매 전무'의 근거로
  사용 금지, 권위는 I-6/I-7/I-14" 로 강화. 상품별 수치 표시는 유지(BE 수정 후
  원복 불필요).
- BEHAVIOR·ABUSE 프롬프트: 구매 관련 판정은 get_funnel(I-7, order_item 기반
  — 실측 확인)·get_order_events 교차 확인 후에만 warning 이상으로 올리도록 명시.

## 변경 2 — 상품별 rows 상한 분리 + 꼬리 합계

구 공용 상한 `seller_summary_max_events=5` < 시드 브랜드 상품 7종이라 하위
2종 수치가 매 호출 소실됐고, 상한만 올려도 상품 수가 더 많은 판매자에서 재발한다.

- I-13 전용 `seller_summary_max_products=10` 신설(I-14 는 기존 5 유지).
- 상한 초과분은 "외 N건(저활동) 합계: 조회 X 담기 Y 결제시작 Z 구매 W" 로
  압축 — 잘림이 표본 누락이 아니라 요약이 된다.
- rows 가 활동량 내림차순 정렬인 것(BE `eventsByProduct` 실측)을 명세에 명문화
  — 잘리는 건 항상 저활동 상품.

## 변경 3 — eventType CSV 명시 직렬화

구 반복 쿼리(`eventType=a&eventType=b`)는 Spring 암묵 변환(반복 파라미터→콤마
문자열)에 의존했다. BE 계약(`String eventType` + comma split)에 맞춰
`",".join()` 으로 명시. **BE 변경 불필요**(컨트롤러 실측 확인).

## 계약

api-spec §4.4 I-13 v0.16.3 — CSV 직렬화·rows 정렬·purchaseComplete 미귀속
경고 명문화 (같은 커밋, 계약 우선 규칙).

author: mashkovd
body:
## Why

Two gaps, both already demonstrated in production.

**Cadence.** Hetzner-side attach/detach wedges are not rare — `stuck-pv-janitor`
caught them 8 times in July 2026 alone (07-12, 07-13, 07-14, 07-16, 07-20,
07-22, 07-23, 07-29). At a daily cadence a wedge found at 04:37 may have been
sitting there for 23 hours. Every one of those hours is an hour a workflow pod
can sit Pending — which on 2026-07-30 meant holding the shared
`mctl-gitops-main-writes` mutex and taking two whole cron cycles down with it.

**`kubectl delete` is not always enough.** When the CSI driver that owns a
VolumeAttachment's finalizer no longer exists, nothing can ever remove that
finalizer, and the delete just parks the object in `Terminating` forever. Six
of the seven attachments found on the janitor's first manual run (2026-07-05)
were exactly this: Longhorn zombies carrying
`external-attacher/driver-longhorn-io`, `deletionTimestamp`s from
2026-02-18/2026-03-31, pointing at long-deleted nodes (`pgo`/`sih`/`vhk`).
Longhorn has since been uninstalled entirely (`enable_longhorn = false`), so
they had to be cleared by hand.

## Change

- Schedule `37 4 * * *` → `37 * * * *`. The `:37` offset keeps it clear of the
  shepherd (`:00`), incidents (`:15`), and the `*/15` pollers.
- Telegram reporting becomes **quiet-unless-it-acted** (same policy as
  `argo-pvc-janitor`). At 24 runs/day a routine "kept N" message would bury the
  runs that matter. Failures still always report.
- New second pass: strip finalizers off zombie VolumeAttachments, gated on
  **all four** of:
  1. already has a `deletionTimestamp` — this pass never *initiates* a
     deletion, it only unblocks one;
  2. that timestamp is older than 1h — never races an in-flight detach;
  3. the Node in `.spec.nodeName` no longer exists;
  4. the CSIDriver in `.spec.attacher` no longer exists.
- The scan **fails closed**: an empty node or csidriver listing is treated as an
  API error, not as "everything is gone".
- ClusterRole gains `volumeattachments/patch` plus read-only `nodes` and
  `csidrivers`.

Conditions 3+4 are what make this safe. A finalizer strip against a **live**
driver would abandon a still-attached volume rather than detach it. Ordinary
hcloud wedges on live nodes are deliberately left completely untouched —
waiting remains the validated remedy there (they self-heal in 12–24h once the
stuck Hetzner action times out server-side).

## Verification

Strip logic run against a fixture covering the real shapes:

| fixture | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| Longhorn zombie: dead node + dead driver, terminating since Feb | STRIP | ✅ |
| **hcloud wedge on a live node** | keep | ✅ keep (node still exists) |
| dead node but **live** hcloud driver | keep | ✅ keep (driver still installed) |
| terminating only 10 min | ignore | ✅ filtered by jq |
| not terminating at all | ignore | ✅ filtered by jq |
| terminating with no finalizers | ignore | ✅ filtered by jq |

Local gates: `sh -n` on the extracted script, `yamllint 1.35.1` with the repo's
CI config, `kubeconform -strict` (4/4 valid).

author: nikhil-nunna
body:
## Motivation

`ncclIbGdrSupport()`'s fallback check scans `/proc/kallsyms` for the `ib_register_peer_memory_client` symbol, but this symbol is exported by `ib_uverbs` regardless of whether any real peer-memory client is actually loaded. This causes a false positive that leads RCCL's GDR-mode selection to prefer peer-memory registration over DMA-BUF, resulting in `ibv_reg_mr_iova2: Bad address` failures on hosts with no real client.

## Technical Details

Replaced the kallsyms symbol check with a generic scan of the `memory_peers` sysfs directory for any subdirectory (any registered client name), instead of checking a single hardcoded `amdkfd` path plus the unreliable kallsyms fallback. A real client creates a named subdirectory there; the kallsyms symbol does not require one.

## Issue Tracking

JIRA ID : AICOMRCCL-1662

## Test Plan

Live-tested across three clusters/NIC vendors with `all_reduce_perf` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, verifying via log evidence and direct `/sys/kernel/mm/memory_peers` ground truth: one AMD Pensando AINIC cluster and one Broadcom Thor 2 cluster (both with no real peer-memory client present — reproduces the bug), and one Mellanox CX-7 cluster (with a real client present — regression check).

## Test Result

On the two no-client clusters (Pensando/AINIC Broadcom Thor 2): both falsely detect peermem support before the fix, but with different consequences — the Pensando cluster hard-fails with `ibv_reg_mr_iova2: Bad address`, while the Broadcom cluster's driver stack can still service the registration call and passes anyway. After the fix, both clusters correctly detect no client and use DMA-BUF, with the Pensando cluster now passing cleanly for the first time. On the client-present cluster (Mellanox), both before and after correctly detect the real client — no regression. `#wrong = 0` and no performance regression across all three clusters.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md.

body:
**Sous-lot B** du chantier des zones orphelines. Périmètre strictement limité aux pages business / conversion.

## Ce lot ne câble rien — et c'est le constat

En ouvrant le sous-lot, les pages business se sont révélées **déjà pilotées** par le CMS :

| Page | Zones actives | Lues par le code |
|---|---|---|
| `contact` | 16 | 14 |
| `travel-planning` | 75 | 74 |
| `expert-hotelier` | 2 | 2 |

Le travail réel était du nettoyage, pas du câblage. Je le livre tel quel plutôt que de fabriquer du travail pour remplir le lot.

## Correction d'une de mes erreurs

J'avais annoncé `contact.service_1/2/3` comme orphelines. **C'est faux** : elles sont bien lues, via `zone={s.zone}` dans un `.map()`. Mon extraction ne reconnaissait que les littéraux et les templates, pas une variable simple. Le script livré ici classe désormais ces cas en « indéterminé » plutôt qu'en orphelins, pour ne plus produire ce faux positif.

## Nettoyage — migration appliquée en prod

Aucune ligne supprimée, `is_active` passe à `false`. Réversible, et le contenu reste consultable.

**`nos-services` (22 zones)** — `app/nos-services/page.tsx` se réduit à `permanentRedirect('/travel-planning')`. La page ne rend rien : ses zones sont inatteignables, tout en restant éditables dans l'admin. Contenu de surcroît rédigé en vouvoiement (« On conçoit **votre** voyage ») sur ce qui était une page B2C.

**`faq` (6 zones)** — aucune route `app/faq/`. ⚠️ Contenu périmé en plus : `faq_3_answer` annonce « à partir de **180 €** » là où `/travel-planning` affiche **250 €**. Le republier tel quel afficherait deux tarifs contradictoires.

**`travel-planning.hero_subtitle`** — le hero rend `hero_title` puis `hero_text` ; `hero_subtitle` n'est lu par personne. Exactement la configuration `hero_text`/`hero_subtitle` déjà corrigée sur `expert-hotelier`. Ici je **désactive plutôt que de câbler** : ajouter une troisième ligne au hero est une décision éditoriale, pas une correction technique. Le texte reste en base si tu le veux.

**`contact.page_title`** (les métadonnées viennent d'un export `metadata` statique) et **`contact.hero_image`** (valeur vide).

## Garde-fou — `scripts/check-cms-zones.mjs`

Pendant de `check-cms-drift.mjs`, qui fait le même travail pour les tables. Il croise les zones actives avec ce que le code lit réellement, par les **trois** chemins existants : `<EditableZone>`, `getCmsOrSetting()` et `getZoneLinks()`. Exit 1 dès qu'une orpheline apparaît sur une page non inventoriée.

L'audit que j'ai fait à la main devient rejouable — c'est ce qui empêchera cette classe de bug de revenir.

```
npm run check:cms-zones
```

Sortie actuelle :

```
Zones actives en base : 316
Clés lues par le code : 283 exactes, 118 globales, 44 motifs

? 18 zone(s) indéterminée(s) — la page utilise zone={variable}, non résoluble :
    contact (3)   app\contact\page.tsx
    home (15)     components\HomeClient.tsx

⚠ 45 zone(s) orpheline(s) sur 6 page(s) déjà inventoriée(s) :
    a-propos (9)   blog (4)   destinations (4)
    global (23)    mentions-legales (2)   politique-confidentialite (3)

✓ Aucune orpheline nouvelle.
```

## Où en est le chantier

Le chiffre de départ était 151. Après le sous-lot A (64 zones `global` câblées) et ce nettoyage (31 neutralisées), il reste **45 orphelines** sur 6 pages — le sous-lot C.

Les 23 zones `global` restantes sont les blocs transverses (CTA Travel Planning, messages d'erreur newsletter, `instagram_*`, `footer_copyright`, `footer_email`, `social_*_url`) : elles touchent d'autres composants que le header et le pied de page, je ne les ai pas tirées dans A pour ne pas en élargir le périmètre.

## Vérifications

- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` : OK
- `npm run check:cms-zones` : exit 0
- Aucun changement de rendu attendu — ce lot ne retire que des zones qui n'étaient affichées nulle part

⚠️ Rappel : l'**édition admin connectée** reste à tester avec ta session.

author: simonheybrock
body:
Fixes #15290.

## Note

*The investigation and write-up below were performed by an AI agent (Claude). I have proofread the descriptions and reviewed the code, but as I do not know much about Bokeh I cannot vouch for every detail. For code review, I therefore used a guide I had Claude make for a "non expert" — not sure it is useful for you (but it also includes an interesting section about how it traced the problem): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f2ef6d92-33ef-4ca8-99c6-240f7e02c3c3?org=e9fd120f-6b16-409a-a437-989319261ed9*

## Problem

Replacing a plot in a layout retains the whole figure for the rest of the session. `PlotView.connect_signals()` subscribes to `resize` on `window.visualViewport` and never unsubscribes. That event target lives as long as the page, so its listener list kept the closure — and through the closure the `PlotView`, the view's model, and every model below it — reachable long after the view was removed and the models were dropped from the document's model graph. The models were unlinked correctly; they just could not be collected.

It is not only a memory problem. Every retained view still ran the handler, so a single viewport resize called `canvas.resize()` and `request_repaint()` once per destroyed plot, i.e. work proportional to how often the dashboard has swapped a plot, on views that have been torn down.

Five other views subscribe to `document` or `window` without unsubscribing on removal, and retain their models the same way.

This is independent of #15289 and its fix in #15291. Pruning the model graph is necessary for removed models to become collectable, but not sufficient: with the pruning forced by hand, the models still stayed in the heap. Both are needed before a long-running server application holds steady.

## Change

`View` owns an `AbortController` that is aborted in `remove()`, exposed to subclasses as `abort_signal`. A listener on an event target that outlives the view is then bound to the view's lifetime with `{signal: this.abort_signal}` where it is registered.

The obvious alternative is a matching `removeEventListener()` in a teardown method, which is what the correct sites already do (`Menu`, `Pane`, `Tooltip`). It requires hoisting the listener into a field to keep its identity, and mirroring the capture flag, and staying in sync with the registration. `core/ui_events.ts` shows where that ends up: it registers `keydown`/`keyup` on `this.hit_area` and removes them from `document`, so both calls are no-ops in opposite directions, and never removes `focus`/`blur` at all. With `{signal}` there is no target to get wrong, no capture flag to mismatch and no function identity to preserve.

`abort()` is called with a shared `DOMException` rather than no argument: aborting without a reason makes the browser construct a fresh `DOMException` with a stack trace, measured at 4.0 µs versus 0.37 µs per call in Chromium, and every view being removed pays it whether or not it registered a listener.

Three commits, because the six sites are not all the same bug:

- The first commit fixes #15290. `PlotView` and `FullscreenToolView` register once per view, so binding the listener to the view is a complete fix.
- The second commit covers `InputWidgetView`, `HelpButtonView` and `AutocompleteInputView`, which register from `render()` or from `_show_menu()`. Those run repeatedly, so nothing outlives the view any more, but a live widget still gains one listener set per rerender. Registering them once means hoisting per-render closure state into fields, and belongs with the `on_change()` connections that accumulate beside them for the same reason — a follow-up that is ready and waiting on this PR to merge.
- The third commit covers `DialogView`, which registers its drag listeners per drag and removes them when the drag ends. Only removal mid-drag leaks, so the signal is the missing half of an otherwise correct teardown.

`{signal}` on `addEventListener` is Chrome 90 / Firefox 86 / Safari 15, and `abort(reason)` is Safari 15.4; both are well inside what bokehjs already requires (array assignment to `adoptedStyleSheets` needs Safari 16.4).

## Measurements

Bokeh server application that replaces a plot in a layout every 3 s while a second periodic callback keeps patches flowing, driven for 40 s (13 replacements), then the model graph is pruned by hand and a heap snapshot is taken after two forced collections:

| | `Figure`s live in heap | unreachable from the model graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 14 | 13 |
| after | 2 | 1 |

Total heap snapshot for the session drops from 65 MB to 38 MB. The one remaining stale `Figure` is a different and bounded effect — a live `GlyphRendererView`'s `visuals` object shares a V8 hidden class whose property accessor closes over the previously removed view — so retention no longer grows with the number of replacements.

## Test plan

- `PlotView` now has a regression test asserting it stops responding to `visualViewport` resizes once removed. Verified to fail without the fix.
- A `core/view` test covers the mechanism itself: a listener registered by a view against a shared target stops firing after the view is removed.
- `node make test:unit` passes: 2262 passed, 5 skipped.

Manual checks, since the remaining paths are user-interaction driven:

- [x] Plot still resizes when the visual viewport changes (pinch-zoom on a touch device, or browser zoom under mobile emulation).
- [x] Input widget description tooltip still opens on hover, pins on click, and closes on an outside click and on window blur.
- [x] `HelpButton` tooltip behaves the same.
- [x] `AutocompleteInput` menu still closes when clicking outside the widget.
- [x] `FullscreenTool` still tracks state when leaving fullscreen with Escape.
- [x] `Dialog` still drags, resizes, and ends the drag on pointer release and on Escape.

## Not addressed here

- `Document` adds a `change` listener to a `matchMedia` query that is never removed, but it retains nothing that is not retained anyway: every `Document` pushes itself into the exported module-global `documents` array in its constructor and is never taken out. Releasing documents is a larger and separate question.
- `core/ui_events.ts` cleanup is wired to the wrong target, as described above. `UIEventBus`, `UIGestures`, `ContextMenu` and `Pane` are not `View`s, so they cannot reach `abort_signal`; `CanvasView` already owns `ui_event_bus.remove()` and could pass its signal down.
- `InputWidgetView._build_title()` and `_build_description()` replace `this.title` / `this.description` with a freshly built view without removing the previous one, which then drops out of `_children_views()` and is never torn down, so its `abort_signal` never fires. Fixed in #15299, along with the same defect in `DropdownView`; that PR stands on its own and does not depend on this one.
- A lint rule against bare `document` / `window` subscriptions in view code would be the durable guard, since nothing stops the next call site from forgetting. `no-restricted-syntax` expresses it without new machinery, but it flags around twenty existing calls, most of them in code that has no view to take a signal from, so it needs its own change and a decision about those.

author: nico2398
body:
Closes #410

## Summary

Fix-until-coherent visual pass across the 10 building scenarios (menu, placement, tier-system, training, living, warehouse, research, vehicle-depot, ramp, destruction), plus one new scenario (`building-research-progression-visual`) closing a coverage gap against `gameplay-buildings` SKILL.md.

The pass surfaced real gameplay/logic gaps behind the visual symptoms, not just rendering bugs:

- **Research tier-gating wired end to end.** `isTierUnlocked`/`queueResearchTask`/`tickResearch` (`BuildingResearch.ts`) existed but had zero callers. Now `placeBuilding` and `build upgrade` reject unresearched tier-2/3 construction, `tickResearch` advances the queue each tick, and a new `research` console command (`research queue type:<type> tier:2|3`, `research status`) exposes it — with a guard against insufficient funds and duplicate queuing.
- **Blast damage to buildings wired end to end.** `BlastExecution.executeBlast` already implemented footprint-overlap building destruction, but the console `blastCommand` never passed `buildingState` into it, so blasts never touched buildings in the real game path (`building-destruction-visual`'s whole premise). Also fixed the scenario's charge amount (`amount:10` exceeded boomite's 8kg max, so the blast never even executed).
- **Employee training relocates the employee** to be visible next to the training building on enrollment (previously stayed at hire-spawn, rendering nowhere near where the scenario says it should).
- **Entry/exit building markers were geometrically invisible on every building, every scenario** — buried inside the opaque base box, and for roof-accented types (`blasting_academy`, `living_quarters`, `research_center`), inside the accent block too. Fixed in `BuildingMesh.ts`.
- **Playability gap found and closed:** the research-gating feature above had no UI entry point — a player hitting the tier-2/3 wall had no clickable path forward, only the dev console. Added a "Queue Research" button to `BuildMenu.ts` (catalog + placed-building rows), with translated status/error messages and a real `clickSelector`-driven interaction step in `building-tier-system-visual.json` proving a player can reach tier 3 via clicks alone.
- Scenario-definition fixes: ramp camera framing (target coordinates + pitch/distance tuning), `building-living-visual`/`building-tier-system-visual`/`building-research-visual` research/tick sequencing so their tier-2/3 steps actually succeed instead of failing silently, and starting-cash adjustments to keep scenarios solvent.

## Decisions taken

Defaulted under `agentic-decision-autonomy`:

- **What was open:** `gameplay-buildings` SKILL.md states the Research Center is a prerequisite for unlocking higher tiers of *other* buildings, implying research should require an actual placed `research_center` building. The wired implementation does not check this — `research queue` succeeds on a fresh game with zero buildings placed.
  **Chosen:** ship research-gating without a research-center-building prerequisite.
  **Why:** requiring a real building would need every scenario that queues research (`building-tier-system-visual`, `building-research-visual`, `building-living-visual`, `building-research-progression-visual`) to place and maintain a `research_center` first, expanding this visual-coherence issue into a second gameplay-balance change with its own scenario rewrites, well past what closing the reported visual incoherence needs.
  **If reversed:** add a `hasResearchCenter(state)` check alongside the existing `isTierUnlocked` check in `src/console/commands/research.ts`'s `queue` case; no other call site moves.
  Filed as a follow-up decision-review issue (material to gameplay economy).

- **What was open:** whether player-reachability of the new "Queue Research" button needs a dedicated `npm run playtest` definition, versus proof via a real-click scenario interaction step.
  **Chosen:** proved reachability via `building-tier-system-visual.json`'s `clickSelector`/`waitForSelector` interaction steps (real DOM clicks, not console commands standing in for a player action) rather than authoring a new playtest definition.
  **Why:** `scripts/playtests/` currently only covers `tutorial`/`training`; adding a third definition for one button is disproportionate to this issue's scope, and the interaction-mode scenario already satisfies the substantive playability requirement ("a player can reach the goal by clicking").
  **If reversed:** add a `scripts/playtests/building-tiers.json` definition following the existing two as a template.

## Verification

- **static** — `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- **logic** — `npm run test`: 201 files / 5830 tests pass (unit + integration, including new `research.integration.test.ts`, `building-scenarios-410.integration.test.ts`).
- **scenario** — `npm run scenarios`: 102/102 pass (command mode).
- **visual** — all 11 scenarios run in `--mode interaction --screenshots`, every screenshot inspected across 4 iterations of the feedback loop; final pass: PASS. `npm run a11y`: 99/99 elements WCAG AA. `npm run validate:state`: 0 schema errors.
- **playability** — no console-command stand-ins: the research-gate UI dead-end was found and closed with a real clickable button, proven via real-click (`clickSelector`) interaction-mode run reaching tier 3, plus `npm run playtest -- tutorial`: 21/21 beats pass (no regression). No dedicated playtest definition exists for building tiers specifically — see Decisions taken.
- **build** — `npm run validate` (typecheck → coverage → integration → scenario defs → build): PASS end to end.

READY TO MERGE

author: cotishq
body: # Description Fixes #993 Previously, every driver's Setup() method contained an ad-hoc line that both set the default retry count and silently mutated it, incrementing it by 1 when a value was already present: ```go // old pattern (e.g. postgres.go) p.config.RetryCount = utils.Ternary(p.config.RetryCount <= 0, 1, p.config.RetryCount+1).(int) ``` This had two bugs: 1. Off-by-one on user-supplied values: a user who set retry_count: 3 would silently get 4 retries. 2. Wrong place for default logic: defaults belong in Config.Validate(), which is called before Setup(), not inside connection setup code. This PR removes all those lines and moves the default initialisation into each driver's Config.Validate(): ```go // new pattern (e.g. drivers/postgres/internal/config.go) if c.RetryCount <= 0 { c.RetryCount = constants.DefaultRetryCount } ``` constants.DefaultRetryCount = 3 is now consistently used as the fallback across all drivers. The value is set once, early, and never mutated again. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) # How Has This Been Tested? - [x] Scenario A - Default retry count ( omitted from config ) Previously, Setup() would have set it to 1. - [x] Scenario B - User-supplied retry count is respected without mutation - Added "retry_count": 5 to source.json and re-ran the same sync command. Logs confirmed: # Screenshots or Recordings https://drive.google.com/file/d/1S1Nzz4CWyiUkyBCyCM5HqSHa2H6rMFZm/view?usp=sharing ## Documentation - [ ] Documentation Link: [link to README, olake.io/docs, or olake-docs] - [x] N/A (bug fix, refactor, or test changes only)

author: doriancollier
body:
Builds E3 of the `execution-defaults` design record: the client half of choosing what a new conversation starts with. Refs DOR-767.

## What ships

Per design record §1–§7:

- **Defaults card** on Settings → Runtimes (§1) — the first UI `runtimes.default` has ever had, joined by model and effort. Model and effort are scoped per runtime, because a model id only means something inside the runtime that offers it. The timing line appears only after a change (§3.2).
- **Exceptions strip** beneath it (§5) — every agent that departs from the defaults, broken ones first in amber, healthy deviations after. A fleet that all inherits renders nothing. A row is a link into that agent's own Config tab, not an editor.
- **Needs-attention bridge** (§5, operator's hard requirement) — breakage also qualifies an agent for the sidebar's smart group, so you don't learn an agent can't start by running it.
- **Config-tab rows with chip-is-reset** (§2, §3.1) — Model and Effort join the Runtime dropdown as three rows, each wearing its own provenance chip. The chip *is* the undo: a "set here" chip offers exactly one action. Mobile pushes the vaul drawer with the inherit line at the foot (§6).
- **Unsupported is said, not hidden** (§3.4) — "Not supported by OpenCode", "This model doesn't take an effort setting", and a soft warning where a stored value does nothing, always with a way to clear it.
- **Onboarding literal fix** (§7.1) — the first DorkBot session respects your default runtime instead of hardcoding Claude Code.

Server side is read-only: `describeExecutionDefaults` exposes the resolved defaults, and `resolveSessionDefaults` seeds them at first write.

## For reviewers — four judgment calls worth your eyes

**1. The cold-catalog evidence rule.** `GET /api/models` answers `200 {models: []}` while a runtime's cache warms up — that empty array is the server's own "client shows loading state" tier, not a claim the runtime offers nothing. Passed through, it reported every pinned model in the fleet as gone and turned a cold cockpit amber for a few seconds after every start. `knownModelsFrom()` collapses `[]` → `undefined` in one place, and both consumers route through it: **evidence nobody has is never evidence against.** Teaching the route to distinguish warming from genuinely-empty would mean a new state on `AgentRuntime.getSupportedModels()` and all three adapters; worth doing the day a runtime legitimately offers zero models, which none does today.

**2. Effective-model vs. pinned-model — a deliberate split, not an inconsistency.** Effort asks about the model that will actually run the turn (the agent's pin *or* what it inherits), so an agent asking for high effort on an inherited Haiku is called broken in the strip, the Config tab, and the sidebar alike. Availability stays scoped to the pin: a server default that stopped being offered is one problem with one fix, and repeating it once per agent would bury the agents that actually chose something. Both halves are stated in `describeAgentExecution`'s TSDoc.

**3. The sidebar's `checkModels: false` trade-off.** The rules are one implementation, but the *evidence* differs by surface, so the two can honestly disagree. Needs-attention sees the two catalog-free breakages (runtime not connected; effort on a runtime whose API has none); a model that is gone, and an effort on a model that can't take one, need a catalog and appear only in the strip and the Config tab. Making the sidebar complete means fetching every runtime's catalog on every fleet render, to change an amber dot. **The changelog fragment is written to match** — it promises Needs-attention only for what that path can actually catch.

**4. The pre-launch picker guard stays, and here is why.** Design §3.3 asks that model/effort be choosable before a session's first message. Browser-verified on a cold `/session?dir=…`: the route loader always mints a session id, so the picker is already enabled, opens, and the old "Send a message first" tooltip never renders — §3.3 is satisfied on the launch-critical surface, now pinned by a loader test. The `disabled={!sessionId}` guard looks vestigial but is **not dead code**: the Obsidian embed has no router and no loader, reads the id from a store that starts `null` and is reset to `null` on a directory switch, where the picker would have no session to write to. Removing it would be a behavior change to a surface this repo can't yet verify end to end, so it stays with the reasoning recorded at the call site. **The embed gap is real and tracked separately.**

One knowing deviation is recorded in `use-execution-exceptions.ts`: it imports sibling entities, which `.claude/rules/fsd-layers.md` § Cross-Module Rule forbids. Both compliant routes are worse (lifting to `features` puts it above the sidebar that consumes it; splitting per entity mints the second implementation of "broken" the module exists to prevent). Only the data-gathering crosses slices — the rules stay pure in `shared/lib`. Same deviation and reason as the existing `use-agent-tool-status.ts`; a third case is the signal to lift these reads into `shared/` properly.

## Verification

- Every fix red-before/green-after or mutation-evidenced (nine mutations, each restoring the pre-fix behavior and going red).
- Client suite green (665 files / 7785 tests); server green standalone (495 / 7816); full monorepo forced run green apart from load-dependent server flakes that differ per run and pass in isolation — this branch touches no server test paths.
- Browser-verified against a live cockpit: the strip's wrapped multi-breakage reasons at 1280 and 390, the chip reset closing its popover and reading "server default" *before* the round-trip, and the pre-launch picker opening on a fresh session.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: renechoi
body:
## Describe the PR

`RuleSetLoader#loadFromString` temporarily replaces the configured `ResourceLoader` with an anonymous wrapper that serves the XML content for the symbolic file name. That wrapper was built with the no-arg `ResourceLoader()` constructor, so it silently fell back to PMD's own class loader.

Resource lookups still behaved correctly, because the wrapper's `loadResourceAsStream` delegates to the previous loader for every other name. Everything that goes through the class loader did not:

* `ResourceLoader#loadRuleFromClassPath` could not find rule classes that are only visible to the class loader passed to `loadResourcesWith(ClassLoader)`, so loading the ruleset failed with `Reflection error while instantiating rule (ClassNotFoundException)`.
* `loadClassPathResourceAsStream` used the wrong class loader for the same reason.

```java
new RuleSetLoader()
  .loadResourcesWith(customClassLoader)
  .loadFromString(location, rulesetXmlContent); // customClassLoader was ignored
```

The fix constructs the wrapper with the previous loader's class loader, so class and classpath resource resolution keep using what the caller configured. Passing the class loader (rather than overriding the individual class-loading methods) also keeps any future `ResourceLoader` method that uses the class loader correct by construction.

`ResourceLoader#getClassLoader()` is added for that. `ResourceLoader` lives in `net.sourceforge.pmd.util.internal` and is marked `@internalApi`, and japicmp reports no API change for this PR.

## Related issues

- Fix #6913

## Ready?

- [x] Added unit tests for fixed bug/feature

  `RuleSetFactoryTest#testLoadFromStringUsesConfiguredClassLoader` loads a ruleset whose `class` attribute is only resolvable through the configured class loader. On `main` it fails with `Reflection error while instantiating rule (ClassNotFoundException)`; the other 59 tests of that class stay green, so the new test is not covered by the existing ones.
- [x] Passing all unit tests

  `./mvnw -pl pmd-core verify` on this branch: `Tests run: 6441, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 7`, with checkstyle, pmd, cpd-check and japicmp all passing.
- [x] Complete build `./mvnw clean verify` passes (checked automatically by github actions)

  GitHub Actions has not run on this PR yet, so I ran the complete build locally on `b141dac`, with Temurin 21.0.9 on macOS aarch64:

  ```
  ./mvnw --show-version --errors --batch-mode clean verify
  BUILD SUCCESS -- Total time: 12:33 min
  ```

  All 44 modules pass. `19188` unit tests (`Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 39`) plus `31` integration tests, `checkstyle:check` reporting `0` violations in each of the 44 modules, and `pmd:check`, `pmd:cpd-check`, `javadoc:jar` and `source:jar` green everywhere. `japicmp:cmp` also runs in all 44 modules and is configured with `breakBuildBasedOnSemanticVersioning`, so the green build covers the API compatibility claim above. `RuleSetFactoryTest` itself runs `Tests run: 60, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0`, that is the 59 existing tests plus the new one.
- [x] Added (in-code) documentation (if needed)

author: blume1977
body:
## Problem

Saving a call-queue outcome with **Completed** stores the comment and the userData phone-call fields, but the pending transaction is never touched. The AmlCheck action selector is hidden exactly when the outcome is Completed:

```ts
const showAmlCheck = hasTx && outcome !== CallOutcome.COMPLETED;
```

so `saveCallOutcome` skips the transaction step entirely and the payment stays on `amlCheck = Pending`.

For `ManualCheckIpCountryPhone` this is a dead end: the reason is part of `BlockAmlReasons` in the API, so the AML recheck cron never picks the pending transaction up again. Setting the userData check date alone has no effect there. This used to work in the Google-Sheet process; since the sheet access was removed, the tool is the only path.

## Fix

- Show the AmlCheck action for transaction-based queue items on all outcomes.
- When the outcome is set to **Completed**, default the action to **Reset** (per review: not Pass). Reset clears `amlCheck` + `amlReason` via `DELETE :id/amlCheck`, so the AML cron re-runs the **full** AML check: with the check date now set the phone error is gone, and the tx only passes if no other errors remain. Overridable via the selector.
- Reorder `saveCallOutcome` to write the **userData update before the transaction step**. A reset transaction is re-evaluated from scratch by the cron; if the check date were written after the reset, the cron could re-pend the tx into its recheck-blocked reason in the gap and it would be stuck again.

## Tests

- Component test `call-queue-outcome-form.test.tsx`: action offered for tx items, Reset default on Completed, override, reset on other outcomes, no action for user-based queue items.
- Hook test `compliance-call-outcome.hook.test.ts`: userData (incl. queue-specific check date, e.g. `phoneCallIpCountryCheckDate`) is written before the transaction reset; no transaction call without an action.
- `npm test`: 62 suites / 610 tests green, `npm run lint` clean on the touched files.

author: tasnim-rizvy
body:
## Summary

Fixes **#13 — Critical: Dockerfile build will fail** and adds a one-command Docker setup for all backend dependencies.

### 1. Dockerfile (issue #13)

The old Dockerfile was broken in two ways:
- `npm ci --only=production` — there is **no lockfile** in the repo (`*-lock.json` is gitignored), so `npm ci` fails immediately
- `--only=production` skips devDependencies, but `npm run build` (tsc) needs TypeScript and `@types/*`

**Fix:** Multi-stage build:
- **builder** — installs all deps (`npm install`), runs `npm run build -w apps/api`, prunes dev deps
- **runner** — copies only production `node_modules` + `dist` (final image: 364 MB)

Also added a root `.dockerignore` since the build context is now the repo root (monorepo).

### 2. Docker compose — one command for all dependencies

New `compose.yaml` at the repo root:

| Service | Image | Port |
|---|---|---|
| `postgres` | postgres:17-alpine | 5432 |
| `mongodb` | mongo:7 | 27017 |
| `redis` | redis:7-alpine | 6379 |

Each has a **healthcheck** and a **named volume** for persistence.

### Usage

```bash
npm run db:up      # ← ONE command: starts Postgres + MongoDB + Redis
npm run dev:api    # ← ANOTHER command: starts the backend
```

Also added `npm run db:down` and `npm run db:logs`.

## Verification

- `docker compose up -d` → all 3 containers **healthy**
- `npm run dev:api` → `✅ MongoDB connected`, `✅ Database migrations complete`, `✅ Redis connected`, `Server is running on port 4000`
- `podman build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t smartdoc-api:test .` → **build succeeds**
- Built image ran standalone with `--network host`: health endpoint returns `{"status":"ok"}`

## Related

- Closes #13

## Summary

Closes #177. `full-validation.yml` fetched the candidate revision with `--depth=1`, marking it a graft boundary and breaking `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — the exact check REPORT-CONTRACT.md requires of every post-T68 report.

**Observed failure**, not theory: dispatching `gate:quick` at `411daa74` ([run 30724489842](https://github.com/accd/verchestra/actions/runs/30724489842)) derived `T68 complete; T68a next` inside the runner while the tree carried `t68a`–`t68d` reports; `context.test.mjs` failed with that exact pair. The same revision passed `gate:security` ([run 30724495375](https://github.com/accd/verchestra/actions/runs/30724495375)) only because that profile does not run `test:agent-readiness`.

It stayed hidden because every earlier dispatch attested a revision whose *tree* predated the inserted reports, so truncated ancestry produced the same pair those trees declared. From T69 onward, no revision can be attested by `gate:quick` without this fix.

## Safety impact and documentation

Workflow change under `.github/workflows/`, so per `docs/merge-governance.md` the body must say which of the three it does: this **preserves** enforcement. Nothing is relaxed, no gate stage removed, no check narrowed — a proof that could never succeed becomes able to succeed honestly. The cost is clone time on a manually dispatched job.

## Verification evidence

- The fix is verified by its consequence: re-dispatching `gate:quick` at the same revision after merge must derive `T68d complete; T69 next` and pass. That run will be linked in the T69 validation report, which cannot be written until it does.
- No local gate is affected (the workflow is not part of any gate profile).

## Issue and milestone state

- Assignee on the linked issue: accd · Labels: bug, area: qualification · Milestone: none · Issue status after merge: closed by this PR

## Merge path

Intended merge path: maintainer bypass per docs/merge-governance.md — enforcement-preserving workflow repair; all required checks must pass on the current head first.

author: fundthmcalculus
body:
## What

Hoist the per-feature column extraction in `tsk_firing_strengths` out of the
label loop. One line moves; the result is bit-identical and ~19% faster on the
antecedent-refinement path.

## Why

`feature_data = X[feature_name].values` sat inside the **label × feature** double
loop, so every call performed `n_labels × n_features` pandas column lookups where
`n_features` would do. On UCI Concrete that is 3 × 8 = 24 lookups per call
instead of 8.

That is cheap in isolation and brutal under `refine_antecedents_coordinate`,
which evaluates its fitness function tens of thousands of times against an
**unchanging** frame — `refine.py` builds `prepared` once, and only the candidate
Gaussian parameters vary between evaluations. The same columns were being
re-extracted from the same DataFrames two million times.

Profile of one seed of the grad-school Concrete reconciliation, serial:

```
257.3s total
  244.0s   refine_antecedents_coordinate        (95%)
  147.9s   pandas DataFrame.__getitem__         2,216,240 calls  <-- 57% of runtime
  120.1s   tsk_firing_strengths (cumulative)       84,104 calls
   10.6s   tsk_firing_strengths (own work)
```

The function's own arithmetic is 10.6s. Nearly everything else attributed to it
was pandas indexing.

## Result

Measured on one seed of the grad-school Concrete reconciliation, serial, **no
profiler**:

| | time |
|---|---:|
| without hoist | 143.0s |
| with hoist | **129.0s** |
| | **9.8% faster** |

**Verified bit-identical**, not merely close: firing strengths computed before
and after on the same fitted model give `max |Δ| = 0.0` and
`np.array_equal(..., equal_nan=True) is True`.

### A caution about the profile above

An earlier revision of this PR claimed 19%, taken from the cProfile run. That
figure was wrong and I have corrected it. cProfile charges per-call overhead,
and pandas `__getitem__` has a deep internal call chain, so it is badly
over-weighted: the profile reports 57% of runtime in pandas and inflates the
seed from ~130s to 257s. The wall clock is the number to trust; the profile is
only good for *finding* the hotspot, not sizing it.

A microbenchmark at the real shape (824 rows × 8 features) sets the ceiling:

| access | per 8-column fetch |
|---|---:|
| `df[col].values` (before) | 57.35 µs |
| `arr[:, idx[col]]` | 1.08 µs |
| `dict[col]` pre-converted | 0.18 µs |
| one-off `df.to_numpy()` | 1.53 µs |

Removing pandas from this path *entirely* is worth about 11%, so this one-line
hoist already captures most of what is available here.

## Not done here

~673k of the remaining ~871k lookups are still this function doing 8 per call
across 84k calls. Since the frame is invariant across a refinement run, an
optional `feature_arrays` parameter — built once per fold by `refine` and passed
down, defaulting to `None` so existing callers are unaffected — would collapse
those to roughly six conversions for the whole run. Rough estimate: another ~40%,
landing the path near 2× overall. Happy to follow up if you want it.

Separately, ~162s of the original profile is scipy finite-difference gradients
inside L-BFGS-B. An analytic gradient is the other large lever, and a much bigger
change.

## Testing

`pytest tests/` from the submodule root: **152 passed, 56 subtests passed, 1
failed** in 19m05s.

The one failure is `test_trapz_math.py::TestTrapzPDF::test_trapz_pdf_degenerate_point`,
and it is **pre-existing and unrelated** — `trapz_pdf` with `a == b == c == d`
returns something that is not all-zero. Verified rather than assumed: it fails
identically on the parent commit with this change reverted.

Two collection issues, also pre-existing:

- `test_textclassifier.py` needs the optional `sentence_transformers`, absent
  here; excluded from the run.
- Running pytest from the *parent* repository picks the wrong rootdir and breaks
  `test_trapz_math.py`'s `from src.tribblefis...` import. Only matters if CI ever
  invokes it that way.

author: mikepantz
body:
## Summary

Two fixes from Mike's second PIE session (overboard#162).

### 1. Mesh scale bug — the real fix, not the wheel-cylinder assumption

**Root cause, exact:** `MeshAssemblyRoot` was attached under `BoxMesh` (`RootComponent = BoxMesh`),
and `BoxMesh` carries its own `SetRelativeScale3D(0.7, 0.25, 0.08)` to shape a 1m cube into a
board-ish placeholder. Child components inherit parent scale by default, so the real mesh —
already correctly converted mm→cm — got that placeholder-shaping scale applied **on top**. Hiding
the box (`SetVisibility(false)`) hides its visibility, not its transform, and the transform is
what propagates to children. The COO's arithmetic against the diagnostic log nailed it exactly:
wheel measured `(10.18, 0.60, 3.64)` cm = expected `(14.54, 7.5, 14.54)` cm × box scale
`(0.7, 0.25, 0.08)`, exact on all three axes.

**Fix:** `SceneRoot`, a new identity-scale `USceneComponent`, is now the actor's true root.
`BoxMesh` and `MeshAssemblyRoot` attach to it as **siblings**, not parent/child — the
placeholder's cosmetic scale can no longer reach anything else in the hierarchy, structurally,
not just by convention.

**Verification is now arithmetic, per the ask, not eyeballed:** `BuildPartFromStl` accumulates
every processed vertex into a local-space `FBox`; `TryBuildRealMesh` logs the union across all 7
STL parts (not the wheel) as a half-extent and full size, checked against the real measured STL
dimensions (938 × 232 × 83mm → `(46.9, 11.6, 4.2)`cm half-extent / `(93.8, 23.2, 8.3)`cm full,
2cm tolerance) and prints `MATCH` or `MISMATCH` explicitly. Computed in the actor's local space,
independent of world position, so it's meaningful before any wire state has arrived.

This also **explains, doesn't separately fix**, the reported turn-direction complaint: a 6cm-wide,
7mm-tall sliver has no visible heading, so a correct carve reads as sideways drift. Turn heading
and path direction were independently verified (by the COO) to already converge correctly in the
underlying data — nothing about steering/yaw handling changed in this commit.

### 2. Ground shadow acne — second attempt

`SetCastShadow(false)` alone (first session) did not resolve it — second session still showed
heavy stipple on a clean `OB_Main`, no landscape. Going straight to the preferred hypothesis: the
ground now uses `/Engine/EngineMaterials/WorldGridMaterial` instead of the engine default.
`WorldGridMaterial` is procedural/world-position-driven, not UV-sampled, so the
100×-stretched-unit-plane's UV concern can't be a factor in what it renders — sidesteps the
problem rather than working around it. Also `SetReceivesDecals(false)` (cheap). `SetCastShadow(false)`
stays (still correct, just evidently not sufficient alone). Deliberately did **not** touch
`r.Lumen.DiffuseIndirect.Allow` or any project-wide VSM/Lumen setting — that hypothesis is for
Mike to test interactively via the in-editor console, not something to bake into project config,
which would be a global quality downgrade for a local artifact.

## Verified running
- `Build.sh OverboardGameEditor Mac Development` succeeds.
- `mesh/` and `wire/` standalone tests unaffected, still passing (3/3, 10/10).
- Hand-verified the new expected bounds constants `(46.9, 11.6, 4.2)` against the raw per-part
  STL bounds already captured in `mesh/tests/test_stl_loader.cpp`'s output — arithmetic matches
  independently of the in-game log.
- CI green: https://github.com/MikePaNtZ/overboard-game/actions/runs/30724704763

## NOT verified
Any of this on screen. No display in this environment, same constraint as every prior pass — the
whole point of the arithmetic bounds check is to give Mike a log line to read instead of judging
scale by eye.

Refs #162.

author: blysspeak
body:
Found while explaining the access-control model: `apply_push` took the authenticated token's project as a parameter but never actually validated pushed nodes/edges against it — a valid collaborator credential for project A could push data tagged as belonging to a different project B on the same server.

Now a node/edge is only accepted if it's linked to the token's project (existing `belongs_to` edge, or one in the same push batch — the normal client behavior — or is the project's own bootstrap node). Everything else is rejected (422), nothing partially written.

3 new tests for the rejection paths + bootstrap; all 9 pre-existing merge tests updated to seed real project membership (they'd been pushing unlinked nodes, which is exactly the gap this closes).

author: me-frankan
body:
## Summary

- `StageBinary` executes the freshly-staged binary to verify its version, then immediately renames its parent directory into place. Safe on Unix by construction; racy on Windows (image-lock release timing + AV on-close scanning can hold a transient lock on a just-executed `.exe`) — this is what stranded 群管理/MAOZH2's rescue attempt with `Access is denied`.
- Adds `renamePublishWithRetry`: exponential backoff (100ms→1.6s, ~3.1s total across 5 retries) around just the `os.Rename` call. Deliberately sub-4-second ceiling, distinct from `UpdateIntentStore`'s minutes-scale backoff (#1771) — this layer absorbs a transient OS/AV lock within a single already-running attempt; the outer layer redelivers the trigger to an unreachable target. They don't overlap.
- Adds a path-filtered `windows-latest` CI job (`server/internal/cli/version_store*.go` and related files only) so this package finally runs under real Windows semantics — CI has been `ubuntu-latest` only until now.

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-daemon-update-mechanism-design.md` (branch `nash/daemon-update-mechanism-design`).

## Test plan

- [x] 4 new unit tests on `renamePublishWithRetry`: immediate success (no retry cost), retry-then-succeed, exhausts and returns the real error at the ~3.1s ceiling, respects context cancellation
- [x] 1 integration test proving `StageBinary` itself survives a transient rename failure (not just the isolated retry function)
- [x] Mutation-verified: reverted the retry wiring, confirmed the integration test reproduces the exact `Access is denied` error from the incident, restored it green
- [x] `go build ./...` / `go vet ./internal/cli/...` clean, full `go test ./internal/cli/...` (`-count=1`) green
- [ ] New `windows-latest` CI job — needs to run once on this PR to confirm it actually exercises real Windows lock semantics (not guaranteed on a hosted runner without Defender/AV parity — will report honestly either way)

author: h4x0r
body:
## Summary

Fixes **RUSTSEC-2026-0002** (`lru` `IterMut` violates Stacked Borrows) by widening the caret `0.12` -> `0.18.1`, and fixes the `deny.toml` config that made the advisory invisible to CI in the first place.

Zero source changes — clean build, 483 tests pass.

## The advisory

`lru`'s `IterMut::next`/`next_back` temporarily create an exclusive reference to the key when dereferencing the internal node pointer, invalidating the shared pointer the internal `HashMap` still holds. `informational = "unsound"`, `patched = [">= 0.16.3"]`.

**Reachability, stated honestly:** `ewf-core` calls only `LruCache::{new, get, put, iter}` — never `iter_mut()` — so the unsound path is not reachable from this crate as written. The bump is still right: nothing structurally stops a future caller from reaching for `iter_mut`, and the affected version should not be in the graph.

The requirement is `0.18.1`, not `0.16`, because a bare `0.16` caret can still resolve 0.16.0-0.16.2, which are **affected**.

Both fuzz workspaces carry their own lockfiles and were independently pinned to `lru 0.12.5`, so the fuzzers were exercising the unsound version. Both are updated.

## The gate could not have caught this

The advisory was already in `deny.toml`'s ignore list — but it was never even *evaluated*.

cargo-deny 0.19.0 defaults `unsound` to `"workspace"`, then builds the workspace-member set that scope compares against **only** when the unrelated `unmaintained` scope is `"workspace"`/`"transitive"` (`src/advisories.rs:77-93`). With `unmaintained` at its own `"all"` default, that set is empty, the membership test at line 120 is always false, and every `informational = "unsound"` advisory hits `continue` unreported.

Setting `unsound = "all"` takes the unconditional branch at line 111 — it does not consult that set at all, so it stays correct if upstream fixes the gating. (Setting `unmaintained = "workspace"` also works, but only as a side effect of populating the set, and would regress the day the bug is fixed.)

Verified empirically against cargo-deny 0.19.0, with the ignore list emptied:

| `unsound` | `unmaintained` | RUSTSEC-2026-0002 reported? |
|---|---|---|
| *(default)* | *unset* | no |
| *(default)* | `all` | no |
| *(default)* | `none` | no |
| *(default)* | `workspace` | **yes** |
| *(default)* | `transitive` | **yes** |
| `all` | *unset* | **yes** |
| `workspace` | *unset* | no |
| `transitive` | *unset* | **yes** |
| `none` | *unset* | no |

## Proof the gate now fires

**Before** (caret reverted to `lru = "0.12"`, `unsound = "all"` in place):

```
error[unsound]: `IterMut` violates Stacked Borrows by invalidating internal pointer
    ┌─ Cargo.lock:75:1
    │
 75 │ lru 0.12.5 registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index
    │ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ unsound advisory detected
    │
    ├ ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0002
    ├ Solution: Upgrade to >=0.16.3 (try `cargo update -p lru`)
    ├ lru v0.12.5
      └── ewf v0.4.7
          ├── ewf-cli v0.3.0
          └── ewf-forensic v0.7.2

advisories FAILED
```

**After:**

```
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
```

## Ignore list emptied, not re-homed

Both entries were reported by cargo-deny as `advisory-not-detected`:

- `RUSTSEC-2026-0002` — fixed by this bump.
- `RUSTSEC-2025-0056` (`adler`) — has left the dependency graph entirely.

The prior comment also **misattributed** RUSTSEC-2026-0002 to `console`, asserting it was "genuinely fixed" by an `indicatif` bump that resolved `console 0.16.4`. The advisory is against `lru`; `console` has no RustSec advisory at all, and the "phantom console 0.15 CI re-resolution artifact" it described was not the thing being suppressed.

## Downstream

`4n6mount` consumes the **published** `ewf 0.4.6`, whose `lru = "0.12"` requirement no downstream `cargo update` can cross. It carries a temporary ignore with an explicit removal condition pointing at this PR (SecurityRonin/4n6mount#11). Once this merges and release-plz publishes `ewf >= 0.4.8`, `cargo update -p ewf` there clears it.

## Verification

`cargo build --workspace --all-features` · `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (483 passed, 5 ignored) · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` · `cargo fmt --all --check` · `cargo deny check`

## Summary

- complete #34 with verified next-season configuration, publication-gated rollout, and transactional refresh cutover tooling
- handle EST1, NOR1, and SWE1 consistently as calendar-year leagues, including mixed `2026` and `2026-27` daily refresh batches
- reconcile existing EST1/NOR1 rows from legacy split-year labels to calendar labels in place during the later seed, preserving `CompetitionSeason` IDs, related ingestion data, publication state, refresh state, and Galaxy snapshots

author: jeremy-luyckfasseel
body:
## Story
Implements 2-6-identity-erasure-handler-and-tombstone.

## Changes
- **libs/go-pitwall/erasure**: closed a real outbox-atomicity gap ahead of its first production caller — `Handler.Enqueue` now runs inside the same transaction as delete+tombstone+inbox-mark, so the `privacy.erased` ack can never be lost between commit and publication. Bumped to v0.2.0.
- **Identity erasure (AC1)**: a validated `privacy.erasure_requested` deletes the `identities` row, writes a tombstone (`identity_tombstones`), and atomically enqueues `privacy.erased` to the same outbox `identity.resolved` uses.
- **Email-hash suppression (AC2, Round 33/Q33.1)**: since Identity's own slice *is* the email↔masterId mapping, the erased email's normalized form is hashed (irreversible SHA-256, never plaintext) into `email_suppressions`. A later `identity.lookup_requested` for that email is held — durably persisted (`held_lookups`), logged at alert severity, never minted, never replied — mirroring Story 2.5's unknown-token exception pattern.
- One queue now carries both `identity.lookup_requested` and `privacy.erasure_requested` (same producer exchange, `frontend.events`), per the library's own "one queue per consumer" design intent.
- Docs updated (`services/identity/README.md`, `docs/analysis/services/identity.md`); a genuine open design question (Round 33/Q33.1) was surfaced and resolved with the user before implementation, per the golden rule.

## Testing
- All four test layers green: unit (`libs/go-pitwall`, `services/identity` × 4 packages), integration (real RabbitMQ + SQLite via testcontainers, incl. 3 new erasure scenarios), contract (no `/contract` diff — no new schema), e2e conformance smoke (all 6 scenarios).
- `services/timing`/`services/leaderboard` confirmed unaffected by the shared-library bump (faithfulness check).
- Both acceptance criteria verified end-to-end, not just at the unit level.
- Adversarial code review complete (Blind Hunter, Edge Case Hunter, Acceptance Auditor): 2 patches applied (defensive email re-normalization before hashing; a test comment fix), 2 items deferred (recorded in `deferred-work.md`), 4 dismissed as noise/pre-existing.

author: ecrlib
body:
## Description

The AD provider's password change has failed on the explicit-bind path for the whole of this investigation, with `0x80070547` and **no server-side authentication event at all**. This PR started as a probe of whether any write path worked from such a host; it ends with the change working.

**The cause was the connection the write went out on.** Both `IADsUser::ChangePassword` and `IADsUser::SetPassword` try LDAP over 128-bit SSL, then Kerberos, then the `Net*` APIs over RPC — and *which one they reach is decided by the connection the `DirectoryEntry` is bound on*. PassCore bound on `LdapPort`, so on a default deployment every write started from a 389-bound entry.

### The measurement

All from the same non-domain-joined runner, against the same directory, in the same run:

| | 389-bound entry | LDAPS-bound entry |
|---|---|---|
| `SetPassword` — the reset (Probe A / A2) | `0x800706BA` RPC server unavailable | **succeeds** |
| `ChangePassword` — service-account bind (Probe C1) | `0x80070547`, as PassCore | **succeeds** |
| `ChangePassword` — user's own bind (Probe C2) | — | **succeeds** |

The DC logs the successful writes as what they are — `[LDAP Password Change,LDAP Modify] user [EXAMPLE]\[probeuser] … NT_STATUS_OK` over `:636` — an ordinary LDAP password modification, attributed to the target user, via ADSI's **first** documented method, reached because the connection allowed it.

C1 is the one that decided the shape of the fix: bound as the *service account*, the modification is still attributed to `probeuser` and still requires the old password as an argument. A service-account bind does not turn the change into a reset — the directory verifies the old password either way, so history and minimum-age policy keep applying.

### The change

`PasswordChangeProvider` binds its own `DirectoryEntry` for the target user over LDAPS and performs **both** writes through it — the ordinary change and the administrative reset. The port comes from `LdapChannelPorts.SslPortFor`, the substitution the SSL fallback already uses: `389` → `636`, any other configured value used as given. There is deliberately no second port setting to drift out of step with `LdapPort`.

Three things it does not do, each for a reason:

- **The service-account context stays on sign-and-seal.** It needs no certificate trust, so every read keeps working on directories this machine cannot validate. Moving it to LDAPS would impose that trust on every operation to fix one.
- **Certificate validation is not relaxed anywhere.** A write nobody can authenticate is not a fix.
- **A failed bind falls back** to the previous principal-based call rather than failing the change, so a deployment with no usable LDAPS is no worse off than it was. The bind is forced eagerly with a one-attribute `RefreshCache` so its failure is attributable: left lazy it would surface from `Invoke` alongside "the directory rejected this password", and falling back there would re-attempt a change the directory had already refused.

### Logging

| | |
|---|---|
| **118** (new, Information) | the write went over LDAPS — host, port, which write |
| **119** (new, Warning) | the LDAPS bind failed and the write fell back — names the **port** and carries the **reason**, since an unreachable 636 and an untrusted certificate need different fixes |
| **115** (rewritten) | the requirement is **LDAPS with a trusted certificate**, not a domain join |
| **117** (retired) | it announced that no write could succeed in this combination and that RPC/SMB reachability was the remedy. Both halves are now false. Retired, not recycled |
| **108** (reworded) | now says explicitly that password writes do *not* go through the service-account context |

### The correction, recorded rather than quietly replaced

For several rounds the recorded conclusion was that the change *requires a domain-joined host*, and that `0x800706BA` from the reset made RPC reachability a genuine prerequisite. Every measurement behind that was accurate. The inference was not — because **only a 389-bound entry had ever been measured**, and reaching an RPC error means the two methods ADSI tries first had already been ruled out *by the binding*, not that RPC was what the operation wanted.

The general form is worth keeping: a negative result at the end of a fallback chain describes the *last* option tried and says nothing about why the earlier ones were skipped.

`TESTING.md` keeps the sections in the order they were written, with the superseded conclusions marked rather than deleted. The **ruled-out evidence list is unchanged**. The `NetUserChangePassword` assessment is kept with its recommendation reversed — it is no longer worth adopting, since the premise (it was the only working write path) is gone along with the SMB/445 requirement that was its principal cost.

### Still open, unchanged by this

- The `ShouldAttempt` gap: the reset would still not fire on an infrastructure-class failure. It no longer needs to. Recorded, not closed — widening it would fire administrative resets during genuine transport problems.
- Nothing here tests a **domain-joined** host with `UseAutomaticContext: false`. That combination remains untested, in either direction, and is not described as affected or unaffected.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Testing/CI harness

## Checklist
- [x] All new code compiles under .NET 8. — the AD provider is `net8.0-windows` and cannot be built off-Windows; CI is the compile check
- [x] `dotnet test` passes locally. — 629 tests, including 6 new source audits and 5 new `AdsiPath` cases
- [x] No external network calls are made in unit tests.
- [x] Documentation (if applicable) is updated. — `README.md`, `appsettings.json`, `TESTING.md`
- [x] Debug provider is gated by `#if DEBUG` and cannot be enabled in Production. — untouched
- [ ] (Optional) Example e2e test runs against the Docker Compose test stack.

**Test 1 has not been relaxed**, and was not relaxed at any point while it was red — which is why this is a fix rather than a re-scoped expectation.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Always-on `vector_store_ids` requests 500'd when a prompt manager was registered
- Error: "prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class"

How it solves it:

- Fallback logger selection skips prompt managers that need a prompt_id when none is passed
- Sync `get_chat_completion_prompt` now no-ops on `prompt_id is None`, matching async

## Relevant issues

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-5109

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy, config with a dotprompt callback registered plus a model carrying always-on `vector_store_ids` pointing at a real OpenAI vector store (containing notes.txt: "The mitochondria capital of Freedonia is Zorblatt City, established in 1847"), calling `/v1/chat/completions` with no `prompt_id`.

Before (commit 23de7a15d9, unpatched source) - 500:

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \
    -d '{"model":"claude-study","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"what is in my study notes?"}],"max_tokens":100}'
{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../litellm/main.py", line 650, in acompletion
  ...
  File ".../litellm/integrations/prompt_management_base.py", ... get_chat_completion_prompt
    raise ValueError("prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class")
```

After (commit 249f59ca27) - 200, vector-store retrieval runs:

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \
    -d '{"model":"claude-study","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"According to my study notes, what is the mitochondria capital of Freedonia and what year was it established?"}],"max_tokens":150}'
{"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"claude-study","object":"chat.completion",
 "choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{
   "content":"According to your study notes, the mitochondria capital of Freedonia is **Zorblatt City**, and it was established in **1847**...",
   "role":"assistant",
   "provider_specific_fields":{"search_results":[{"object":"vector_store.search_results.page",
     "data":[{"file_id":"file-...","filename":"notes.txt","score":0.997,
       "content":[{"type":"text","text":"My study notes: The mitochondria capital of Freedonia is Zorblatt City, established in 1847."}]}]}]}}}],
 "usage":{"completion_tokens":90,"prompt_tokens":61,"total_tokens":151}}
```

The `search_results` block confirms the request went through vector-store retrieval instead of being hijacked by the prompt manager.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

`should_run_prompt_management_hooks` correctly returns True for vector-store requests even without a `prompt_id`, but two spots downstream assumed a `prompt_id` was always present once hooks ran.

`get_custom_logger_for_prompt_management` fell back to the first registered `CustomPromptManagement` callback (e.g. DotpromptManager) regardless of `prompt_id`. It now skips any prompt manager whose `should_run_prompt_management(prompt_id=None, ...)` is False, so vector-store requests fall through to the `VectorStorePreCallHook` instead.

`PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt` (sync) raised `ValueError("prompt_id is required...")` when `prompt_id is None`; it now returns `(model, messages, non_default_params)` unchanged, matching the async counterpart.

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## What

`eval/run-case.js` (`npm run review:case`) re-runs a frozen golden case (`eval/cases/<name>/`, from 2fk.1) through the **real** review engine — the same `synthesizeProviderConfig` → `parseUnifiedDiff` → `buildPrMaterial` → `runMultiScope` seams and the same MCP collector production uses — with **no GitHub**. It is an *instrument, not a second review implementation* (the pattern `scripts/local-review.js` already proves), so a measured difference between two engine versions is attributable to the code change under test, never to a replay that drifted. It is the ground the scorer (2fk.3) and baseline (2fk.4) build on.

## How it works

- Extracts `repo.tar.gz` to a temp dir that becomes `REVIEWED_REPO_ROOT`; the diff comes from `change.diff` (the freeze comment superseded the ticket's original "git-fetch the SHA" plan — sibling repo heads are unfetchable, so the tree is bundled).
- Drives the engine on the case's **pinned** provider/model. The credential is read from the same env var the action uses (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` etc., selected by the pin).
- **Append-only**: one invocation stamps a timestamp and writes one dir per repeat:
  ```
  eval/out/<case>/<timestamp>-run<i>/{findings.json, summary.txt, usage.json, meta.json, transcripts/}
  ```
  `findings.json` is the raw merged `runMultiScope` findings *pre* anchor-partition — `{path,line,body,severity}` — exactly what the scorer matches against `expected.json`.

## Refuses loudly

- Missing credential (via `synthesizeProviderConfig`, naming the input).
- Missing/corrupt `repo.tar.gz` (a dead case must say so, not review the wrong tree).
- Model/reasoning **pin mismatch** — a replay off the pin corrupts baseline comparison.

## Design notes

- Module load stays **pure** (helpers unit-tested; no engine stack, no IO on import). All effects live in `main()`, which sets `RUNNER_TEMP` **before the first `src` require** so the engine's module-load-constant `TRANSCRIPT_DIR` resolves into this run's staging dir — then drains transcripts per-run so same-named transcripts across the N repeats never clobber (`[LAW:no-ambient-temporal-coupling]`).
- Explicit `eval/out/` `.gitignore` entry (it was only *incidentally* covered by a stray Next.js `out` rule).

## Scope / versioning

Dev-only tooling under `eval/` — **no `dist/` rebuild, no version bump** (`package.json` stays `1.38.0`). `eval/out/` is git-ignored.

## Verification

- `node --test`: **800 pass / 0 fail** (incl. 11 new pure-helper tests).
- Loud-failure paths verified live: missing case.json, missing credential, missing tree.
- **Real end-to-end** against the DeepSeek engine (`laws-4` case, `-n 2`): two append-only run dirs, 5 real findings each, real usage (~\$0.079, 611k input tokens), 4 transcripts each drained into the correct per-run dir, no clobber.

Closes copirate-eval-harness-2fk.2.

body:
Optional in-game menus to manage the recording library, hosted by **SKSE Menu Framework (SMF)** and/or **FUCK** — each auto-detected and **inert when its framework isn't installed**, so devbench can host SMF, FUCK, both, or neither (headless otherwise, as today).

> Stacked on #58 (the v2 recording format + `recordings` tool it sits on). Retarget to `main` once #58 merges; review the two menu commits here.

## What's here (2 commits)
- **SMF menu** (`f7b271e`): a "devbench" SMF section with a **Recordings** page (list every recording + format/samples/validated, per-row Replay/Validate/Delete, Replay-last) and a **Keybinds** page. Drawn via `ImGuiMCP::` in a separate PCH-free `devbench-UI` target (SMF's cimgui typedefs can't share the imgui PCH). Adds `dvb::RunTool` so the render-thread menu can invoke devbench tools.
- **FUCK menu** (`c22f651`): the twin, via `FUCK_API` (fetched from the `FUCK.dll` `RequestFUCK` export) in its own PCH-free `devbench-UI-fuck` target (FUCK_API pulls real `imgui.h`). Same recordings actions + a **rebindable `ManagedHotkey`** to toggle the menu — FUCK's edge over SMF.

## Design
- Both draw the same library over the shared `dvb::RunTool` → the `recordings`/`record` tools (render-thread-safe: only fast/async tools, no `RunAndWait`).
- Graceful detection: SMF via `IsInstalled()`, FUCK via its interface export; no hard dependency on either.
- Vendored client headers as header-only xmake packages (`skse-menu-framework-api`, `fuck-api`).

## Validation
Both build green (xmake releasedbg, prebuilt CommonLib; `devbench.dll` links both UI targets, 0 errors). **Not yet visually tested in-game** — the button *actions* are the already-live-validated `recordings`/`record` tools, so risk is confined to the ImGui draw calls; needs one in-game pass with SMF/FUCK installed to confirm rendering.

## Follow-ups (not here)
- In-menu keybind *rebinding* on the SMF side (SMF has no keybind framework; FUCK already does it).
- **VR** rendering via imgui-vr-helper (both draw flat-only now).

body: Adds first-class kind and Slack identity columns to principals, backfills and indexes them, and exposes native API fields and filters. Kind is restricted to the supported allowlist; Slack identity fields validate workspace and Enterprise Grid scopes, canonical IDs, the special USLACK user, and email formats. The kind backfill is derived solely from canonical foreign IDs, including team- and enterprise-scoped DMs, while unscoped DM IDs remain unknown. Legacy label-only clients remain supported by promoting reserved aliases into columns on write, synthesizing them in responses, translating filters, and resolving old Postgres principal_label references through columns, but identity aliases are never persisted in JSON labels. Mixed top-level and legacy-label writes are rejected with 422, legacy use emits value-free deprecation telemetry, and Rust clients remain unchanged for this compatibility release.

author: joaolucasoliv
body:
## Fila de revisão travada

A recuperação das recusas por obra arquivada só reenfileirava quando a obra não tivesse **nenhuma** outra mutação ativa. Num cliente offline isso quase nunca acontece: basta um RDO pendente na mesma obra para todas as recusas serem puladas em todo ciclo — que é exatamente o estado relatado em campo, com quinze registros parados em "revisão necessária" indefinidamente.

Só mutação sobre a própria obra decide se ela está arquivada do outro lado; a guarda passa a olhar apenas para essas. A espera pela restauração ainda na fila continua valendo, que era o motivo original da guarda.

Além disso, a fila ganhou a saída que não tinha. As recuperações automáticas cobrem as recusas que o cliente sabe reconhecer; o que elas não cobrem ficava sem ação nenhuma na tela, porque "Sincronizar agora" não toca em registro recusado. A bandeja de sincronização agora oferece o reenvio explícito do que está em revisão, preservando as mutações substituídas — essas não devem voltar, sob pena de duplicar o lançamento.

## Apagar e recuperar RDO

A coluna `cancelado_em` existe desde a base do esquema e toda leitura já a respeita — receita, PDOR, frequência, encadeamento do RDO anterior, importação e relatórios filtram `cancelado_em IS NULL`. Nada nunca a escreveu. Apagar um RDO passa a ser preencher essa marca; recuperar é limpá-la.

Apagar a linha de verdade levaria junto mão de obra, equipamentos, controle geométrico e fotos, e deixaria a memória operacional apontando para um registro inexistente. Marcado, o lançamento sai de todos os números, continua auditável e pode voltar. O estado de volta não é escolhido: sai de `enviado_em`, que o apagamento não toca.

Duas operações novas no envelope canônico — `CANCELAR_RDO` e `RESTAURAR_RDO` — com o mesmo encadeamento por `baseVersion` do ciclo de vida da obra, para que um apagamento não suba concorrendo com uma edição ainda não confirmada. Na lista, o apagado sai de vista e volta a ser alcançável pelo filtro de status, que é por onde se recupera.

Sem migração: a coluna e todos os filtros já existiam.

## Entrada mais rápida

A raiz do documento fica vazia até o bootstrap decidir o que montar, e essa decisão dependia de uma sondagem **sem prazo nenhum** contra um serviço que sobe sob demanda. Com o serviço frio, a tela ficava em branco pelo tempo que o navegador aguentasse — antes mesmo de aparecer o campo de CPF.

- A subida do servidor começa na primeira linha do bootstrap, e não no envio do CPF: o tempo de achar o campo e digitar onze dígitos passa a ser usado pelo serviço subindo em paralelo. É um GET público de prontidão, sem credencial e sem tratamento de erro — não decide nada.
- A sondagem de ativação ganhou prazo. Estourá-lo cai no mesmo ramo já usado para falha de rede: seguir para a entrada normal.
- Enquanto a sessão é consultada, a tela mostra a marca e o que está acontecendo, em vez de nada.
- No contêiner, o arranque declara heap e coletor adequados à instância pequena onde ele roda; o padrão da JVM reservava um quarto de 512 MB justamente durante a subida.

Nada disso muda quem pode entrar.

## Verificação

- `tsc --noEmit`: limpo
- `eslint`: 0 erros (1 aviso pré-existente em `FinanceInvoicesPanel.tsx:439`)
- Web: **1435 testes passando**, 7 pulados
- API: **1334 testes passando**, 53 pulados

Cobertura nova: a guarda da fila foi verificada falhando sem a correção (recupera 0 em vez de 1); o encadeamento e a idempotência do apagar/recuperar; a convergência do estado vindo do servidor; e o prazo da sondagem de ativação.

## Correção estrutural incluída

A lista de tipos de evento válidos no coordenador local só era conferida numa direção: um tipo novo na união passava despercebido até falhar em execução, dentro de uma transação já aberta. Agora a omissão é erro de compilação, com o nome do faltante.
